RC8 closed on 2026-11-19. It brings the app notes below and REST API 1.450.0 to 1.766.0 (333 versions).

<!-- truncate -->

## What's new in the app

From the in-app **What's new** for *Apiome 11-2026 RC8*.

### Features/Improvements

- **More of the list above the fold** — on **Versions** the status row now starts closed, so the versions come straight after it; each chip still names its version and date, and a click opens its detail. The **Catalog** filters fit one row: the view switch moved to the chips row, **Domain** and **Tag** appear once an item has one, and the search box makes room for them. A **Catalog item** stacks its buttons beside the score rings, so the description and pills sit on fewer lines, and on **MCP servers** the **Owner** filter joins the toolbar. Every unavailable button on Versions, Catalog, Projects, the import wizard and Export now says why when you hover it
- **Five features held back, one at a time** — RC8 is about **Catalog** and **Projects**, so **Connectors**, **Products**, **Shadow APIs**, the **Dependency graph** and the **Schema registry** leave the sidebar, the command palette and the shortcuts for now. They stay in the application and in the API and CLI, and each opens again, on its own, when it is finished.
- **More features, open to everyone** — **Teams** and ownership, **Style guides**, **Access audit** and **SDK settings** are now in the sidebar and Export studio for every workspace, with no preview setting. The Catalog also lists agents, models and components with their scorecard facts and the Backstage and Compass imports, and each project has its **Consumers** page for consumer contracts. Projects, Catalog and Published show the **Owner** column, filter and bulk action. The unfinished **Data browser** and **Migrations** tools are removed, with the Data API, migration plans and the `apiome data` and `apiome migrations` commands: working with stored records belongs to Api-DB, a separate product
- **Sign-in and identity overview** — the administration guide has a new **Sign-in and identity overview** page: all forty-one sign-in providers Apiome now supports, grouped by kind (code hosts, workforce identity, work tools, consumer, regional, payments), which market each regional provider is for, and when to use a sign-in provider, single sign-on or two-factor. It completes the expanded sign-in catalog; Kakao, Naver and Yandex are still to come.
- **Specs, API clients, diagrams and documents** — **Export to any format** in the guide now has one table for everything a version can go out as besides another format: the OpenAPI 3.1 document, a Postman or other API-client collection, the Export studio's pictures and the **Copy Mermaid** projection graph, a migration guide as Markdown or PDF, and an approved change report as a PDF. It also says what isn't available yet: PlantUML, and saving the schema canvas as an image or a PDF
- **Two-factor codes by text message** — when your administrator has connected Twilio, the **Security** card on **Profile** has a **Text message code** box: **Add phone number**, enter the code we text you, then **Send codes by text** with your password. At sign-in the code tab then reads **Text message** and texts the code to your number (shown as •••• 0123). A new number puts codes back on email until you choose text again, **Remove** deletes it, and a phone number is never a way to sign in on its own
- **Sign in with Paybin** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Paybin account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Paybin** with the client ID and client secret of an OAuth client registered with Paybin's identity provider; no issuer is needed. A Paybin sign-in joins or creates an account only when Paybin reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Gumroad** — people can now link their Gumroad account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Gumroad** with the Application ID and Application Secret of an application created under Settings → Advanced → Applications on Gumroad; no issuer is needed. Gumroad does not say whether the email address it shares is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Gumroad sign-in works only after the person has linked Gumroad
- **Sign in with Patreon** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Patreon account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Patreon** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a client created under Clients & API Keys on the Patreon developer portal; no issuer is needed. A Patreon sign-in joins or creates an account only when Patreon reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Polar** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Polar account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Polar** with the Client ID and Client Secret of an OAuth app created under Settings → Developers on Polar; no issuer is needed. A Polar sign-in joins or creates an account only when Polar reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with PayPal** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their PayPal account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → PayPal** with the Client ID and Secret of a PayPal REST API app that has **Log in with PayPal** turned on. The **Environment** is optional: leave it empty for live PayPal, or set it to `sandbox` for a sandbox app and its test accounts. A PayPal sign-in joins or creates an account only when PayPal reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Kick** — people can now link their Kick account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Kick** with the Client ID and Client Secret of an app created under Settings → Developer on Kick; no issuer is needed. Kick does not say whether the email address it shares is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Kick sign-in works only after the person has linked Kick
- **Sign in with Roblox** — people can now link their Roblox account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Roblox** with the Client ID and Client secret of an OAuth 2.0 App on the Roblox Creator Dashboard; no issuer is needed. Apiome reads no email address from Roblox, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Roblox sign-in works only after the person has linked Roblox
- **Sign in with TikTok** — people can now link their TikTok account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → TikTok** with the Client key (entered as the client ID) and Client secret of a TikTok for Developers app with Login Kit; no issuer is needed. TikTok shares no email address, so nobody can create an account with it, and a TikTok sign-in works only after the person has linked TikTok
- **Sign in with Twitch** — people can now sign in to Apiome with their Twitch account, and link Twitch beside any other provider on **Linked accounts**. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Twitch** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a Confidential application registered in the Twitch Developer Console; no issuer is needed. A Twitch sign-in joins or creates an account only when Twitch reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Spotify** — people can now link their Spotify account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Spotify** with the Client ID and Client secret of an app created in the Spotify Developer Dashboard with the Web API; no issuer is needed. Spotify does not verify the email address it shares, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Spotify sign-in works only after the person has linked Spotify
- **Sign in with Reddit** — people can now link their Reddit account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Reddit** with the client ID and secret of a web app created at reddit.com/prefs/apps; no issuer is needed. Reddit shares no email address, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Reddit sign-in works only after the person has linked Reddit
- **Sign in with X (Twitter)** — people can now link their X account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on, even when X shares no email address. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → X (Twitter)** with the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret of a Web App in the X Developer Portal; no issuer is needed. X often shares no email address and Apiome does not trust the one it shares, so nobody can create an account with it, and an X sign-in works only after the person has linked X
- **Sign in with Facebook** — people can now link their Facebook account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Facebook** with the App ID and App secret of a Meta for Developers app that has the Facebook Login use case and the `email` and `public_profile` permissions; no issuer is needed. Facebook does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Facebook sign-in works only after the person has linked Facebook
- **Sign in with Apple** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Apple Account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Apple** with a Services ID, the private key (`.p8` file) of a Sign in with Apple key, its Key ID and the Apple Developer Team ID; there is no client secret to renew, because Apiome signs a fresh one for every sign-in. An Apple sign-in is accepted only when Apple reports the email address as verified. People who choose Hide My Email share a private relay address, which never matches an existing account, so people who already have an account link Apple from **Linked accounts** first
- **Sign in with HubSpot** — people can now link their HubSpot account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → HubSpot** with the Client ID and Client secret of a public app in a HubSpot developer account that requires only the `oauth` scope; no issuer is needed. HubSpot does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and a HubSpot sign-in works only after the person has linked HubSpot
- **Sign in with Railway** — people can now link their Railway account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Railway** with the client ID and client secret of a Web OAuth app created under the Railway workspace's **Settings → Developer**; no issuer is needed. Railway does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and a Railway sign-in works only after the person has linked Railway
- **Sign in with Vercel** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Vercel account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Vercel** with the Client ID and client secret of an App in the Vercel team's settings that has the `openid`, `email` and `profile` scopes; no issuer is needed. A Vercel sign-in is accepted only when the Vercel account's email address is verified
- **Sign in with Hugging Face** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Hugging Face account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Hugging Face** with the client ID and client secret of a Hugging Face OAuth app that has the `openid`, `profile` and `email` scopes; no issuer is needed. A Hugging Face sign-in is accepted only when the Hugging Face account's email address is verified
- **Sign in with Zoom** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Zoom account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Zoom** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a Zoom General App that has the `user:read:user` scope; no issuer is needed. A Zoom sign-in is accepted only when the Zoom account's email address is verified
- **Sign in with Dropbox** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Dropbox account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Dropbox** with the App key and App secret of a Dropbox app; no issuer is needed. A Dropbox sign-in is accepted only when the Dropbox account's email address is verified
- **Sign in with Linear** — people can now link their Linear account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Linear** with the Client ID and Client secret of a Linear OAuth application; no issuer is needed. Linear does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and signing in with Linear works only after linking
- **Sign in with Figma** — people can now link their Figma account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Figma** with the Client ID and Client secret of a Figma OAuth app that has the `current_user:read` scope; no issuer is needed. Figma does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and signing in with Figma works only after linking
- **Sign in with Notion** — people can now link their Notion account on **Linked accounts** and sign in with it from then on. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Notion** with the OAuth Client ID and OAuth Client Secret of a public Notion integration; no issuer is needed. Notion does not say whether an email address is verified, so nobody can create an account with it, and signing in with Notion works only after linking
- **Sign in with Salesforce** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Salesforce account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Salesforce** with the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret of a Salesforce app. The **Issuer** is optional: leave it empty for `login.salesforce.com`, or set it to your org's My Domain or to a sandbox. A Salesforce sign-in is accepted only when Salesforce reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Discord** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Discord account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Discord** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a Discord application; no issuer is needed. A Discord sign-in is accepted only when the Discord account's email address is verified
- **Sign in with LinkedIn** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their LinkedIn account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → LinkedIn** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a LinkedIn app that has the **Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect** product; no issuer is needed. A LinkedIn sign-in joins an existing account only when LinkedIn reports the email address as verified
- **Sign in with Slack** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Slack account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Slack** with the Client ID and Client Secret of a Slack app that has the **openid**, **profile** and **email** user token scopes; no issuer is needed. A Slack sign-in joins an existing account only when Slack reports the email address as verified
- **Join by signing in** — the first time a colleague signs in through your workspace's identity provider they are added to the workspace with the provider's default role (**Viewer** unless you chose another; never **Owner**) and taken straight to it. Members keep the role they have. **Members & seats** shows **SSO ·** and the provider's name under **Joined** for people who joined this way. When every seat is in use the colleague signs in but is not added, sees **Your workspace is out of seats**, and the owners get a notification
- **Single sign-on for your workspace** — owners and admins can now connect their own SAML 2.0 or OIDC identity provider under **Workspace → Single sign-on**. Add the provider, add your email domain, publish the DNS TXT record Apiome shows and **Verify** it, then **Enable**. A domain routes sign-ins only once it is verified, and one domain belongs to one workspace. On the sign-in page, an email at a verified domain is offered **Continue with SSO** in place of the password
- **Sign in with Bitbucket** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with their Bitbucket Cloud account. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Bitbucket** with the Key and Secret of a Bitbucket OAuth consumer that has the Account **Email** and **Read** permissions; no issuer is needed. The sign-in address is the account's primary Bitbucket address, which must be confirmed
- **Sign in with Atlassian** — people can now sign in, sign up and link with the Atlassian account they use for Jira and Confluence. An administrator turns it on under **System settings → Add Provider → Atlassian** with a client ID and client secret from an Atlassian OAuth 2.0 integration; no issuer is needed. An Atlassian sign-in joins an existing account only when Atlassian reports the email address as verified
- **Maturity level gates** — a style guide with a maturity ladder can now set a required publish level: a version below it is refused at publish (force-publish with a reason gets past it, and is audited), the deploy gate gains a **maturity** signal, the API change check suite a **maturity** component, and `apiome lint gate` prints the level and can fail on it when the new `failOnMaturityLevel` CI outcome is on (off by default). A guide without a ladder never arms these gates
- **Maturity levels** — when a style guide has a maturity ladder, every version and MCP server version scored under it now reports its level (such as Bronze or Silver), the next level and what blocks it: rule findings over a level's limit, axes below their floor or never assessed, and missing review or verification evidence. Read it over the REST API; the maturity ladders docs page explains how a level is judged
- **Maturity ladders** — a style guide can now hold ordered levels such as Bronze, Silver and Gold, each adding rule severities, axis grades and required evidence to the one below it; a level that relaxes a lower one is refused. Ladders are saved over the REST API and recorded in the guide's history, and a new docs page explains them and the built-in guide's default ladder
- **Plan and product lifecycle** — set a plan's **State** to **Deprecated** to stop new subscriptions, with a **Retire on** date, a **Replacement plan** and a message for subscribers (told once). **Migrate to plan…** previews and moves the plan's subscriptions to the replacement without new keys, and **Retired** becomes available on the retirement date. Deprecated products and plans now appear on the **Sunset timeline** and on the changelog of each API a portal product includes
- **API products in Browse** — a product with **Portal** visibility gets its own page in Browse (`/tenant/<org>/products/<product>`): what it includes, linked to each API's version page, and a card per plan with its authentication, limits, approval, key lifetime, pricing and terms. **Sign in to request access** signs a reader in to the portal; the organization's page lists its products under **Products**, and search finds them with `type:product`
- **API plans** — a product's new **Plans** section offers it in tiers such as Sandbox and Standard: **New plan** sets the auth strategy (API key, OAuth2 client credentials, mutual TLS or none), limits per second, minute, hour, day or month, manual or automatic approval, the gateway environments it is provisioned to and its terms. A plan Apiome cannot provision yet is saved as **Declared only** with a notice, members whose security schemes do not fit the auth strategy are flagged, and OpenAPI exports carry the plans as `x-apiome-plans`
- **API products** — Ship's new **Products** page bundles the projects (at latest or at a version such as `2.x`), MCP servers and catalog items a consumer gets access to under one name, with a state, a visibility and an owner team: **New product**, then **Add member** in the editor. A project at latest follows every new publish, **Portal** visibility needs every member published, and the dependency graph's blast radius lists the products a change reaches
- **Stored overlays** — a version's new **Overlays** tab keeps an ordered chain of OpenAPI Overlay files that apply when the version is exported or published, without changing the version itself: **Add overlay**, **Remove**, and **Preview** every value the chain changes (and any overlay that no longer matches). Export Studio's **Overlays** step lists them with an **Apply stored overlays** switch and saves an uploaded file to the chain; **Agent access → Save as overlay** copies a toolset's accepted descriptions into a draft version's chain
- **A changelog page for every published API** — Browse's new **Changelog** page (next to a project's **Version history**) lists every published version's classified changes, breaking first, with **Severity**, **Path group** and **Since version** filters kept in the URL, a permalink and **View in compare** link on each change, and a Markdown copy at `changelog.md`
- **Search changelogs in Browse** — the catalog search now returns each classified changelog entry as a **Change** result with its severity pill; filter with `severity:breaking` (or `warning`, `info`) or the rail's **Severity** checkboxes, and click a result to open the version's **Changes** tab — e.g. `severity:breaking status after:2026`
- **Publication change reports** — a new docs page explains the report each publish writes: what it covers (schemas, properties, references, relationships, documentation), how the baseline is chosen (`auto`, `initial`, `manual`), editing and regenerating it, the Mustache templates and their order (regenerate, project, tenant, system), and the review and PDF export
- **Breaking changes across formats** — a new docs page explains how Avro, JSON Schema, Protobuf and AsyncAPI changes are graded **Safe**, **Dangerous** or **Breaking** under a registry-style compatibility mode or a Buf category, where the grades show (Versions, `apiome diff`, the CI gate, the publish guardrail), and how the grades are checked against the reference tools
- **Find your way around** — a new docs page maps the sidebar and the launcher: which group holds each page, why **Workspace** starts folded, the footer's **Notifications** count, and where **Tenants**, **SDK settings**, **Data browser** and **Migrations** live now
- Readers can sign in to Browse: an organization's portal page has a **Sign in** chip; enter your email, open the link we send (it works once, for 15 minutes) and press **Continue**. You stay signed in for a week, or until you **Sign out** — no workspace seat or API key needed
- **Compare from search** — Browse search results for a version, operation or schema carry a **Compare** tick (or press `c`): tick two of one project and **Compare v1.0.0 → v2.0.0** opens the compare page at those versions. A result's version chip opens the project's other published versions, landing on the same operation or schema where it exists
- **Cards that answer the retail questions** — Browse project cards, project and version headers and **Project** search results show a facts line for the latest version: operation and schema counts, the quality **Grade**, **Mock** and **SDK** when you can try or download it, the format and when it was published. Sort the home page's project rail by **Most operations** or **Best grade**, and an organization's projects with the new **Sort** menu
- **Find in a version** — every Browse version page has a **Find in this version** box: type words, `"phrases"`, `method:DELETE`, `path:` or `type:schema` and the sidebar's **Contents** and the **Overview** narrow to the matches, highlighted and counted (*3 of 42*). `/` focuses it, `↵` jumps to the next match, and the query stays in the URL as `?find=` so a link opens the page already narrowed
- **Consumer feedback** — readers signed in to Browse can send feedback on a published version or one of its operations from its **Feedback** tab. It appears in the project's **Discussion** tab with a **Consumer** tag, the new **Origin** chips (**Team** / **Consumer feedback**) filter it, and your replies and **Resolve** show up for the reader in Browse
- **Design gates** — a new docs page maps the five tests that keep the quiet pass in place: honey only in brand moments, a short page header, one banner per page, no dead controls, and a first-row-of-data budget on list pages
- **Team workflows** — a new docs page maps the four ways to work on an API together: presence and soft locks on **Versions**, **Suggested changes** on a review, **draft branches and merge requests**, and **consumer feedback** from Browse in the **Discussion** tab
- **SDK compatibility** — a new **Export studio** tab shows, for each generated SDK artifact (snippets, Go client, server stubs, Terraform provider, MCP server), how many operations it covers, its runtime and dependencies, the auth schemes it can't carry and how it handles pagination, with every gap listed first and what to change; `apiome sdk compatibility` prints the same manifest
- **Usage data controls** — a project's **Consumers** page has a **Usage data** panel: **Download export** saves the daily usage rollups as CSV or JSON, **Retention** keeps hourly counters and daily rollups for less than your plan allows, and **Sources** and **Agent toolsets** set field capture and body samples in one place. Opening a sample window needs a ticked acknowledgement. In a consumer's **Bindings and traffic**, **Erase usage identity** deletes its bindings and moves its counted calls to anonymous, for deletion requests
- **Sunset readiness** — on the **Sunset timeline** and the **Published** page, a deprecated version now says who still calls it: *Still used by 2 consumers (1,240 calls, 7-day)* with their handles and a **Consumers** link, or *Anonymous traffic only — bind consumers to attribute it*. When a sunset is 30 days away or less and bound consumers still call it, the version's collaborators get a **Sunsets still in use** notification, at most once a week, and push webhooks receive `sunset.still_used`
- **SDK compatibility overview** — a new docs page puts the two halves together: the **SDK compatibility** manifest in **Export studio** says what a generated SDK leaves out before you ship it, and the opt-in beacon in the generated Go client tells you which published release your SDK users find incompatible, keyed by the same revision and operation ids
- Look and feel:
  - A facelift across the Control Panel: the navigation rail follows your theme — warm paper on the light themes, Apiome's navy on the dark ones — with a honey marker on the current page, page titles and the big numbers use a display face, cards sit on a soft shadow instead of a hairline and lift under the pointer, and a catalog item, project or table row carries its format's colour as a hexagon avatar and a rule on its edge. Content rises in when a page opens and figures count up once; **Reduce motion** in Preferences turns all of it off
  - **Versions** now opens as a **Timeline**: a spine with a node per version coloured by its state (published green, deprecated orange with its sunset flag, archived grey, beta blue, HEAD in honey), the revision message and changelog as the body, and the same actions as before on hover. A **Timeline** / **Table** switch on the toolbar keeps the table one click away and remembers your choice on this device
  - A review has a **Suggestions** tab: reviewers suggest a concrete edit to a class or property (pick it, pick the field, type the new value) and the author **Applies** or **Rejects** it in one click from a before/after diff; a suggestion whose field changed since is marked **Stale** instead of being misapplied
  - **Draft branches and merge requests** (behind the Git-like switch): **New draft branch** drafts a change off a version line without touching it, **Open merge request** asks reviewers to review the branch, and **Merge into main** merges it through a merge session once they approve — with the classified diff on **Changes** and overlapping edits on **Conflicts**
  - **Versions** shows **who else has the project open** as a row of avatars, and an element someone is editing reads **“<Name> is editing this”** with **Ask to take over** and **Take over**; a lock lapses on its own if the tab closes, so nothing stays stuck
  - **Home** — a ring beside **Published** shows the share of versions that are published and a sparkline under **Versions** draws the last twelve weeks of publishing
  - **Export** targets are compact tiles with a three-segment **fidelity meter** and the tier under each name; the **Changes** tab of a version with no classified changelog yet explains the three steps that fill it
  - **Mock scenarios** — the headers, body and match-rules fields are editor panes that name what they hold, and the advanced match rules fold away until an operation has some
  - **Versions** lists versions by version number, highest first, and the highest one reads **(latest)** beside its number; **Sorted by** still switches to created date or any other column
  - **Compare version schemas** opens its **Diff View** with **Show only changes** ticked, so only the changed lines and three lines around each show, with the rest folded; every tab's body, including the **Schema Changes** class list, now fills the dialog. The **Canvas** tab is switched off while it is fixed
  - On a project's **Changes** tab, the newest published version reads **Latest** instead of **No changes** when nothing changed since the version before it
  - **Dark** is now Apiome's own dark theme — navy-black surfaces, a honey primary button, azure links — and **Preferences** shows **Follow system**, **Light**, **Dark** and **High contrast** first, with the other five under **More themes**
  - In the sidebar, **Lint posture**'s **Preview** pill is now a small honey dot after its name — hover it to read *Preview*; screen readers announce the link as “Lint posture, preview”, and with the sidebar collapsed its tooltip reads *Lint posture · Preview*
  - **Notifications** at the foot of the sidebar shows a blue unread count (up to *99+*) and comes first, before **Help & docs**, **Preferences** and your account; with the sidebar collapsed the count is a dot on the bell and its tooltip says the number. Marking something read on the notifications page clears it from the count straight away
  - The launcher's **Recently shipped** card shows the three newest entries from **What's new**, with **All release notes** to read the rest, where the stale **On the roadmap** card used to be. **What's new** is an icon in the top bar with a honey dot until you open this build's notes, the build string moved to the footer (click it for **What's new**), and **Resources** adds **Video walkthroughs** and **Keyboard shortcuts**
  - Honey is kept for Apiome's own marks: a pinned search on **MCP servers** is now a plain chip that fills while its view is showing and goes back to an outline when you change a filter, and the **gitlike** marker on **Versions** is a small outline badge shown only when the Git-like features are switched on
- Primitives & types:
  - **Primitives & types** is back under **Build** for every member: the registry of reusable JSON Schema types, each type's page with **Test this type** and what uses it, **Import from schema**, **Namespaces & scopes**, the **Resolver** and **Settings**
  - **Deprecate** a type from its page with an optional **Sunset date**, **Message** and **Replacement type**. The type keeps working — references still resolve and bindings are unchanged — and shows a **deprecated** badge and notice until you **Restore** it
  - A namespace has a **Root status**: mark the next version **Draft** while it is still changing, then **Stable**. The **All / Stable / Draft** filter on **Namespaces & scopes** lists draft roots apart from stable ones
  - CLI: `apiome primitives import <file>` adds a JSON or YAML file of primitives in one go — `--dry-run` shows what would be added and which names already exist, `--update` overwrites those, and `--report` writes what happened to each row
- Data records:
  - CLI: `apiome data create --class <project>/<version>/<Class>` adds one record to a class of a published version, from `--from-file` (JSON or YAML), `--stdin` or `--field key=value` (`key=:<json>` for numbers, booleans and lists). The record is checked against the class's JSON Schema first, and every field that does not fit is listed (exit 7); `--dry-run` only checks
  - CLI: `apiome data list --class <project>/<version>/<Class>` shows a class's records a page at a time — `--filter key=value`, `--sort -created_at`, `--next <cursor>` for the following page or `--all`, `--columns` to pick fields and `--include-deleted` for soft-deleted ones; `--json` and `--ndjson` stream every record for scripts and ETL
  - CLI: `apiome data import <file> --class <project>/<version>/<Class>` bulk-loads records from NDJSON, a JSON array or CSV (`--mapping 'first_name,email_addr=email'` picks and renames columns; cells are typed from the class schema). Every row is checked against the schema first, then sent in parallel batches (`--batch`, `--concurrency`) with retries on 429 and 5xx and a progress bar. The first failed row stops the import (exit 7) unless `--continue-on-error`; `--report` writes each row's result and `--dry-run` only checks
- Migration plans:
  - CLI: `apiome migrations list --project <project>` lists a project's migration plans, newest first — the versions each moves data from and to, and how many classes and rules it maps. `--from <version>` and `--to <version>` (a label, revision id or version tag) narrow it to one pair; `--limit N` or `--all`, and `--json` prints the plans as one array
  - CLI: `apiome migrations counts` counts each project's migration plans — how many plans, the distinct classes they map and their rules, most plans first. `--project <project>` rolls up one project, and `--json` prints `{projects, total}`
  - CLI: `apiome migrations show <plan-id>` prints one migration plan — its project, from and to versions, dates and every mapping (`Charge.legacy_status → Charge.status  (simple · rename)`; a rule with no target reads `(removed)`). `--scope mappings` prints only the mappings, and `--json` prints the plan as the API returns it. Backed by the new `GET /v1/migration-plans/{tenant_slug}/{plan_id}`
- Members:
  - **Import CSV** on **Members** invites many people at once: choose an `email,role,display_name` file of up to 1,000 rows and **Check file** shows what each row would do — **Invite**, **Already a member**, **Invalid email**, **Unknown role**, **No account** or **No seat left** — before anything is sent. **Send N invites** then invites each row on its own, through the same check as **Invite member**, and lists any row that was refused with the reason
  - **Export CSV** downloads the roster: email, status, role, two-factor, how they joined, last sign-in and when they were added. Importing the file back changes nothing — every row reads **Already a member**
- API keys:
  - **API keys** now manages MCP keys too, in the same list as REST keys: each row shows its **Type** (**REST API** or **MCP server**), its access (scopes or tools) and status, and **All types** / **REST API** / **MCP server** above the table shows one kind or both. **Create MCP key** sits beside **Create API key**, shows the key once and revokes from the row; a **Connect a host** card has the MCP URL and bearer header with **Copy**. MCP keys are for workspace administrators
  - The **MCP server** now needs an MCP key on every request — there is no anonymous access. HTTP hosts send it as a bearer token; stdio hosts set `APIOME_MCP_API_KEY`. **MCP settings** no longer has **Allow anonymous MCP calls** or the per-tool **Anonymous** flags
  - **Regenerate** a key instead of deleting it and creating another: the ↻ on any live REST or MCP key replaces its secret and keeps its name, scopes or tools and expiry, then shows the new secret once. The old secret is refused from its next request. The manage drawer's **Per-key capabilities** has **Regenerate secret** for MCP keys too
- MCP servers:
  - **Add MCP server** opens its own dialog — **Connect → Discover → Done** — instead of the Import specification wizard with every spec source beside it. It asks for one server (URL, name, transport, auth) or a registry, then discovers and grades the server. **Postman Collection** is no longer a card in any import dialog: import a collection with **Import to catalog**
  - A server's page has a **Credentials** tab: it shows the stored credential **masked** — the scheme, `••••••••`, the encryption key version and when it was written — and lets you set or replace a **Bearer token**, a **Custom header** or an **OAuth 2.1 access token**, or **Clear credential** to reach the server anonymously again. Secrets are encrypted at rest and never shown again; the **OAuth connection** section lives on this tab
  - **Connect with OAuth** — an MCP server protected by OAuth 2.1 gets an **OAuth connection** section on its **Credentials** tab once discovery finds its authorization server. Sign in once in your browser and Apiome stores the token encrypted, sends it on discovery, the scheduled sweep and **Test** calls, and renews it before it expires. Apiome registers itself with the server, or takes a **Client ID** you registered
  - A server's page has a **Test** tab: pick one of its tools, fill the argument form built from the tool's input schema and **Run test** to call it on the live server with the stored credential. The result shows **Succeeded**, **Tool error** or **Call failed**, the latency and `isError`, and what the tool returned. A destructive or open-world tool waits for you to tick a confirmation, and a server with no stored credential says the call runs anonymously. `apiome mcp test` does the same from the CLI
  - **From a registry** keeps imported servers in sync **hourly** (it was daily), and unticking **Keep these servers in sync** now registers the connector paused, so it syncs only when you ask. Each sync records the registry's status on every server — a server the registry deletes is kept and marked **deleted** — and a name already in your catalog is never added twice
  - MCP Registry integration — a new docs page maps all of it: importing servers **From a registry**, how they stay in sync and keep their names and status, searching the registry beside your catalog, and serving your own catalog as a registry
  - MCP notifications and monitoring — a new docs page maps how Apiome keeps watching your MCP servers: signed `mcp.version.created` webhooks when a server changes, the **Uptime** badge and its history, **Analytics** and the re-discovery health check for operators
  - Search MCP servers together with the **MCP Registry**: tick **Include MCP Registry** on the browse app's MCP search (or add `include_registry=true` to the REST search) and matching registry servers are listed after your results, badged **MCP Registry** — a server already in the catalog shows once, with an **In MCP Registry** badge
  - **Uptime** — a server's page shows how reachable it has been over the last day, e.g. **Up · 99.6% · 118 ms**: Apiome checks every enabled server every five minutes with a quick handshake and the badge reads **Up**, **Degraded** (under 99%), **Down** or **Uptime unknown**; hover for the counts and the slowest response times. The history is on `GET …/endpoints/{id}/uptime`, and a public server's README badge can show it with `?metric=uptime`
  - CLI: `apiome mcp server-json export --toolset <id>` (or `--tenant-wide`) writes your agent runtime as a registry `server.json` — the runtime's URL, how to sign in (an agent key, or OAuth once it is set up) and a `digest` that changes only when a toolset's tools do. Output is byte-stable for CI, importing it back gives a catalog entry with the same tools, and your tenant's MCP registry endpoint lists the runtime to signed-in callers
- Repositories:
  - Scans skip `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage` and `__pycache__` folders at any depth, so large repositories scan faster and use less provider quota. An `ignore:` list in the repository's `.apiome/repo.yaml` skips more; a file under its `specs:` is always scanned, even inside a skipped folder
- Documentation:
  - Every docs link in the app — **Help & docs**, lint rule references, governance panels, What's new — opens **docs.apiome.dev** instead of GitHub
- Suite Access:
  - A **Suite** link now sits right under **Home** in the sidebar for a user licensed for the Apiome Suite (the same Suite Access that shows **Designer**). It opens the suite at `suite.apiome.dev` in a new tab. The Suite is a separate commercial application, not part of the open-source project; Apiome only links to it, and the link is hidden without the license
  - **Designer** and **Developer** now show in the **Build** section and on the launcher only for a user an administrator gives **Suite Access** (admin console → **Users** → ⋮ → **Grant Suite Access**). A license, including the free plan, no longer shows them
  - The **Designer** menu's **Design** group now lists **Workspace**, **Workspace · Paths** and **Code & exports** in place of **Designer** and **Paths Editor**. **Workspace** needs the Designer plan and **Workspace · Paths** the Paths plan, as the entries they replace did; **Code & exports** opens with either. Old Designer and Paths Editor links still open
  - Designer's separate **Designer** and **Paths Editor** screens are removed; the **Workspace** is where schemas and paths are edited. Links to `/ade/studio`, `/ade/studio/editor` and `/ade/studio/paths` still open — in the Workspace, with a paths link on its **Paths** lens
- Style guides:
  - A style guide's **Policy** tab has a **Component library** section: add up to five ordered **approval stages** (a name, how many approvals, and an optional reviewer role) that a shared Designer component revision must pass before it can be published, and a **Deprecation notice (days)** that sets how far ahead a component deprecation must announce its sunset. With no stages, component revisions publish as before
  - **Export** and **Import guide** — the download icon on a guide's row saves its rules (name, description, built-in rule settings and custom rules) as a `.style-guide.json` file, and **Import guide** creates a new guide from such a file or from a URL. Built-in rules the file names but this instance lacks are listed as skipped instead of failing the import
- Tools:
  - **Data browser** and **Migrations** are withdrawn from your user menu and ⌘K until they are finished; a bookmark to either opens a **Not available yet** page
- Version:
  - The version shown on the home page, in the user menu and on **Help & docs** now names its release candidate (`RC8`)
- Mocks:
  - Kafka publishing — an AsyncAPI version bound to a Kafka broker now publishes its events there: one message per channel every couple of seconds while its mock is on, and one more on demand with `POST …/__channels__/<channel>/publish`. Payloads follow the same order as REST mocks (scenario, declared example, fixture, generated), are checked against the message schema before anything is sent, and are encoded as JSON, Avro or Protobuf as the message's `schemaFormat` says. A channel whose topic can't be worked out (an address parameter with no example) is listed as unsupported by `GET …/__channels__` and never published
  - Kafka for event mocks — an AsyncAPI version's **Mock** cell on **Published** now says where its events go: *no broker bound* (WebSocket/SSE only) or *Kafka broker bound*. Bind a version to your own Kafka cluster through the REST API, with TLS and a SASL credential that is stored encrypted and never shown again, and **test** the connection (a wrong password reads `unreachable: auth`). Brokers on private addresses are refused. Locally, `docker compose --profile broker up` adds a Redpanda broker that the mock's `/health` reports as reachable
  - GraphQL mocks — a published GraphQL version with its mock on answers queries and mutations at its mock URL plus `/graphql`, which its **Mock** cell on **Published** shows and copies; open it in a browser for **GraphiQL**. Declared examples are returned where they exist and seeded data everywhere else, scenarios and chaos name a root field as `Query.user`, and depth and complexity limits answer with a GraphQL error. Subscriptions are not served yet and say so
- Contract testing:
  - Contract testing and CI gates — a new docs page maps every breaking-change gate: `apiome diff --fail-on breaking` and the GitHub Action in pull requests, the classified changelog on **Changes** and in the `version.published` webhook, the breaking-publish guardrail, and checking live deployments, consumers and the deploy gate
- Import:
  - Import and catalog any format — a new docs page maps all of multi-format import: where to import from, the guide for each format family, and what every catalog item gets (versions, compare, lint, toolchain, search by protocol, convert and export)
  - URL catalog items refresh — a catalog item imported with **URL Import** in **Import to catalog** now follows its **Document URL**: Apiome asks the URL whether the document changed on the connector cadence and adds a revision, with a change report, only when it did. Existing URL items are covered by a new **Catalog URLs** connector, and URL items you import later join it automatically
  - Refresh defaults — **Repositories** has a **Refresh defaults** tab where workspace administrators set the cadence, refresh-conflict behaviour and auto-refresh switch every new repository starts from, optionally applying them to existing repositories that follow them. On a repository's **Settings** tab, **Scan cadence** now has a **Cadence** choice and marks each refresh setting **Workspace default** or **Custom**, with **Use workspace default** to follow the default again
  - Branch refresh rules — a repository's **Settings** tab has **Branch refresh rules**: name a branch (`main`) or a pattern (`release/*`) and set whether it refreshes, how often, and the version line its refreshes land in (`2.x-2026-11-03T21:00Z`). **Tracked branches** shows how each branch refreshes and which rule decided it. From the CLI: `apiome repository branch-rules show|set|remove|clear`
  - Legacy, mainframe and middleware formats — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Legacy, mainframe and middleware formats**: which importer to use for COBOL copybooks, z/OS Connect, WADL, CORBA IDL, ASN.1, XML-RPC and ONC RPC, how each compares versions the way its wire does, linking z/OS Connect to its copybooks, and the way forward to OpenAPI, OpenRPC, gRPC or JSON Schema
  - Healthcare and finance standards — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Healthcare and finance standards**: which importer to use for FHIR, HL7 v2, ISO 20022, FIX and FIX Orchestra, ISO 8583, EDI X12, UN/EDIFACT and UBL / Peppol, how they are linted and compared between versions, and what comes after the import: FHIR live refresh, the HL7 v2 to FHIR map, FIX links and export
  - RPC and event formats — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **RPC and event formats**: which importer to use for OpenRPC, xRegistry and CloudEvents, Thrift, FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto, Connect RPC and JSON Type Definition, reading a running service, comparing versions by each format's rules, lint, converting to OpenAPI and exporting
  - Smithy — the **Import a Smithy model** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import a file, a JSON AST or a multi-file model, Smithy lint, comparing versions with `smithy diff`, converting to OpenAPI and exporting back to Smithy
  - API Blueprint — the **Import an API Blueprint** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import, what the catalog item holds, drafter's checks, lint, moving to OpenAPI and exporting back to API Blueprint
  - RAML — the **Import a RAML API** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import a file or a file set, what is resolved, lint, comparing versions, moving to OpenAPI and exporting back to RAML
  - TypeSpec — the **Import a TypeSpec API** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import a file or a project, `tspconfig.yaml`, compiler warnings, versioned services, converting to OpenAPI and exporting back to TypeSpec
  - SOAP / WSDL — the **Import a SOAP / WSDL service** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import a file, a file set or a live service, the WS-I Basic Profile checks, comparing versions, converting to OpenAPI and exporting back to WSDL and XSD
  - Avro — the **Import an Apache Avro schema** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import a file or a schema registry schema, mirror a registry, fingerprints, comparing versions, the lint pack, converting to OpenAPI, exporting back to Avro and pushing to a registry
  - OData — the **Import an OData service** guide in **Help & docs** now opens with when to use it and a table of every step: import or discover a service, the metadata checks, comparing versions, converting to OpenAPI and exporting back to OData
  - Collections and captured traffic — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Collections and captured traffic**: importing Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, Hoppscotch and Thunder Client collections, `.http` files and HAR recordings, how the API is inferred from the requests with every credential removed, and converting the result to OpenAPI
  - How importing works — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **How importing works**: every import source, the preview-then-commit flow, importing several specs from one archive with **Import all**, and where to find import history
  - OData service roots — **URL Import** in **Import to catalog** now accepts an OData service root (`https://host/odata/trippin/`): the wizard recognizes the service document it returns and imports the service's `$metadata` instead, keeping a query string such as `?sap-client=100`
  - OData functions and actions — an OData item now lists every function and action as an operation, with its parameters, return type and route: a bound one through its entity set (`/Products({key})/Shop.Discount`), an unbound one through its import (`/Search`). Each overload stays separate, a v2/v3 `FunctionImport` (SAP Gateway) is kept too, and exporting the item to OData writes them back unchanged
  - Avro types — an Avro item now reads every Avro 1.12 logical type (`timestamp-nanos`, `big-decimal`, `duration` …), also on a nullable field (`["null", {"type": "long", "logicalType": "timestamp-millis"}]`) and on a named `fixed`; a logical type written on the wrong type is ignored, as Avro requires. A union of named types (`["Cat", "Dog"]`) keeps every member, and an `.avsc` now keeps an enum's `default`, `aliases` and a field's `order`, so editing them creates a new version
  - Avro from a schema registry — **URL Import** in **Import to catalog** now accepts a Confluent schema registry URL (`…/subjects/orders-value/versions/3`, `…/subjects/orders-value/versions` for the latest, or `…/schemas/ids/21`): the wizard recognizes the registry's answer and imports the schema itself. From the CLI, `apiome import avro --registry <url>` takes `--subject`, `--schema-id`, or a `--topic` / `--record` named by `--strategy` (`topic`, `record`, `topic_record`)
  - WSDL and XSD sets — a SOAP description or an XML Schema uploaded as several files in folders now imports as one: each `schemaLocation` / `location` is found relative to the file that declares it, a WSDL 2.0 `import` / `include` is followed, and an XSD set catalogs the types of every schema it imports. **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Import an XML Schema (XSD)**
  - SOAP services — **URL Import** in **Import to catalog** now takes a SOAP service's `?wsdl` URL or a bare `.svc` / `.asmx` endpoint: the wizard reads the description from `?singleWsdl` when the service offers it (every import inlined), else from `?wsdl`, as `apiome import wsdl --discover` does
  - TypeSpec files — a single `.tsp` file is now compiled by the TypeSpec compiler and cataloged from the OpenAPI it emits, exactly like a multi-file project, so its operations, diff and lint match; a server without the compiler still reads it with the built-in reader
  - API Blueprint — every API Blueprint import now records a hash of the API its blueprint describes, taken from drafter's parse with prose and examples left out, and **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Import an API Blueprint**
  - FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto — comparing two versions now follows each format's field numbers: a renamed field keeps its identity, a reused or shifted id is breaking, and a `(deprecated)` FlatBuffers field is safe. Both formats get a lint pack, and **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Import a FlatBuffers or Cap'n Proto schema**
  - Keeping imports current — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Keep imports up to date**: how repositories, URL imports, catalog live refresh and uploaded files stay current, and how to turn refresh off
  - Postman collections — a Postman Collection v2.0/v2.1 is now read by the same engine as Insomnia, Bruno and HAR: requests that share a method and path become one operation, schemas are inferred from example bodies, folders group operations, and saved credentials are removed. The **Postman Collection** card converts through it too, so the OpenAPI it imports has schemas and lists what was left out
  - Array merge — with **Additive merge** or **Override merge** selected on the **Changes** step, **Arrays** decides what happens to a list both sides define (`enum`, `required`, `examples` …): **Replace** keeps the merge's list, **Append** adds the other side's items, **Deduplicate** does the same without repeats. **Done** says how many lists were combined
  - Override merge — the **Changes** step's **Merge strategy** also offers **Override merge**: like additive, nothing in the latest version is removed, but wherever both define the same property, operation or security scheme, the spec's definition wins. **Done** says what was merged, added, updated and kept
  - Additive merge — when an import adds a new version to an existing project, the **Changes** step's **Merge strategy** can keep everything in the latest version and add only what the spec newly defines (schemas, properties, paths, operations). Nothing is removed or overwritten, and **Done** says what was merged and kept
  - URL imports stay up to date — a project imported with **URL Import** keeps following its URL: Apiome checks it every five minutes and, when the document changed, imports it into the same project with the options you chose, as a new date/time version. An unchanged or older document is skipped, a version you edited in Apiome is never overwritten, and a URL imported with credentials is not refreshed
  - Version already taken — importing into an existing project at a **Version** it already has no longer fails: the import is added as the next free sub-version (`2.5.0b`, `2.5.0c` …). The **Changes** step says which one, and **Done** lists it
  - References that won't resolve — the **Preview** step now warns when a schema you tick references a schema the spec doesn't define, or a URL Apiome doesn't fetch, naming each one. The import still runs and keeps the reference as written
  - Property conflicts — the **Preview** step now warns when the schemas you tick use one property name with different definitions (for example `status` as two different enums), listing every definition and the schemas that use it. The import still runs: each definition becomes its own library property (`status`, `status_1`)
  - Schemas that other schemas use — on the **Preview** step, ticking a schema also ticks every schema it references (`$ref`), and a schema that a ticked schema references can't be unticked: its row says **Required by …** until you untick the schema that uses it. An import can no longer leave a reference pointing at a schema it skipped
  - Changes step — importing a spec whose slug matches an existing project now stops at **Changes** before **Import**: added, changed, removed and breaking counts against the project's latest version, a filterable list of every changed path, operation, schema and property (breaking first), and a **Side-by-side spec** tab with the latest version on the left and the incoming spec on the right. Breaking changes are a warning, never a block — **Continue to import** is always available, for a dry run too
  - Catalog dry run — **Import to catalog** has a **Dry run** button on the **Options** step: it shows the detected format, where the import would land and why, the catalog item's name and slug, its contents, quality score and fingerprint, and saves nothing. **Continue** still goes on to **Quality** and **Import**
- Catalog:
  - FHIR servers — a FHIR server's CapabilityStatement (its `/metadata`) now imports as the server's API, a service per resource with the interactions it declares, and FHIR items say whether they are R4, R5 or R6. **Live refresh** can re-read a FHIR server's `/metadata` (**Discover with → FHIR server /metadata**)
  - Re-upload — an item imported from an uploaded file now says when it **may be stale**: a banner names the file and how long ago it was uploaded (90 days by default). **Re-upload…** imports the current copy with the same import settings the first upload used, adding a version only when the file changed. The **Uploaded file** card on **Provenance** shows the age and the settings a re-upload uses
  - Search box — the Catalog's search now says what it matches, **Search name, slug, format, protocol…  ( / )**, and is wide enough to show it; the **Cards / Table** switch moves to the next line of the toolbar
  - Live refresh — a GraphQL or gRPC catalog item can be re-checked against its live endpoint (GraphQL introspection or gRPC server reflection) **Hourly**, **Daily**, **Weekly** or on demand: set it up from the **Live refresh** card on the item's **Provenance** tab (**Set up refresh…**), with an optional credential stored encrypted and never shown again. The card says whether the source is **Up to date** or has **Changed**; a check that fails shows **Last check failed** with the reason, backs off, and never changes the item. **Check now** runs one at once, an administrator can pause every check in the workspace, and the CLI has `apiome catalog refresh` and `apiome catalog refresh-policy`
  - Drift alerts — when a live refresh adds a version, the change is graded **Breaking**, **Dangerous** or **Safe**: the catalog card shows a drift badge, the item shows a banner (**See what changed** opens **What changed** on the **Versions** tab, with every change and the two versions ticked for the diff; **Dismiss** clears it), and the workspace's webhooks and the item's owner team are told. **Drift alerts** on the Catalog page chooses which grades are announced (safe drift only badges by default) and whether they go out right away or in one daily digest; `apiome catalog drift` and `apiome catalog drift-alerts` do the same from the CLI
  - Drift email — ticking **Email me about drift too** in **Drift alerts** now emails the item's owner team: each alert right away, or one email per member per daily digest listing their team's items. It needs a mail sender on the server; without one, the other alerts still go out
  - Version retention — the **Live refresh** dialog has **Keep versions** (50 by default): refresh keeps that many of the versions it adds and prunes older ones, never a tagged, breaking-drift or converted version or one you imported yourself. When **What changed** compares with a pruned version it says so and diffs against the nearest kept one; `apiome catalog refresh set --keep-versions` does the same from the CLI
  - Convert button — the conversion preview's button now says what it does: **Convert & create Project** on a first conversion, **Re-convert** when the item has been converted before (a re-convert adds a version to the same project). The item's primary **Convert to OpenAPI Project** action opens the preview
- Catalog:
  - Catalog cards — the ⋯ actions menu now sits beside the status pill in the card's header row, always visible, instead of appearing on hover on top of the **Active** pill
- Export:
  - HTTP routes in Protobuf and Connect RPC — tick **HTTP annotations** on **Options** when exporting a REST API to **Protocol Buffers (proto3)** or **Connect RPC** and each `rpc` keeps its method and route as a `google.api.http` annotation, ready for gRPC-Gateway or Connect. The fidelity report shows each route as retained, or approximated when the request message has no field for a route variable or query parameter or the operation reads a header; with the option off it is listed as dropped. **Toolchain checks** builds the annotated bundle with `buf`, for Connect RPC too
  - GraphQL Federation subgraphs — tick **Federation subgraph** on **Options** when exporting to **GraphQL SDL** and the file is Apollo Federation v2 subgraph SDL: a `@link` header importing the directives it uses and an `@key` on every entity. A type keeps its own `@key`; otherwise Apiome keys it by its primary key, its `id` field or its one `ID` field, and the fidelity report lists each key it chose as synthesized. **Toolchain checks** composes the file with `rover supergraph compose`
  - Export studio is released — **Export studio** is back in the rail's **Ship** section for everyone. It opens from a catalog item's **⋯** → **Export to another format…**, the Catalog's bulk **Export…**, the Export dialog's **Open in Export Studio**, a version's export cards and the project facts card
  - Export several at once — the docs' new **Export several at once, and on every publish** page shows which to use: several formats in one job, several items or every version, presets, or auto-export on publish
  - Batch, presets and auto-export where you export — the **Export** dialog's **Target** step has **Several targets** (formats ticked with their fidelity badges, one archive), **Apply a preset** and **Save as preset**; a version's **Export** panel adds **Export all versions…** and an **Auto-export on publish** card next to **Recent exports**
  - Export to any format — a new docs page maps all of export: where to start one (Export dialog, Export studio, Browse, CLI, MCP, API), what survives a conversion, and the guide for every part
  - Get an export out — a new docs page sums up what an export gives you: one file or a `.zip` with a manifest, streamed and kept for 24 hours, delivered to git, a webhook or a bucket, or pushed to a schema registry
  - Run exports at scale — a new docs page sums up Export studio's operations side: following and recovering jobs, the **History** tab, the **Deliver** section, presets and auto-export, and what each screen shows when something is missing
  - Clearer states in Export studio — every step now says what's happening when there's nothing to show or something didn't load: loading targets, no target for this source, choose a target, the generated file couldn't be opened (with **Try again**), nothing to test drive or draw yet. When export targets can't be reached, the studio and the Export dialog keep the list loaded earlier, say it may be out of date, and offer **Retry**. The studio also records a few anonymous usage events (no names, sources or files) — see *What Export studio records* in the docs
  - Presets from the studio — a preset now keeps every delivery profile you ticked, in order, so applying it gives back exactly the export you saved. On **Review**, **Auto-export on publish** runs the preset you just saved or applied on every publish of the project, with one tick. On the **Presets** tab, **Open in Studio** starts an export with a preset, and **Edit** ticks up to five delivery profiles
  - Deliver section — the Review step's **Deliver** section lists **Download** (the default), your delivery profiles and, for Avro, JSON Schema or Protobuf, a **Schema registry**. Each delivery shows what it left behind: the git **pull request** as a link (or the commit), the webhook receiver's HTTP status, the objects written to a bucket and its manifest; a registry push lists each subject with its version and schema id. With no profile or registry connector, it says where to add one
  - Export history — Export studio's new **History** tab lists every export in the workspace for 90 days: source and version → target, outcome, share preserved, validation and lint verdicts, the delivery gate and where the file was delivered, who ran it and when. Filter by source, target, person, outcome, delivery channel, verdicts and dates; open a run to read its stored fidelity, validation and delivery reports, and **Re-run in Studio** with the same source, version, target and options
  - Pictures of an export — on **Review** in Export studio, a switch above the file (or the file tree) offers the pictures a target has: an **Import graph** and a **Service map** for Protocol Buffers and Connect RPC (services → methods → messages, streams marked, well-known imports external), and a **Channel topology** for AsyncAPI (operations → channels → messages) and xRegistry (message groups → messages → event types). Clicking a node selects it in the entity tree; the picture you pick is kept per target for the session
  - ERD for database exports — on **Review** in Export studio, a SQL DDL export (and its DBML, Prisma, Liquibase and Flyway outputs) has an **ERD** view beside its text: every table with its columns, types, **NOT NULL** and **PK** / **FK** / **UQ** keys, a line per foreign key, and **✚** on what the export made up — generated keys, nested-object foreign keys, junction and child tables. Clicking a table or column selects it in the entity tree, and going back to the text scrolls to its line
  - Fidelity overlay — on **Review** in Export studio, the mapping graph now wears the export's fidelity report: each entity carries the glyph of its worst finding (**✕ DROP**, **≈ APPROX**, **✚ SYNTH**, **✓ OK**) and how many it has, the chips above it give the report's counts and filter by kind, hovering an entity lists its findings, and **Treemap** shows the same findings compactly by type, service or channel for large APIs
  - AsyncAPI viewer — after you generate an AsyncAPI file in Export studio, **Test drive** opens it in the **AsyncAPI viewer**, the standard AsyncAPI documentation renderer, for 3.x and 2.x files alike: operations by channel, their messages and payloads, and a sidebar to jump between them, in a sandbox that makes no network requests. A file the renderer rejects shows its errors
  - Toolchain checks — after you generate a file in Export studio, **Test drive** › **Toolchain checks** runs the format's own tools on it (`buf lint`, `buf build`, `tsp compile`, `smithy build`, `redocly lint`…): **Run** streams the tool's output into a console you can copy, a chip says **Passed**, **Failed · exit N** or **Timed out**, and each finished check is listed with the verify result. A tool this server lacks says so instead of offering **Run**
  - GraphiQL — after you generate a GraphQL schema in Export studio, **Test drive** opens it in **GraphiQL**: browse its docs, write queries with autocomplete and run them against **mock data** made up in your browser, in a sandbox that makes no network requests. A file that is not valid SDL shows a notice with the reason
  - Swagger UI and ReDoc — after you generate an OpenAPI file in Export studio, **Test drive** opens it in **Swagger UI** and **ReDoc**, each in a sandbox that makes no network requests; with the **Mock server** running, Swagger UI's **Try it out** sends requests to it. Large files open collapsed
  - Test drive — after you generate a file in Export studio, **Review** shows a **Test drive** tab for each tool that can try that format: the **Mock server** for OpenAPI, and the format's own checks (`buf lint`, `tsp compile`, `redocly lint`…) with whether each is installed on this server. A tool this server cannot run is greyed out with the reason
  - Auto-export on publish — on Export studio's **Presets** tab, **Auto-export** runs a preset on every publish of a project and delivers the new version; when the export loses too much (critical loss by default) delivery is halted and you get a **Halted auto-exports** notification, with **Release** to deliver it anyway. From the CLI: `apiome export auto add|list|update|remove|runs|release`
  - Export presets — save an export's targets, their options and a delivery profile with **Save as preset** on **Review**, apply one with **Apply a preset** on the **Target** step, and manage them on Export studio's new **Presets** tab. From the CLI: `apiome export presets create|list|show|update|delete` and `apiome export --preset NAME ARTIFACT --out PATH`
  - Export delivery — finished exports go where they are used: a git repository (pull request or commit), a pipeline's webhook (signed and retried) or an S3-compatible bucket, chosen by saved profile on Export studio's **Delivery** tab; the docs' new **Deliver an export** page compares the three channels
  - Delivery profiles — **Export studio** has a **Delivery** tab where you save a git repository, webhook or bucket destination once (**New profile**), see each profile's **Deliveries**, and edit or delete it; on **Review**, tick profiles under **Deliver when it completes** before **Generate**, or pick one and **Deliver now** after. From the CLI: `apiome export profiles list|show|create|update|delete|deliveries`, `apiome export deliver`, `apiome export deliveries`, and `--deliver PROFILE` on any `apiome export <format>`
  - FIX Orchestra overview — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** opens its FIX Orchestra section with **When to export to FIX Orchestra** and **FIX Orchestra export at a glance**, now including how the FIX tags stay stable across exports
  - FIX Orchestra card — the **Export** dialog's **FIX Orchestra** card (under **Data schema & graph**) badges every source `types-only` with its preserved share and offers the repository **Version**; from the CLI, `apiome export fix-orchestra` (also `orchestra`) exports it and prints the fidelity report
  - FIX Orchestra checks — every **FIX Orchestra** export is validated against the official FIX Orchestra 1.0 XSD and imported again before you download it; one that fails is never delivered, and the export lists each problem with its path
  - FIX Orchestra fidelity — the **FIX Orchestra** export keeps the FIX tags it assigns, so every re-export of an item gives each field the same tag; an operation whose request or response body is a message is written as a message scenario, an inline enumeration as a code set, and bounds as Orchestra's field attributes, and the fidelity report lists each of these
  - FIX Orchestra — a new **FIX Orchestra** export target writes an item's types as an Orchestra 1.0 repository: messages, components, repeating groups, fields with their FIX tags, and code sets, written to the official Orchestra XSD; an imported Orchestra repository keeps its tags, ids, scenarios, rules, actors and flows, and other sources get tags from FIX's user-defined range
  - Data-lake schemas — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** opens a **Data-lake and analytics schemas** section with **When to use which** (Arrow / Parquet, BigQuery, Spark or Iceberg) and **Data-lake schemas at a glance**
  - Data-lake cards — the **Export** dialog's **Apache Arrow / Parquet** card picks its **Output** (`arrow`, `bigquery`, `spark`) with **Parquet** and **Bundle**, and the **Apache Iceberg** card sits beside it; both badge an API `types-only`, and from the CLI `apiome export parquet`, `bigquery`, `spark` and `iceberg` export each mode
  - Data-lake fidelity — the fidelity report for **Apache Arrow / Parquet** (and its BigQuery and Spark outputs) and **Apache Iceberg** now lists every union and enumeration as approximated, with how each format writes it, instead of as kept
  - Apache Iceberg — a new **Apache Iceberg** export target writes each table as the Iceberg schema JSON a table's metadata holds, with nested structs, lists and maps and logical types; every column's field ID is assigned on the first export and kept by every re-export, so the table evolves cleanly; pyiceberg parses every schema before you download it
  - BigQuery and Spark schemas — the **Apache Arrow / Parquet** export's new **output** option writes the same tables as BigQuery table-schema JSON (`bq mk --schema`) or Spark StructType DDL (`DataType.fromDDL`), one file per table or, with **bundle**, one file for all; each is checked against the engine's rules before you download it
  - Apache Arrow / Parquet — a new **Apache Arrow / Parquet** export target writes each root record as an Arrow schema (`<table>.arrow.json`) and the Parquet message it becomes (`<table>.parquet.txt`), with nested structs, lists, maps and unions and logical types for dates, timestamps, decimals and UUIDs; pyarrow builds every schema before you download it
  - SQL DDL — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** opens its SQL section with **When to export to SQL DDL** (a script, DBML or Prisma, or Liquibase / Flyway changesets) and **SQL DDL export at a glance**
  - SQL from the CLI — `apiome export sql <item> --dialect mysql` writes a SQL script, and `apiome export dbml`, `prisma`, `liquibase` and `flyway` write the other outputs of the **SQL DDL** card; each prints the fidelity report
  - SQL fidelity — the **SQL DDL** card's fidelity report now lists a union as approximated (one JSON column, no table per variant), each field whose constraints become `CHECK` clauses as preserved, and any constraint SQL cannot hold; an item with operations starts with a critical "types only" warning
  - Liquibase and Flyway — the **SQL DDL** card's **Output** option has `liquibase` (a formatted-SQL changelog) and `flyway` (a versioned migration): the first export creates every table, and each later export of the same item writes only what changed since. **From Scratch** starts over; **Changeset Author** names your changesets
  - CloudEvents and xRegistry — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new section, **CloudEvents and xRegistry**: when to export a CloudEvents event or an xRegistry document, and when to point tools at the xRegistry API instead, and the three side by side
  - xRegistry card — the **xRegistry** card under **Events** shows a fidelity badge for each source and its **Registry Id**, **Source** and **Indent** options; it is greyed out, with the reason, for an item with neither a type nor an event. `apiome export xregistry <item>` prints the fidelity report
  - xRegistry checks — an **xRegistry** export of a REST, RPC or GraphQL item now starts its fidelity report with a critical warning (only types and events are exported) and asks you to confirm; an event item (AsyncAPI, CloudEvents, xRegistry) — to **xRegistry** or **CloudEvents** — no longer asks. Every xRegistry document is also checked against the official xRegistry schema and must import back before you can download it
  - xRegistry API — tools that read xRegistry can now point at Apiome instead of downloading a file: a read-only xRegistry of each organization's published schemas and CloudEvents message definitions, public at `/v1/browse/tenants/{tenant}/xregistry` (linked as **xRegistry** on the organization's Browse page) and for members at `/v1/xregistry/{tenant}`. See **Serve your catalog as an xRegistry** in **Help & docs**
  - xRegistry — the **Export** dialog has a new **xRegistry** card under **Events**: it writes a CNCF xRegistry document with the item's types as a JSON Schema registry and its events as CloudEvents message definitions (`type`, `source`, `datacontenttype` and the payload schema). An imported xRegistry exports back and re-imports. From the CLI: `apiome export xregistry <item> --out orders.xregistry.json`
  - Agent interfaces — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new section, **Agent interfaces: MCP, A2A and agent manifests**: when to export MCP tool definitions or an A2A Agent Card (and when Browse's `agents.json` / `llms.txt` is enough), and the three side by side
  - MCP and A2A cards — **MCP Tool Definitions** and **A2A Agent Card** under **Agents & tools** show a fidelity badge for each source (an imported A2A agent is lossless; a schema-only item is greyed out with the reason), and `apiome export mcp` / `apiome export a2a` print the fidelity report
  - MCP and A2A fidelity — exporting to **MCP Tool Definitions** or an **A2A Agent Card** now lists, with reasons, what the agent interface cannot carry: each tool's HTTP binding (now written into its description), each auth scheme, streams and events, and the server name and grouping. A descriptor or card of more than 128 tools or skills needs your confirmation before it exports
  - A2A Agent Card — the **Export** dialog has a new **A2A Agent Card** target under **Agents & tools**: an imported A2A agent exports back as its own `agent-card.json`, and a REST or RPC API is written as an agent whose skills are its operations (or its tags), with its endpoints and auth. The fidelity report lists what each skill keeps
  - EDI and e-invoicing — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new section, **EDI and e-invoicing guides**: when to export an X12 implementation guide, a UN/EDIFACT message guide or a UBL / Peppol document schema, and the three side by side
  - Schema registry pushes — **Push to a schema registry** in **Help & docs** (was *Push Avro to a schema registry*) now covers JSON Schema and Protobuf subjects too, and setting each subject's compatibility level. Pushing is done over the REST API: `POST /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/schema-registry/push`
  - Legacy REST descriptors — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new section, **Legacy REST descriptors**: when to export WADL or a Google API Discovery document (and when to prefer OpenAPI), and the two side by side
  - Healthcare exports — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new section, **Healthcare exports**: when to export FHIR, an HL7 v2 segment guide or an HL7 v2 message, and the three side by side. In **Export studio**, the **HL7 v2 segment guide** card now sits under **Healthcare** with **FHIR** and **HL7 v2**
  - UBL and Peppol e-invoices — the **XSD** card's **Profile** option has `ubl`, which writes the item's types as a UBL 2.1 document schema (UBL data types and names, `cbc:` components, a document such as `Invoice` headed by the UBL header), and `peppol`, the same as a Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 invoice or credit note with its mandatory identifiers. The download ships the official OASIS UBL 2.1 schemas it imports, so it validates on its own, and every export is checked against them.
