From the CLI: `apiome export xsd <item> --option profile=peppol --out <file>.zip`
  - UN/EDIFACT message guides — the **Export** dialog has a **UN/EDIFACT message guide** card under **Data schema & graph**: it writes the item's types as an EDIFACT message implementation guide (JSON, CSV and Markdown) — tags, simple and composite data elements, coded values, segment groups and the `UNH` / `UNT` envelope — laid out exactly like the X12 implementation guide. Type the **Message Type** (`ORDERS`, `INVOIC` …) and **Release** (`96A`, `01B` …). From the CLI: `apiome export edifact <item> --out <folder>`
  - HL7 v2 segment guides — the **Export** dialog has an **HL7 v2 segment guide** card under **Data schema & graph**: it writes the item's types as HL7 v2 message and segment definitions (JSON, CSV and Markdown) for an integration engine — Z-segments with `ST` / `NM` / `DT` / `TS` fields, optionality, repetition, segment groups, the `MSH` header and a user-defined table for each enum — laid out like the X12 and EDIFACT guides. Type the **Message Type** (`ADT^A01`, `ORU^R01` …) and **Version** (`2.5.1`, `2.8` …). From the CLI: `apiome export hl7guide <item> --out <folder>`
  - Google API Discovery — the **Export** dialog has a **Google API Discovery** card: it writes the item as a Google API Discovery document — resources, methods, path and query parameters, and schemas in Discovery's JSON Schema subset — that Google's client libraries build a client from. An imported Discovery item keeps its resource tree and method ids. From the CLI: `apiome export discovery <item> --out petstore.discovery.json`
  - WADL and Google API Discovery cards — the **Export** dialog's **WADL** card (multi-file, with a **Layout** picker: `bundle` or `single`) and **Google API Discovery** card (with **Name** and **Version**) are badged by what each source keeps: an item imported from WADL or Discovery exports back **lossless**, a REST item **lossy**. Both are under **REST & HTTP** in Export studio and on a public item's Export dialog in Browse. From the CLI: `apiome export wadl` and `apiome export discovery`
  - COBOL copybooks — the **COBOL copybook** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to a copybook and a table of every step: the card and its options, how the layout is planned, the fidelity report, PL/I include structures, the cb2xml check, the CLI and Browse
  - PL/I include structures — the **COBOL Copybook** card in the **Export** dialog has a **Mode** option: `pli` writes the same record layout as PL/I `DECLARE` structures (`<Name>.pli`: `CHAR`, `FIXED DEC`, `FIXED BIN`, numeric pictures, `REFER` tables and `UNION` overlays, each item the same bytes as in the copybook). The fidelity report lists the same entries in PL/I terms, plus what only PL/I changes, such as 88-level values written as a comment. From the CLI: `apiome export copybook <item> --option mode=pli --out <Name>.pli`
  - XSD — the **XSD** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to XSD and a table of every step: picking the card and its version, mode and profile, the fidelity report, RELAX NG and DTD output, ISO 20022 message definitions, the checks, the CLI and Browse
  - ISO 20022 message definitions — the **XSD** card in the **Export** dialog has a **Profile** option: `iso20022` writes the item's types as an ISO 20022 message schema (`pain.001.001.09.xsd`): one `urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:` namespace, a `Document` root around the business element, UpperCamelCase names and descriptions as documentation, with a `message-catalog.json` beside it. Name the message with **Message Identifier** (or **Business Area**) and **Message Type**; the fidelity report lists every convention the item could not meet, such as a missing identifier or a name ISO 20022 cannot hold. From the CLI: `apiome export xsd <item> --option profile=iso20022 --option message_identifier=pain.001.001.09 --out <file>.zip`
  - RELAX NG and DTD — the **XSD** card in the **Export** dialog has a **Mode** option: `relaxng` writes a RELAX NG grammar (`.rng`), `relaxng-compact` the same grammar in the compact syntax (`.rnc`) and `dtd` a DTD (`.dtd`). The fidelity report lists what each mode cannot carry — a DTD has no datatypes or facets — and every grammar is checked before you download it. From the CLI: `apiome export xsd <item> --option mode=dtd --out <file>.dtd`
  - Read an exported file — **Help & docs** has a new guide, **Read an exported file**: where the export viewer is (the **Export** dialog's **Export** step, the Export studio's **Review & Generate** step and the round-trip **Text diff**), its **Copy**, **Download file**, **Wrap**, **Folding** and **Find** actions, the file tree and tabs for a bundle, the problem markers from the checks, and how large files are shown
  - OpenRPC — the **OpenRPC from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to OpenRPC (describe an API as JSON-RPC 2.0 methods and notifications, or round-trip an OpenRPC item) and a table of every step: the **OpenRPC** card, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the meta-schema check before every download, and the CLI
  - API clients — **Export to an API client** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export a collection (hand an API to the people who call it, move a collection to another client, round-trip it, share it without secrets) and a table of every step: the Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, Hoppscotch and Thunder Client cards and their options, what each operation becomes, what a collection cannot carry, the checks before every download, the credentials to fill in, and the CLI
  - FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto — the **Cap'n Proto from any source** and **FlatBuffers from any source** sections of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now each open with when to export to that format (move an API or its data types to it, keep readers compatible with stable field numbers, or round-trip an item) and a table of every step: the card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the `capnp compile` or `flatc` check before every download, and the CLI
  - OMG IDL — the **OMG IDL (CORBA or DDS) from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to OMG IDL (serve a CORBA estate, define DDS topic types, or round-trip a CORBA IDL item) and a table of every step: the **CORBA IDL** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists for each profile, the omniidl or `idlc` check before every download, and the CLI
  - ASN.1 — the **ASN.1 from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to ASN.1 (hand data types to a telecom, LDAP, PKI or aviation tool chain with their rules as subtype constraints, or round-trip an ASN.1 item) and a table of every step: the **ASN.1** card and its options, how the item and its constraints are written, what the fidelity report lists, the `asn1tools` check before every download, and the CLI
  - Thrift — the **Thrift from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to Thrift (move an API to Thrift, keep clients compatible with stable field ids, or round-trip a Thrift item) and a table of every step: the **Apache Thrift** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the Thrift compiler and thriftpy2 checks before every download, and the CLI
  - JSON Schema — the **JSON Schema from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to JSON Schema (share data types on their own, target an older draft, generate strict code with JTD, or round-trip a JSON Schema item) and a table of every step: the **JSON Schema** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists for the draft you pick, JTD mode, the checks before every download, and the CLI
  - Smithy — the **Smithy from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to Smithy (move an API to Smithy, or round-trip a Smithy item) and a table of every step: the **Smithy** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the `smithy validate` check before every download, and the CLI
  - Avro — **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** has a new **Apache Avro from any source** section: when to export to Avro (schemas for Kafka producers and consumers, pushed to a schema registry), how types, nullable fields and logical types are written, the Schema Registry subject of each schema, what the fidelity report lists, the check before every download, and where to find the **Apache Avro** card
  - API Blueprint — the **API Blueprint from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to API Blueprint (publish human-readable docs, or round-trip an API Blueprint item) and a table of every step: the **API Blueprint** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the drafter check before every download, and the CLI
  - RAML — the **RAML from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to RAML (supply a tool that still reads RAML, or round-trip a RAML item) and a table of every step: the **RAML** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the AMF check before every download, and the CLI
  - OData — the **OData (CSDL) from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to OData (describe an API as an OData service, or round-trip an OData item) and a table of every step: the **OData** card and its output, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the checks before every download, and the CLI
  - TypeSpec — the **TypeSpec from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to TypeSpec (move an API to TypeSpec, or round-trip a TypeSpec item) and a table of every step: the **TypeSpec** card and its options, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the compile check before every download, and the CLI
  - WSDL — the **WSDL and XSD from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to WSDL (hand a SOAP description to a SOAP toolchain, or round-trip a WSDL) and a table of every step: the **WSDL** card and its layout, how the item is written, what the fidelity report lists, the checks before every download, and the CLI
  - WSDL fidelity report — exporting a JSON-shaped item (OpenAPI, JSON Schema, GraphQL …) to **WSDL** now lists, on each type and field, what XML Schema cannot say the same way: a union written as an `xs:choice`, a nullable field written `nillable`, examples that are not written, and `multipleOf`, `uniqueItems` or an inexpressible pattern reported as dropped.   - AsyncAPI — the **AsyncAPI 3.1, 3.0 and 2.6** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to AsyncAPI (round-trip an event API, describe a REST or RPC API as messages, or serve consumers on an older version) and a table of every step: the **AsyncAPI** card under **Events**, the fidelity report, the parser check and the CLI
  - Arazzo — the **Arazzo from any source** section of **Export a spec** in **Help & docs** now opens with when to export to Arazzo (round-trip an Arazzo document, or start workflows for an API you already have), how it differs from a published version's own Arazzo document, and a table of every step: the fidelity report, the **Arazzo** card, the CLI, the export checks and the placeholder source description to replace
  - Export from the CLI — **Help & docs** lists a new guide, **Export from the CLI**: `apiome export <format>` for every export target, the fidelity report it prints, several formats or items in one archive, gating a CI job with `--force`, `--min-grade` and `--fail-on`, and the format tools that check each export
  - SQL DDL — the **Export** dialog offers **SQL DDL**: `CREATE TABLE` statements for PostgreSQL, MySQL or standard SQL, with `NOT NULL` and `CHECK` constraints and enums; nested objects as JSON columns or, with **nested** `tables`, as foreign keys and junction tables
  - SQL DDL — the same tables as **DBML** (for dbdiagram.io) or a Prisma `schema.prisma`: set **output** to `dbml` or `prisma`; both are checked by their own tools (`@dbml/core`, `prisma validate`) before the download
  - MCP tool definitions — the **Export** dialog offers **MCP Tool Definitions**: an MCP server descriptor with one tool per operation (name, description, input schema and, on 2025-06-18, output schema) that MCP hosts and **Import to catalog** read; the CLI exports it with `apiome export mcp`

  - OpenAPI 3.2 — the **OpenAPI** export's **openapi_version** offers **3.2**, badged `3.2 · newer`: `QUERY` and custom methods and the tag tree are written natively, and the 3.1 fidelity report now lists them as approximated or dropped
  - X12 implementation guide card — the **Export** dialog's **X12 implementation guide** card (types-only, multi-file) takes a **Transaction Set** and **Version**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export x12 --option transaction_set=810`
  - WSDL card — the **Export** dialog's **WSDL** card (multi-file: the WSDL and its XSD) takes a **Layout** (`bundle` or `single`), and an item imported from WSDL now badges **lossless**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export wsdl --option layout=single`
  - WSDL 2.0 — the **Export** dialog's **WSDL** card takes a **Wsdl Version**: `1.1` (the default) or `2.0`, a W3C WSDL 2.0 description (`interface`, `binding`, `service`, `endpoint`, one message-exchange pattern per operation) checked against the WSDL 2.0 schema before every download.   - TypeSpec card — the **Export** dialog's **TypeSpec** card (one `.tsp` file) offers **Include Http Imports** and **Include Comments**, and an item imported from TypeSpec badges **lossless**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export typespec --out api.tsp`
  - OData card — the **Export** dialog's **OData** card (one `.csdl.json` file by default) offers **Output** (`json`, `xml` or `both`) and **Include Comments**, and an item imported from OData now badges **lossless**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export odata --option output=xml`
  - RAML card — the **Export** dialog's **RAML** card (one `.raml` file) offers **Include Comments** and **Media Type**, badges an item imported from RAML **lossless**, and a GraphQL, RPC or data-schema item's fidelity report starts with **RAML captures REST only**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export raml --out api.raml`
  - API Blueprint card — the **Export** dialog's **API Blueprint** card (one `.apib` file, for human-readable docs) offers **Format Version**, **Include Comments** and **Media Type**, badges an item imported from API Blueprint **lossless**, and lists the constraints MSON cannot express as dropped; the CLI exports it with `apiome export apiblueprint --out api.apib`
  - Smithy card — the **Export** dialog's **Smithy** card (one `.smithy` file by default) offers **Output** (`idl`, `json-ast` or `both`), **Protocol** (`none`, `restJson1` or `rpcv2Cbor`), **Include Comments** and **Smithy Version**, and an item imported from Smithy badges **lossless**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export smithy --option protocol=restJson1`
  - XSD card — the **Export** dialog's **XSD** card (one `.xsd` per namespace) offers **Xsd Version** (`1.0` or `1.1`), **Include Xml Declaration** and **Include Comments**, badges an item imported from XSD **lossless** and any other source **types-only**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export xsd --option xsd_version=1.1`
  - Apache Thrift card — the **Export** dialog's **Apache Thrift** card (one `.thrift` file) offers **Include Comments**, badges an item imported from Thrift **lossless**, and keeps every field's id stable across exports; the CLI exports it with `apiome export thrift --out api.thrift`
  - ASN.1 card — the **Export** dialog's **ASN.1** card (one `.asn1` module) offers **Module Name**, **Oid**, **Automatic Tags** and **Include Comments**, badges an item imported from ASN.1 **lossless** and any other source **types-only**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export asn1 --option module_name=Acme-Pets`
  - OMG IDL card — the **Export** dialog's **CORBA IDL** card (one `.idl` file) offers **Profile** (`corba` or `dds`), **Module** and **Include Comments**, and an item imported from CORBA IDL now badges **lossless**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export idl --option profile=dds`
  - FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto cards — the **Export** dialog's **FlatBuffers** (`.fbs`, with **Root Type**) and **Cap'n Proto** (`.capnp`) cards offer **Include Comments**, badge an item in their own format **lossless**, and keep field ids stable across exports; the CLI exports them with `apiome export flatbuffers` and `apiome export capnp`
  - OpenRPC card — the **Export** dialog's **OpenRPC** card (one `.openrpc.json` file) badges an item imported from OpenRPC **lossless** and any other paradigm **lossy** with its preserved share; the CLI exports it with `apiome export openrpc` and prints the fidelity report
  - Arazzo card — the **Export** dialog's **Arazzo** card (one `.arazzo.yaml` workflow document) offers **Pretty Print** and **Arazzo Version**, badges an item imported from Arazzo **lossless** and any other item with operations **lossy** (it captures workflows, not the full API surface), and is greyed out for an item with nothing to sequence; the CLI exports it with `apiome export arazzo` and prints the fidelity report
  - GraphQL directives — a GraphQL schema imported as a project keeps every applied directive (`@deprecated`, `@key(fields: "id")`, your own) as `x-graphql-directive` on its classes and properties, and a union with a directive keeps its member types
  - Protobuf and Avro — a `.proto` imported as a project keeps each `oneof` (members marked `x-proto-oneof`, groups under `x-proto-oneofs`), and an `.avsc` maps its logical types (`date`, `timestamp-*`, `uuid`, `decimal`…) to the types they stand for, marked `x-avro-logical-type`
  - COBOL copybook card — the **Export** dialog's **COBOL Copybook** card badges a copybook item **lossless** and anything else **types-only**; pick it to set **Numeric Usage**, **Fixed Format** and **Include Comments**. The CLI exports it with `apiome export copybook`
  - JSON Schema card — the **Export** dialog's **JSON Schema** card now badges a JSON Schema item **lossless** (it said **types-only**); an item with operations stays **types-only**. Pick the card to set **Draft**, **Packaging** and **Mode**; the CLI exports it with `apiome export jsonschema`
  - Overlays on export — the **Export studio** has an **Overlays** step: add OpenAPI Overlay files (1.0, 1.1 or 1.2) and set their order, and the export applies them to the version's OpenAPI document before anything else runs, so a partner gets their own servers, descriptions or `x-` extensions without a fork. **Verify** and **Review** list every value an overlay changed and any action that matched nothing (`overlay.unmatched-target`); the fidelity, lint grade and export policy describe the overlaid document. The CLI takes `--overlay FILE` on `apiome export`
  - Round-trip diff — the round-trip check has two views: **Model diff** (what changed in the API, with each predicted drop marked seen or not seen) and **Text diff** (the exported file beside the same file read back and exported again, side by side). Start it from the **Fidelity** tab with **“See what a round-trip changes”**
  - Healthcare targets — **Export studio**'s **Target** step files **FHIR** and **HL7 v2** under a new **Healthcare** heading; the FHIR card picks **fhir_version** (`R4` or `R5`) and **packaging**
  - Fewer failed exports — a format that needs an HTTP operation (Kong, Gateway API, Envoy, Istio, Traefik, Apigee, AWS API Gateway, Azure APIM, Hoppscotch, Thunder Client, `.http`) or a record type (ODCS, Kafka Connect) is greyed out with the reason for a source that has none, instead of failing; GraphQL, Avro, ASN.1 and Kafka Connect exports from many more catalog formats now succeed, and say what they had to rename or approximate
  - Nothing to export from — a catalog item whose source file wasn't kept (or wasn't stored because it contained credentials) now says so in the **Export** dialog, with a **Re-import** button that opens **Import to catalog**, instead of an error. A format this deployment can't run is greyed out with the reason and is never offered and then failed
  - Every file in the .zip — exporting to a format that writes several files (an Avro or Protobuf schema set, for example) from the **Export** dialog now puts every file in **Download all files (.zip)**, with a `manifest.json` listing them; before, the .zip held only the main file. Single-file formats are unchanged
  - Safer downloads — an exported file named in any script (`注文-api.jtd.json`) now downloads under its own name instead of failing, and every file and folder in a download stays inside the folder you unpack it into, whatever names the source uses
  - Protobuf and Thrift from OpenAPI — exporting an OpenAPI project to Protobuf or Thrift now writes files that compile: `integer`, `number` and `boolean` fields become `int32`/`int64`, `double`/`float` and `bool` (the schema's `format` picks the width), and Thrift fields get their own ids instead of all being `1`
  - Stable Thrift field ids — exporting an item to Thrift again keeps every field's id, like Protobuf; a field added later gets a new id, and an id of a removed field is never reused
  - Cap'n Proto export compiles — exporting any item to Cap'n Proto now writes a `.capnp` schema that `capnp` compiles: fields, enum values and methods numbered `@0`, `@1`, … with no gaps, a file `@0x…` id, unions, maps and interfaces, and names in Cap'n Proto's style; every later export keeps the same numbers and file id, and a removed field stays as `obsolete<Name>`
  - Arazzo exports pass the official Arazzo schema before download — a document built from a non-Arazzo item gets a placeholder source description to point at your API, each schema problem is its own finding with its location, every export must import again, and an item with nothing to sequence (only types or events) is no longer offered Arazzo
  - CORBA IDL exports are checked by an IDL compiler — omniidl for the `corba` profile, Cyclone DDS idlc for `dds`; a compile error quotes the compiler's message and line
  - FHIR export checks list every issue — each validator error, or each broken structural rule when the server has no validator, is its own finding with its resource path
  - OData exports check every reference and key before download — each OASIS schema violation is its own finding, every `$Type` and `$Key` must resolve, and multi-schema OData items now export with references that resolve
  - OpenRPC exports check every reference before they are offered — each meta-schema violation is its own finding with its pointer, a `$ref` to a missing component fails, and the document must import again
  - Postman exports list every schema violation — each break of the Collection v2.1.0 schema is its own finding with its JSON path, and the collection must import again before download
  - Thrift exports are compiled and read by a second parser before download — a compile error quotes the compiler, thriftpy2 must agree with the importer on every type and field id, and the export must import again
  - XSD exports are built by a schema processor before download — every `xs:import` must be in the export, an XSD 1.0 export must build under the 1.0 and 1.1 processors, and the export must import again
  - JSON Schema exports check every reference before download — each document passes its draft's metaschema, every `$ref` into the export resolves (also between `per-type` files), and each document imports again
  - Smithy exports are validated by the Smithy CLI before download — an `ERROR` or `DANGER` event names its validator, shape, line and column, and a model that does not import again is not delivered
  - API Blueprint exports must pass drafter with no warnings — a drafter error or warning names its code, line and column, and a document that does not import again is not delivered
  - OMG IDL fidelity report — a CORBA IDL export keeps a maximum string length or list size as `string<N>` / `sequence<T, N>`, writes other constraints as comments, and its report follows the profile: under `corba` HTTP operations lose their method, path and status codes and channels are dropped; under `dds` operations are dropped and each channel is a DDS topic named in a comment
  - Thrift fidelity report — a Thrift export now writes each field's constraints as a `// constraints: …` comment, and its fidelity report names every change: nullable fields written optional, HTTP operations written as RPC methods with their method, path and status codes dropped, event operations and channels dropped, inherited fields flattened into one struct, and the field ids and names Apiome assigned
  - API-client export cards — the **Export** dialog shows **Postman**, **Insomnia** and **Bruno** cards, each with the fidelity badge for this version, and **Bruno** marked multi-file; the **Postman** card's **Flavor** writes the same collection for Insomnia or Bruno. `apiome export postman --flavor insomnia|bruno` does the same from the CLI, which unpacks a Bruno bundle into the `--out` folder. On a public version page, a multi-file export now downloads every file as a `.zip`
  - Insomnia and Bruno export — any HTTP API exports as an Insomnia v4 export (a workspace with folders, requests and a base environment) or a Bruno collection (`bruno.json` and one `.bru` file per request, delivered as a `.zip`); credentials are empty or secret variables, never values, and the export is read back by Apiome's own Insomnia or Bruno importer before download. The **Postman** target's `flavor` option writes the same files
  - RAML fidelity report — exporting a GraphQL, gRPC, event or data-schema item to RAML now warns **RAML captures REST only** at the top of the report, with the operations and channels that are not written; the report also names what reads back differently (services merged into one API, renamed types, properties numbered by position, source details on types and parameters)
  - RAML exports are validated by AMF and imported again before download — a RAML 1.0 violation names its rule, line and column, and a document that does not import again is not delivered
  - TypeSpec exports are compiled to OpenAPI before download — a compile error names its file, line and code, and an export whose compiled OpenAPI does not import is not delivered
  - WSDL exports are checked before download — the `.zip` must hold every schema the WSDL imports, pass the WS-I checks, validate against the WSDL 1.1 schema with every reference resolving, and re-import; a bundle that fails is not delivered, and one-way and rpc-style operations of imported WSDL now export correctly
  - WSDL export is valid from any source — exporting to WSDL now writes a `.wsdl` and its `.xsd` types (or one file with **layout** `single`) that XML tools and the WS-I checks accept: 64-bit integers and dates keep their XSD types, lists repeat, optional fields are `minOccurs="0"`, lengths, ranges, patterns and enums become facets, and each operation's parameters, body and error responses become its SOAP request, response and faults; renames, the target namespace and anything XSD cannot express are listed in the fidelity report
  - WADL export validates — exporting to WADL now writes a `.wadl` that passes the W3C WADL schema and a linked `.xsd` grammar (or one file with **layout** `single`): query and header parameters, status codes, error responses and media types are written, operations on `/` are kept, and operations WADL cannot carry, cookie parameters, status ranges, extra servers and gateway details are listed in the fidelity report; WADL imports now read method request parameters and an included grammar, so a WADL item round-trips unchanged
  - RAML export is valid RAML 1.0 — exporting any item to RAML now writes a `.raml` that starts with the `#%RAML 1.0` header RAML tools require: fields keep their order, 64-bit integers and dates their types, constraints become facets, unions, maps and aliases are written, and each method gets its query parameters, headers, operation name, media types and error responses; the export is checked with AMF when the server has it, and operations RAML cannot carry, cookie parameters, status ranges, extra servers, formats and renamed types are listed in the fidelity report
  - Postman export is ready to run — exporting any HTTP API to Postman now writes a Collection v2.1 that passes the published schema: requests grouped in folders by tag or service, every server as a collection variable (`{{baseUrl}}`), example request bodies and saved example responses built from the schemas, and Bearer, Basic, Digest, API key and OAuth 2 auth with empty credential variables; choose **folder_strategy**, **variable_style** and **example_depth** in the export options, and a collection imported from Postman exports back unchanged
  - API Blueprint export reads as documentation — exporting any item to API Blueprint now writes a `.apib` that starts with `FORMAT: 1A`: each action keeps its description, query parameters (in the URI), path parameters, request media type and one response per status code, and data structures keep their field order, `required` members, descriptions and defaults; the export is checked with drafter when the server has it, and validation rules MSON cannot express, operations API Blueprint cannot carry, header and cookie parameters, status ranges and renamed types are listed in the fidelity report
  - Export guides — **Help & docs** finds the **Export studio** guide again and a new **Export catalog items** guide: the **Export** dialog, the studio, bulk export from the Catalog and the CLI side by side, with each target's fidelity tier for a REST API, an RPC service, an event API and a set of types
- API Formats:
  - Adds formats:
    - Bruno collection import — a Bruno collection folder (`bruno.json` and its `.bru` files) imports as one REST API from an archive or straight from git, with the same result either way: folders as operation groups, requests as operations with inferred body schemas, `{{baseUrl}}` as a server variable and whole-variable parameters with their value as default; credentials and secret variables are never kept, and scripts and tests are listed in the coverage ledger
    - Insomnia collection import — an Insomnia v4 (JSON) or v5 (YAML) export and its environment files become one REST API: folders as operation groups, requests as operations with inferred body schemas, `{{ _.baseUrl }}` as a server variable and whole-variable parameters with their environment value as default; saved credentials, secret variables and cookie jars are never kept, and scripts, template tags, gRPC and WebSocket requests are listed in the coverage ledger
    - HAR capture import — save your browser's devtools Network log (or a proxy capture) as HAR and catalog the API it called: repeated calls become parameterized operations with request and response schemas inferred from the traffic, page assets and analytics are left out, each host becomes its own catalog item, and cookies and credentials are never kept
  - Collection source cards — **HAR (inferred)**, **Insomnia collection** and **Bruno collection** each have a card in **Import to catalog** (HAR with an activity icon), take a file or a `.zip` / `.tar.gz` archive, and import from the CLI with `apiome import har`, `apiome import insomnia` and `apiome import bruno`. A single Bruno `.bru` request is no longer mistaken for an `.http` file
  - RAML includes and libraries — a RAML API split across files imports whole: types pulled in with `!include` and the types of `uses` libraries (as `alias.Type`) join the catalog item, references that leave the upload are refused, and a missing file or invalid document says exactly what and where
  - RAML resource types and traits — a RAML API that shares shapes through `type:` and `is:` imports with them applied: each operation carries the headers, parameters, bodies and responses they add (with `<<parameters>>` filled in), bodiless responses such as `204` keep their status, the operation records which resource type and traits shaped it, and an OpenAPI export keeps every response under its own status code
  - Thrift file sets — upload a `.zip` / `.tar.gz` of a Thrift API split across files and every `include`d file joins the catalog item: `shared.Money` links to its definition, services that `extend` another record it, diffs between versions grade fields by their Thrift id (a rename that keeps the id is dangerous, a reused id breaking), and a Thrift lint pack checks namespaces, `required` fields, duplicate ids, enum numbering and `oneway` methods
  - Smithy multi-file models — upload a `.zip` / `.tar.gz` of a Smithy model split across files and the Smithy CLI assembles it into one JSON AST before cataloging: namespaces spread over files and shapes from other namespaces join one catalog item, and the item records the model's `$version`, namespaces and source files. A Smithy JSON AST (`.json`) imports on its own too
  - TypeSpec projects — upload a `.zip` / `.tar.gz` of a TypeSpec API split across `.tsp` files and the TypeSpec compiler turns it into OpenAPI, which is cataloged (with the server now shipping `@typespec/http`, `rest`, `openapi3` and `versioning`); a project that does not compile lists each error with its file and line, and archives of RAML, Smithy, Thrift and TypeSpec files now find their entry point instead of being refused
  - TypeSpec `tspconfig.yaml` — a TypeSpec project's `tspconfig.yaml` now sets the emitted OpenAPI version and options (`omit-unreachable-types`, `safeint-strategy`, …), a single `.tsp` with its config compiles as a project, every setting left out is listed on the catalog item, and `apiome import typespec ./my-api/` imports a project folder from the CLI
  - OData CSDL JSON — OData v4 metadata imports in its JSON form as well as XML, every v4 document is checked against the OASIS CSDL schema, and a document that strays from it still imports with each problem listed on the catalog item and reported by the new `odata.csdl-schema` lint rule
  - Smithy from the CLI — `apiome import smithy` takes a `.smithy` file, a JSON AST, an archive or a model folder (packed for you, build output left out), and the Smithy card accepts the same files
  - OData live discovery — `apiome import odata --discover <service root>` imports a running OData service's `$metadata` (a `$metadata` URL or SAP `sap-client` query works too), and OData now counts among the live-discovery formats
  - WSDL live fetch — `apiome import wsdl --discover <service URL>` imports a running SOAP service's WSDL (`?singleWsdl` first, so WCF services arrive fully inlined), a WSDL split across files with `wsdl:import` now imports whole, and archives of `.wsdl` / `.xsd` files find their root
  - OpenRPC live discovery — `apiome import openrpc --discover <endpoint>` imports a running JSON-RPC service's OpenRPC document through `rpc.discover`, diffs now grade parameter changes by position, name and requiredness, and a new `openrpc` lint pack checks duplicate methods and parameters and parameter order
  - OData validation — OData metadata is now checked against the OASIS CSDL XML schemas too (catching misspelled attributes the JSON form cannot see), and every name it uses is followed: an undeclared type, entity set, partner, binding or operation, or an entity type with no usable key, is listed on the catalog item and reported by the new `odata.unresolved-reference` and `odata.entity-key` lint rules (v2, v3 and v4)
  - Avro lint pack — Avro schemas (`.avsc` and IDL) are now linted as written: a default that is not a value of its type (or of a union's first branch), a nested or repeated union branch, an optional field written `[T, "null"]` or missing `"default": null`, an invalid or clashing alias, and a `doc` tools would drop are each reported by a new `avro.*` rule
  - Avro fingerprints — every Avro schema now records Avro's Parsing Canonical Form hashes (CRC-64-AVRO and SHA-256) and a semantic hash that also covers `doc`, `default`, `aliases` and `order` for each type it declares; a `doc`-only edit changes the semantic hash but not the PCF, and mints no new catalog version
  - Avro compatibility — Avro schemas are now checked the way a Confluent Schema Registry checks them: comparing two versions grades each change by whether new readers can read old data (breaking) or only old readers fail (dangerous), and the schema registry enforces `BACKWARD`, `FORWARD` and `FULL` (and their `TRANSITIVE` forms) on Avro subjects, refusing an incompatible version with Confluent's own messages
  - REST hypermedia conventions — an OpenAPI, Swagger or RAML API that declares JSON:API, HAL, HAL-FORMS, JSON-LD or Hydra media types is tagged with them: the catalog item lists each convention with its resource types, link relations or templates, a **Convention** filter appears on the Catalog to narrow the list to one, and a new `rest-conventions` lint pack checks each body against its convention (resource objects, `_links.self`, link `href`s, `_templates.default`, `@context`, Hydra members)
  - z/OS Connect binding — a z/OS Connect descriptor, the copybooks that declare its request and response structures, and the OpenAPI it targets are suggested as links to each other, and the descriptor's catalog item shows a **z/OS Connect binding** panel: each operation with its COBOL structures, the copybook items that declare them and the OpenAPI that defines it
  - WS-I lint pack — SOAP / WSDL descriptions are now checked against the WS-I Basic Profile: `encoded` messages, bindings that mix rpc and document styles, document-/rpc-literal bodies with the wrong parts, operations a receiver cannot tell apart, shared `soapAction`s, and imports that do not resolve are each reported by a new `wsi.*` lint rule
  - TypeSpec compiler warnings — a compiled TypeSpec project now runs TypeSpec's built-in linter rules, and every warning the compile reports (such as `deprecated` or `@typespec/http/op-reference-container-route`) is kept on the catalog item with its file and line and reported by the new `typespec.compiler-diagnostic` lint rule
  - RAML lint pack — RAML APIs are now checked by AMF's validation of the RAML profile on every import, each problem reported with its file and line (a self-contained document AMF rejects now imports, with its violations as errors), plus hygiene checks for undeclared `securedBy` schemes, unused base-URI and URI parameters, and methods without responses
  - API Blueprint lint pack — API Blueprint imports are now also run through drafter, the reference API Blueprint parser, and each warning (a parameter missing from the URI template, a duplicate resource, an action with no response) or error (an undefined base type) is reported with its line by a new `apiblueprint.*` lint rule
  - Smithy lint pack — Smithy models are now validated by the Smithy CLI on import with the `smithy-linters` validators switched on (`CamelCase`, `MissingPaginatedTrait`, `AbbreviationName`, `ShouldHaveUsedTimestamp`, `MissingSensitiveTrait`, …), and each event is reported with its file and line by a new `smithy.*` lint rule
  - OData breaking changes — comparing two versions of an OData service now grades each change by OData's own model-versioning rules: a new nullable property or collection navigation is safe, a new required property, a changed key or a changed property type is breaking, and every breaking change says whether the schema's `Core.SchemaVersion` was bumped
  - WSDL / XSD breaking changes — comparing two versions of a SOAP service now grades soapAction, binding-style and message-pattern changes, and XML Schema changes element by element (minOccurs / maxOccurs, nillable, defaults, enumerations, lengths, patterns and bounds), treating new optional elements as dangerous because SOAP receivers validate strictly
  - Fuller WSDL catalog items — a SOAP service's faults now appear as error messages, rpc-style messages with several parts keep every part, and each port is a server with its SOAP 1.1 / SOAP 1.2 / HTTP binding, all written back when you export to WSDL
  - TypeSpec versioned services — a TypeSpec service using `@typespec/versioning` now compiles every version: the catalog item describes the newest one, and lists each version with whether the step from the previous one was breaking or safe (and why)
  - RAML breaking changes — comparing two versions of a RAML API now grades parameter, property and enum changes individually: a new required parameter or property, a changed type or a removed enum value is breaking, a new optional one is safe
  - Smithy breaking changes — comparing two versions of a Smithy model now runs Smithy's own `smithy diff` and grades each change by its findings: `ERROR` is breaking, `DANGER` and `WARNING` are dangerous, `NOTE` is safe. Findings that belong to no single change, such as reordered members, are listed separately and still count toward the overall result, and a single `.smithy` file is now read by the Smithy CLI too, inline input and output members included
  - Arazzo source resolution — a Projects import of an Arazzo workflow validates its `sourceDescriptions` and resolves each step's `operationId` / `operationPath` against the documents supplied with the import, keeps an unresolved reference with a warning, and returns the result as `arazzoResolution` on the import job; the **Import** dialog sends only the workflow for now, so sources show as not in the import bundle
  - OpenAPI 3.2 `$self` references — a `$ref` that resolves against the document's `$self` back into the same document links to its class like a local reference, references to other documents are kept and listed in a warning, a `summary` / `description` beside a `$ref` is kept as a local override, and **Analyze** lists **Document base URI ($self)**
  - OpenAPI 3.2 tag hierarchy — tags keep their `summary`, `parent`, `kind` and `externalDocs` on the project (`x-apiome-tag-taxonomy`), classes list the tags their schema declares, a cyclic or undeclared parent imports as a top-level tag with a warning, and **Analyze** lists the taxonomy under **Feature compatibility**
  - OpenAPI 3.2 QUERY and custom methods — a path's `query` operation and its `additionalOperations` entries (such as `REPORT`) import as path operations with their request and response schemas, keep their method token, and export to `x-apiome-query-operation` / `x-apiome-additional-operations` so they survive a round-trip
  - OpenAPI 3.2 streaming responses — an `itemSchema` under JSON Lines (`application/jsonl`), JSON text sequences (`application/json-seq`) or Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) imports its element schema as a class tagged `x-apiome-stream-kind`, the operation links to it, and **Analyze** lists the streaming media types under **Feature compatibility**
  - Secret scrubbing for collections and captures — Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, HAR and `.http` imports always strip credentials, whatever your workspace's scrub policy says. Variables keep their names but not their secret values, auth becomes security-scheme stubs in the converted OpenAPI document, and the catalog item's **Provenance** tab lists every redaction in a new **Secret scrub** row

### Bug Fixes

- Mocks:
  - A property that is one of several plain types (for example `oneOf: [string, integer]`) now gets a value of the first type in a mock response, such as a string. Before, the mock filled it with an empty object, which matched none of its types
- Browse:
  - Versions created before Apiome recorded each version's format now show under the **format** and **paradigm** filters too: OpenAPI versions as `openapi` (or their exact version, such as `openapi-3.1`, when Apiome knows it) and Arazzo versions as `arazzo`, both under **REST**. Before, they matched no format or paradigm filter
- Sign-in:
  - The workspace you pick is the same on the web app and on Studio: the choice is now kept on the sign-in's shared domain rather than on the site you made it on, so switching workspace in one is switching it in the other, and signing out clears it in both
  - Studio is built from the same checkout as the web app again (`docker compose build studio` had been pointing at a Dockerfile that did not exist), and the two now sign the service token they send to the API with one shared module
  - Confirming a new account no longer flashes *We could not sign you in automatically* before the **Let's set up your first workspace** screen
  - **Sign In** stays disabled while you are being signed in, instead of turning back on and inviting a second click; it comes back only if the attempt fails
  - The sign-in page's *Watch our intro video* link, which no longer worked, is now **Explore our YouTube** and opens the Apiome YouTube channel
- Spacing and type:
  - Spacing across the Control Panel now matches the design: gaps and padding that had drifted to 24, 32 and 48 px are back to 20, 24 and 32 px, and **Compact** density in Preferences tightens spacing as well as controls. Body text follows the **Font size** preference everywhere, and pages load about 80 KB less stylesheet
  - Muted lines, small caps labels, meta lines and plain field labels now come from four shared styles instead of 21 per-screen copies, so they stay the same size and colour on every screen. Nothing looks different today
- Controls:
  - Switches such as **All types** / **REST API** / **MCP server** on **API keys** are now as tall as the buttons and fields beside them; they were 2 px shorter. Text inputs, dropdowns and text areas also come in the small and large sizes that buttons have, so a small button and a small field line up
- Dialogs and menus:
  - Every dialog, drawer and confirm now dims the whole screen behind it, Studio's top header included — the header could stay bright and clickable over an open dialog. A list, menu or tooltip opened inside a dialog, or inside a dialog opened from a drawer, now shows in full above it instead of being cut off underneath, and toasts always show above an open dialog
  - Dialogs with steps or tabs can now keep one size from the first step to the last, with their buttons fixed at the bottom and a long step scrolling inside. Studio's import, editor, settings and export dialogs use it; dialogs in the Control Panel look the same as before
  - Forms can now share one layout: sections and fields evenly spaced, three standard widths, and Save and Cancel in a footer that stays visible while the form scrolls. **Enter** in a single-line field and **⌘S** / **Ctrl+S** save the form. Forms in the Control Panel look the same as before; the design-system gallery shows it under **Forms**
  - A new split pane puts a form beside a preview, or three panes side by side, with handles you can drag or move with the arrow keys, **Home** and **End**; **Enter** collapses a side pane. Each page can remember its widths, and resizing never reloads a preview. Screens in the web app look the same as before; the design-system gallery shows it under **Split pane**
  - Steps in a progress row can now be clicked to jump to that step. Studio's class and property editors use it in **Guided** mode; steppers in the Control Panel are unchanged
- Code editors:
  - Code in Apiome's editors (the spec viewer under **Versions**, and others) is easier to read: keys, strings, numbers and line numbers now have enough contrast against the code background in every theme. Before, light-theme keys, strings and line numbers were too faint
- Contrast and touch targets:
  - The hexagon avatar of a catalog item, project or table row now draws its initials on a deeper shade of the format colour, so they are readable on every format (white on the brighter hues, such as cyan and orange, was too faint)
  - In the export studio's coverage heatmap, the level line under the count in the two hottest cells is now full-strength text instead of muted, so it stays readable on the red wash
  - On an MCP server's **Credentials** tab, a greyed-out **Save**, **Clear credential** or **Connect with OAuth** now says why when you point at it, and the error icons there and on **Test** use the readable error colour
  - The delivery-profile checkboxes in an export preset sit a little further apart, so each one is easier to hit, and the hidden **Add overlay files** input is named for screen readers
- Admin console:
  - Signing up again with the address of a deleted account no longer fails with *We could not send the confirmation email*. Deleting a user now releases their email address and linked sign-ins, signs them out everywhere, and the reason for a failed sign-up is logged
  - A disabled or deleted account can no longer sign in with its password
  - The **Users** list shows each account's **Created** date instead of *Invalid Date*, and a new **Last active** column shows its last sign-in or activity (*Never* for an unused account). Email and password sign-ins are now recorded too, not just provider sign-ins

## REST API

### 1.766.0 — 2026-11-18

#### Removed
- **Data API and migration plans — OpenAPI 1.597.0 (breaking):** these surfaces belong to Api-DB
  (`apiome/api-db`), a separate product, and are no longer served by this API.
  - `GET /v1/data/{tenant_slug}`, `GET /v1/data/{tenant_slug}/classes`,
    `GET` / `POST /v1/data/{tenant_slug}/records`,
    `GET` / `PATCH` / `DELETE /v1/data/{tenant_slug}/records/{record_id}` and
    `POST /v1/data/{tenant_slug}/records/{record_id}/restore`, with the `DataRecordCreateBody` and
    `DataRecordUpdateBody` schemas.
  - `GET` / `PUT /v1/migration-plans/{tenant_slug}`, `GET /v1/migration-plans/{tenant_slug}/counts`,
    `GET /v1/migration-plans/{tenant_slug}/projects/{project_id}` and
    `GET /v1/migration-plans/{tenant_slug}/{plan_id}`.
  - `POST /v1/versions/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/{version_id}/unpublish` no longer answers
    `409 VERSION_HAS_DATA`.
  - The record and migration-plan methods of `app.database.Database`, `app.data_routes`,
    `app.migration_plans_routes` and `embedding.embed_record_data` are deleted.
  - No migration: the `data_record`, `data_snapshot`, `migration_plans`, `migration_plan_rules` and
    `migration_rule_templates` tables are left in place. `class_schema` stays in use by
    **Freeze schema**.

    is made in `apiome-ui`.
  - No migration: `apple` has been in the provider vocabulary CHECKs since V395. No request or response
    shape changed.

### 1.737.0 — 2026-11-17

#### Added
- **Tenant linking & just-in-time provisioning (EID-1.3, #5013)** — OpenAPI 1.595.0:
  - `POST /v1/tenants/{t}/sso/providers/{id}/provision` — service-to-service (`X-Internal-Service-Token`; no session,
    no API key). apiome-ui calls it after every sign-in through a workspace's identity provider, with `{user_id}`; it
    is idempotent on `(workspace, user)` and always answers `200` with `outcome`:
    - `provisioned` — first sign-in: an `active` membership with the provider's `default_role_slug` (`viewer` when it
      is unset or the role is gone; never `owner`), `tenant_users.provisioned_by = sso:<slug>`, audited as
      `member.provisioned`, source `sso`;
    - `activated` — a pending invitation is accepted by signing in; the invited role is kept;
    - `existing` — already a member: nothing changes and the member keeps their role (never demoted);
    - `suspended` — nothing changes; reinstating stays an administrator's action;
    - `seat-cap-blocked` — every `max_users_per_tenant` seat is in use: **no membership is created**, the block is
      audited as `member.provision_blocked` (source `sso`, reason `license-seats-exhausted`) and every owner and tenant
      administrator receives a `seat_cap_blocked_sso` notification — once per blocked person per 24 hours.
    The workspace row is locked for the transaction, so two first sign-ins cannot both take the last seat; the
    membership, role, audit row and notifications commit together. `APIOME_LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED=false` lifts
    the cap here as it does for invitations (`seat_limit` is then `null`).
  - No cross-workspace provisioning: `{t}` (the workspace's id or slug) must be the provider's own workspace, else
    `404 sso-provider-not-found`. Only an account that holds the provider's `sso:<slug>` identity
    (`403 sso-identity-missing`) with an email in one of its **verified** domains (`403 sso-email-domain-mismatch`) is
    provisioned; a disabled provider provisions nobody (`409 sso-provider-disabled`); an unknown or deleted account is
    `404 sso-user-not-found`.
  - `GET /v1/access/{t}/members` rows gain `provisioned_by` (`sso:<slug>`, or `null` for an invited member) and
    `provisioned_by_label` (the provider's display name; `null` once the provider is removed). The members CSV export's
    `provenance` column now reports `sso:<slug>` for those members.
  - New notification type `seat_cap_blocked_sso` (payload: `summary`, `link`, `user_id`, `user_email`, `provider_slug`,
    `provider_name`, `seat_limit`).

#### Changed
- **Every SSO provider belongs to a workspace.** `POST /v1/admin/sso/providers` now requires `tenant_id`
  (`422 sso-tenant-required`), which must be a live workspace (`422 sso-tenant-not-found`); `PATCH` can move a provider
  to another workspace but not detach it. apiome-db **V394** enforces it with a CHECK, **disables** (and keeps) any
  provider registered earlier without a workspace, and such a provider accepts no change until it is given one. A
  provider without a workspace is never returned by `GET /v1/internal/sso/providers/resolved`.
- apiome-db **V394** also adds `tenant_users.provisioned_by` and widens `notifications_type_check`.

### 1.736.0 — 2026-11-17

#### Added
- **Per-tenant IdP registration & domain verification (EID-1.2, #5012)** — OpenAPI 1.594.0:
  - A workspace's owners and tenant admins manage their own SAML 2.0 / OIDC identity providers:
    `GET|POST /v1/tenants/{t}/sso/providers`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /v1/tenants/{t}/sso/providers/{id}`,
    `POST …/{id}/domains`, `DELETE …/{id}/domains/{domain}` and `POST …/{id}/domains/{domain}/verify`. Every route —
    reads included — needs a signed-in tenant administrator (`require_tenant_admin_session`; API keys are refused, no
    new RBAC resource). The authenticated tenant scopes every read and write: another workspace's provider is a `404`,
    and a provider created here always belongs to the caller's workspace. The request and response shapes are the admin
    surface's, minus `tenant_id`, plus `member_count` (members who signed in through the provider).
  - **Domain verification by DNS.** Adding a domain issues a challenge: publish `verification_token` as a TXT record at
    `record_name` (`_apiome-challenge.<domain>`). `verify` looks it up (`dnspython`, 5 s) and always answers `200` with
    `check.status`: `verified`, `not-found`, `mismatch` (with the values found) or `could-not-check` (timeout, SERVFAIL —
    with what the resolver said; nothing is changed and the domain is never marked verified). An already verified
    domain answers without a lookup. Three checks an hour per domain (`429 sso-verify-rate-limited`, `Retry-After`).
  - Refusals: a public mailbox domain or a subdomain of one (`422 sso-domain-public`; `APIOME_SSO_PUBLIC_DOMAINS`
    replaces the built-in list), a domain another provider has verified (`409 sso-domain-claimed`), a domain the
    provider already lists (`409 sso-domain-exists`), a default role that is `owner` or not a role of the workspace
    (`422 sso-default-role-invalid`).
  - Every change is written to the workspace's access audit, source `web`, secret-free: `sso.provider.created`,
    `sso.provider.updated` (changed field names; a domain added or removed), `sso.provider.deleted`,
    `sso.domain.verified`.
  - `SsoDomainView` (admin and tenant) gains `record_name`.

#### Changed
- apiome-db **V393**: a domain is unique installation-wide only once **verified** (partial unique index); an
  unverified domain reserves nothing, and a provider lists a domain once (`UNIQUE (provider_id, domain)`). On
  `/v1/admin/sso/providers`, adding a domain is refused `409 sso-domain-claimed` only when another provider has
  *verified* it (and `409 sso-domain-exists` when the same provider already lists it); marking a domain verified can
  now answer `409 sso-domain-claimed`.
- `dnspython` is declared as a direct dependency (it was already installed through `email-validator`).

### 1.733.0 — 2026-11-16

#### Added
- **Cumulative level gates (GVM-1.3, #5856)** — OpenAPI 1.593.0:
  - apiome-db **V392**: `style_guides.required_publish_level` and `style_guide_policy_versions.required_publish_level`
    (`TEXT NULL`, no CHECK). `PUT /v1/style-guides/{t}/{g}/policy` takes `requiredPublishLevel` (a level key of the
    guide's ladder; `null` clears, omitted leaves it; else `422 required-publish-level-unknown`) and
    `ciOutcomes.failOnMaturityLevel` (default `false`). Snapshots freeze the level into the pack
    (`StyleGuidePolicyVersionOut.requiredPublishLevel`); it enters the pack fingerprint only when set, and the
    toggle only when on, so existing packs keep their fingerprints. `PUT …/ladder` refuses a ladder without the
    required level (`422 ladder-required-level-removed`).
  - `app.maturity_gate.judge_maturity` (pure): a GVM-1.2 level result against a required level →
    `pass | fail | not_configured | unknown` with the next level's blockers;
    `app.lint_policy_service.judge_catalog_revision_maturity` is the one read behind every gate below.
  - Publish (`app.maturity_publish_gate`): runs in `enforce_publish_prechecks` after the GOV error gate and before
    the COL-2.3 approval gate; below the level → `422 {"detail": {"message", "maturityGate": {status, level,
    requiredLevel, blockers, …}}}`. `skipPublishChecks` + `forcePublishReason` gets past it. Every judged publish
    appends `version.maturity_gate` (`action` `satisfied | forced | unavailable`) to `workflow_audit`; faults degrade
    to `unavailable` and never block; a guide without a ladder or level never arms it.
  - Deploy gate: `DeployGateThresholds.maturity.minMaturityLevel` (`null` uses the guide's required level) and a
    fifth signal `maturity` (`not_configured` without a ladder or level, `unknown` when unreadable). The group enters
    the thresholds fingerprint only when set.
  - API change check suite: a sixth component `maturity` (default `advisory`), judged by the deploy gate's
    `evaluate_maturity`; `skipped` without a ladder, never `pass`. At its default it is left out of the policy
    fingerprints, so existing evaluations stay current for the publish gate.
  - Lint CI gate: `gate.maturityGate` (`counted`, `passed`); `gate.passed` folds in a `fail` only when
    `failOnMaturityLevel` is on. SARIF run properties carry `apiome.maturity`, JUnit `apiome.maturity.*`
    properties, and the Markdown summary a maturity row.

### 1.732.0 — 2026-11-16

#### Added
- **Maturity-level evaluation engine (GVM-1.2, #5855)** — OpenAPI 1.592.0:
  - `app.maturity_ladder.evaluate_ladder(findings, axes, decisions, ladder, *, evidence, now)` (pure): walks
    the levels lowest first against each level's accumulated requirements and stops at the first unmet one;
    returns `{ladderName, level, levelLabel, levelIndex, nextLevel, nextLevelLabel, blockers[{levelKey, kind:
    rule|axis|evidence, ruleId|axis|evidence, count, sample[], reason?}], waiversCounted, unassessedAxes,
    reason}`. Unassessed axes block with `reason: not_assessed`; `fixed` / `false_positive` findings never
    count; `waived` ones count unless the level's `waiversSatisfy` is on. No ladder → `level: null, reason:
    no-ladder`; no level met → `reason: below-first-level`.
  - Evidence (`app.lint_policy_service.ladder_evidence`): `review_approved` from the COL-2.3 approval gate (one
    approval when the guide sets none), `verification_passing` from the latest verification-policy evaluation;
    `null` (not assessed) for MCP versions and on a read fault.
  - `build_lint_policy_response` and the lint gate store the result as `gate_results.maturity` and in apiome-db
    **V391**'s new `lint_policy_evaluations.maturity_level` column (indexed with `evaluated_at`); packs without a
    ladder store no maturity block. `LintPolicyEvaluationOut.evaluatedAt` is now filled.
  - `record_lint_policy_evaluation` returns the stored row's id when subject, pack, evidence, axis evaluation,
    gate results and finding decisions are unchanged (previously `null`), and appends a row when any of them
    changed (previously a changed decision or axis evaluation was not recorded).
  - `GET /v1/versions/{t}/{p}/{v}/lint/level` and `GET /v1/mcp/{t}/endpoints/{e}/versions/{v}/lint/level`
    (`LintLevelResponse`, `?policyVersionId=`).

#### Changed
- Ladder levels (GVM-1.1): an omitted `waiversSatisfy` defaults to `true` on every level but the last (was
  `false`); the default template's Gold level now asks for waived findings to be fixed (GVM-1.2, #5855).

### 1.731.0 — 2026-11-16

#### Added
- **Maturity ladders frozen into policy packs (GVM-1.1, #5854)** — OpenAPI 1.591.0:
  - apiome-db **V390**: `style_guide_ladders` (one per guide: `guide_id` UNIQUE, `tenant_id`, `name`,
    `levels JSONB` with a `jsonb_typeof(levels) = 'array'` CHECK, `content_fingerprint`), a nullable

    grade, a lower score, or waivers turned back on), `ladder-unknown-rule` (not in the rule registry),
    `ladder-unknown-axis`, `ladder-axis-threshold-missing`, `ladder-duplicate-*`, `ladder-empty`,
    `ladder-invalid`.

    snapshot / content fingerprints move), and audits `style_guide.ladder_changed`; an identical ladder
    changes nothing. Revisions and packs of a guide without a ladder carry `ladder: null`, and their
    fingerprints are unchanged from before ladders existed.

    read-only `template` (not applied to tenants). `StyleGuideRevisionDetailOut` and
    `StyleGuidePolicyVersionOut` gain `ladder`.

### 1.730.0 — 2026-11-16

#### Added
- **Product and plan lifecycle (APX-1.4, #6101)** — OpenAPI 1.590.0:
  - apiome-db **V389**: `api_plans` gains `deprecated_at`, `retire_at`, `retired_at`, `deprecation_message`,
    `successor_plan_id` (→ `api_plans`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`, never itself) and `owners_notified_at`;
    `api_products` gains `deprecated_at`, `retire_at`, `retired_at` and `deprecation_message`. A `retire_at`
    needs a deprecated or retired record and a `retired_at` a retired one; messages are at most 1000 characters.
  - Lifecycle steps (`app.api_lifecycle`): `draft ⇄ published → deprecated → retired`, and `deprecated →
    published` reinstates (clearing the deprecation). `PATCH …/products/{p}` and `…/plans/{plan}` take `retire_at`
    and `deprecation_message` (and, for a plan, `successor` — a published plan of the product with the same auth
    strategy) while the record is deprecated. Refusals: `409 api-lifecycle-transition`, `409
    api-lifecycle-retire-early` (before `retire_at`), `422 api-lifecycle-successor-invalid`, `409
    api-product-plans-live` (a product retires only once every plan has), and `400 api-lifecycle-invalid-state`
    for creating a record as `deprecated` or `retired`.
  - Deprecating a plan blocks new subscriptions (`accepts_subscriptions: false`, for APX-2.2), adds an
    `api-plan-deprecated` notice and notifies subscribed application owners once per deprecation
    (`owners_notified_at`, claimed with a conditional update). Retiring revokes the plan's provisioning. Until
    applications (APX-2.1/2.2) and provisioning (APX-4.1) ship, those hooks reach nobody and revoke nothing; each
    step is audited as `api_product.plan.deprecate | reinstate | retire` (`api_product.deprecate | reinstate |
    retire` for products) with `owners_notified` / `provisioning_revoked` counts.
  - `POST …/plans/{plan}/migrate` (`{to, dry_run}`, `projects:edit`) moves a deprecated plan's subscriptions to
    `to`'s consumer group (`plan:<product>-<plan>`) keeping every credential (`credentials_changed: false`),
    records `to` as the successor and is audited as `api_product.plan.migrate` (not on a dry run).
  - `GET /v1/versions/{t}/sunset-timeline` returns `products`: deprecated and retired products and plans with
    `retireAt`, `timelineStatus`, `lifecyclePhase` (`deprecated | sunset_reached | retired`), the message and the
    successor plan — empty without `projects:view`, filtered by `projectId`.
  - `x-apiome-plans` entries of a deprecated plan carry `retire_at`, `deprecation_message` and `successor`.

    `idp_config_id`, `scopes` — never a secret); `limits` `[{window, requests}]` with `window` `second | minute |
    hour | day | month`; optional `concurrency`; `approval` `auto | manual`; `environments` (gateway config ids)
    and `declared_only`; optional `credential_ttl_days` (1–3650); `terms_url` (http/https), `pricing_note`,
    `billing_ref` (internal); `state` `draft | published | deprecated | retired`.
  - `GET | POST /v1/tenants/{t}/products/{p}/plans` and `GET | PATCH | DELETE …/plans/{plan}`
    (`projects:view | edit`). Limits validate: every count positive (422) and every window once
    (`400 api-plan-invalid`). An auth setting on the wrong strategy is refused. `environments` are gateway config
    slugs or ids (`422 api-plan-environment-not-found`). A plan with no environment, or one whose connector cannot
    provision — every connector until APX-4.1 — is saved with `declared_only: true` and an
    `api-plan-declared-only` notice. A member whose resolved version declares no security scheme for the plan's
    strategy (`apiKey`; `oauth2` / `openIdConnect`; `mutualTLS`) is an `api-plan-auth-mismatch` warning on reads.
    Every write is audited (`api_product.plan.create | update | delete`).
  - Export: an authenticated export of a revision that an API product includes (a member resolves to it today)
    carries the product's non-retired plans. OpenAPI writes them as the root `x-apiome-plans` extension in every
    dialect (3.2, 3.1, 3.0, Swagger 2.0), without `billing_ref` or the IdP config id. Every other target's
    fidelity report lists them as an `info` drop; OpenAPI's lists them as kept. Public (anonymous) exports carry no
    plans.

### 1.718.0 — 2026-11-15

#### Added
- **Compatibility modes in the classified diff and compatibility API (XPC-4.5, #5749)** — OpenAPI 1.578.0:
  - `POST /v1/diff/{tenant}/classified` and `POST /v1/versions/{tenant}/{project}/compatibility` take `mode`
    (`BACKWARD` / `FORWARD` / `FULL` / `NONE`, any case; a `_TRANSITIVE` name also sets `transitive`), `transitive`
    and `category` (Protobuf: `WIRE` / `WIRE_JSON` / `PACKAGE` / `FILE`). Each defaults to the project's style-guide
    policy; an unknown value is a `400`.
  - Revisions whose `source_format` has a mode-aware classifier (Avro, JSON Schema, AsyncAPI) or a category-aware one
    (Protobuf) are rebuilt as canonical models and graded by it (`app.compatibility_modes`); an inline head is read
    with the base's importer. Other formats keep the OpenAPI taxonomy (`ctg`) or the native engine
    (`openapi-compatibility`).
  - Every response carries `evaluatedUnder` (`mode`, `transitive`, `category`, `formats`, `modeApplied`,
    `categoryApplied`, `ruleset`, `source`, `comparedRevisions`, `comparedRevisionsTruncated`). Classified-diff
    changes add `grade` and `rationale` when a canonical classifier graded them; compatibility findings add `ruleId`,
    `severity` and, on a transitive check, `against`. The markdown changelog ends with a "Graded under …" line when a
    mode, category or transitive check applied.
  - `transitive` compares the head with every earlier revision of the base (published ancestors; a catalog item's
    earlier revisions), at most 50: every base finding is kept, earlier revisions add only breaking findings not
    already reported, each naming its revision (`Database.list_prior_revisions_for_transitive_check`).
  - `NONE` grades as `BACKWARD` would, with breaks lowered to dangerous and rationales led by `[NONE]`.
  - `GET /v1/compatibility/rules?format=` — the rule catalogue (`app.compatibility_rule_catalogue`): every rule id
    XPC-4.1–4.4 emit with its family, formats, direction, severity per mode or per Protobuf category, and description.
    Readable with `diff:read` and `registry:read` API keys. `scripts/generate_compatibility_rule_catalogue.py` renders
    it into `apiome-docs/docs/govern/compatibility-modes.md`.
  - Style-guide policy `compatibilityMode` (default `BACKWARD`), `compatibilityTransitive` (default `false`) and
    `protobufBreakingCategory` (default `WIRE_JSON`) on `GET`/`PUT /v1/style-guides/{tenant}/{guide}/policy`, resolved
    through the GOV-1.4 guide chain (`app.compatibility_policy`) and frozen into `style_guide_revisions.policy`
    (migration V382; the roadmap's V276 was taken).
  - The breaking-change publish guardrail grades by the project's policy: canonical classifiers for mode-graded
    formats, and every earlier published revision when transitive. `breakingChanges[]` entries name `againstVersion`
    / `againstRevisionId`, the message names the earlier version, and the payload carries `evaluatedUnder`.

#### Changed
- `AvroBreakingChangeClassifier(mode=…)` grades by mode (a problem is breaking when the mode checks its direction,
  dangerous otherwise); under a mode other than the default `BACKWARD` its rationale starts with the mode.
- `ClassifiedChange` carries an optional `rationale` (omitted when unset), used as the changelog summary of a rule the
  taxonomy does not know.

### 1.717.0 — 2026-11-15

#### Added
- **AsyncAPI channel and operation compatibility (XPC-4.4, #5748)** — OpenAPI 1.577.0 (no schema change):
  - `AsyncApiBreakingChangeClassifier(mode=…)` (2.x and 3.x) grades channels, operations, messages, payloads and servers
    for **consumers** and **producers** and reads the two grades by compatibility mode: `BACKWARD` (default; new
    consumers against old producers), `FORWARD` (old consumers against new producers) or `FULL`, `_TRANSITIVE`
    accepted. A side the mode does not check drops one tier. `classify_asyncapi(..., mode=…)` takes the same values.
  - New module `app.asyncapi_compatibility_rules` (`evaluate`, `severity_under`, `mode_sides`): `address-changed`,

    `reply-removed`, `message-removed`, `message-added`, `server-changed` and `security-changed`. Rule ids are
    `asyncapi.<side>.<rule>`, naming the side the change is worst for (`asyncapi.consumer.message-removed`); every
    rationale starts with the mode (`[BACKWARD: new consumers against old producers] …`) and ends with both sides'
    grades. A channel whose address moved, and an AsyncAPI 2 operation without an `operationId` whose action flipped,
    are paired across their removed and added rows. Server findings are `unattributed`.

    when `buf` can compile the `.proto` text) — keeping that format's rule ids; a change of schema language is

#### Added
- **Protobuf reserved numbers and Buf breaking categories (XPC-4.3, #5747)** — OpenAPI 1.576.0 (no schema change):
  - `ProtobufBreakingChangeClassifier(category=…)` grades at a `buf breaking` category (`WIRE` / `WIRE_JSON` / `PACKAGE`
    / `FILE`, any case; default `WIRE_JSON`). `classify_protobuf(..., strictness=…)` and `classify_async(strictness=…)`
    take the same values and run `buf` at that category. New `coerce_category` and the `BufBreakingCategory` alias.
  - New module `app.proto_breaking_rules` (`category_findings`): structural rules graded under all four categories, with
    no `buf` binary needed — `reserved-removed` (dangerous), `reserved-number-reused` / `reserved-name-reused` (breaking),
    `field-deleted-unreserved` / `field-deleted` (graded by which of number and name the new version reserves),
    `field-renamed`, `field-number-reused`, `json-name-changed`, `type-moved-file`, `package-changed`,
    `enum-value-number-reused`, `enum-value-number-changed`, `oneof-membership-changed`, `cardinality-changed`,
    `required-changed` and `presence-changed`. Rule ids are `protobuf.<category>.<rule>`, naming the least strict category
    where the rule is at its worst (`protobuf.wire_json.json-name-changed`); every rationale starts with the category
    graded at (`[WIRE_JSON] …`) and a rule's rationale lists its grade under all four. A modified change confined to
    reservations / oneof declarations grades `protobuf.compatible` (safe).
  - Grades follow Buf's rule placement except where the roadmap decided otherwise: removing a reservation is dangerous,
    and deleting a field whose number is not reserved is dangerous under `WIRE`. A Buf rule corpus
    (`tests/fixtures/proto_breaking_categories`, recorded by `scripts/record_proto_breaking_fixtures.py`) pins every rule
    in every category and lists those two disagreements.
  - The `buf breaking` overlay now lists each `buf` finding in `unattributed` (rule `protobuf.buf-breaking.<type>`) when
    it finds a break, and names any disagreement with the structural rules in the rationale
    (`overlay_disagreement`).
  - The Protobuf normalizer records a field's `json_name` in `extras` when it differs from the `protoc` default, and each
    target file's package, syntax and top-level types under `CanonicalApi.extras["protobuf_files"]` (kept out of the
    version fingerprint, like `xml_import_graph`, and out of the import pipeline's revision fingerprint, so a descriptor set
    and its source tree still fingerprint alike). The `.proto` emitter writes a recorded `json_name` back.

#### Changed
- Protobuf grades now carry the category in their rationale, and catalog drift and the re-import delta show the new
  rules' grades. Protobuf corpus goldens gain the `protobuf_files` record (fingerprints unchanged).

### 1.715.0 — 2026-11-15

#### Added
- **JSON Schema open/closed compatibility classifier (XPC-4.2, #5746)** — OpenAPI 1.575.0 (no schema change):
  - New breaking-change classifier `jsonschema-compatibility`, registered under `json-schema` (the key the JSON Schema
    import source emits), `jsonschema` and `json-schema-2020-12`. It compares each type's schema from the imported
    document (`raw["source"]`) — falling back to `canonical_json_schema.build_bundle_schemas` when either version has
    none — and grades every canonical change by Confluent compatibility mode (`BACKWARD` default; `FORWARD`, `FULL`,
    `*_TRANSITIVE` via `JsonSchemaBreakingChangeClassifier(mode=…)`): a finding that breaks a direction the mode checks is
    breaking, one that breaks only the other direction is dangerous.
  - The open/closed content model follows Confluent and Apicurio: a property added to a closed model
    (`additionalProperties: false` / `unevaluatedProperties: false`) breaks FORWARD, removed breaks BACKWARD; in an open
    model the reverse; a partially open model checks the property against its `additionalProperties` schema. Also graded:
    `additionalProperties` open↔closed, `required` added/removed, `enum`/`const` narrowed/widened, `type` widened
    (`integer` → `number`, FORWARD only) / narrowed / changed, `oneOf`/`anyOf` branches removed/added, bounds
    (`maximum`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, …) tightened/loosened, `pattern`/`format`/`multipleOf`, `uniqueItems`, and
    `allOf` part by part. Local `$ref`s resolve per version; a shared definition is compared once, on itself.
  - Stable rule ids `jsonschema.<backward|forward>.<rule>` (e.g. `jsonschema.forward.closed-property-added`); unmodeled
    keywords (`not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `patternProperties`, …) and external `$ref` changes are
    `jsonschema.review.*` (dangerous, never fail a mode). Rationales name the mode and the content model.
  - Findings with no canonical change (an `additionalProperties` flip, a nested-object property) are kept in
    `unattributed` and count toward the overall severity. New modules `app.jsonschema_compatibility` (pure comparator,
    `compare_schemas`, `is_compatible(findings, mode)`) and `app.jsonschema_breaking`.

#### Changed
- Catalog drift and the re-import delta now grade JSON Schema items with `jsonschema-compatibility` instead of the
  builtin ruleset. A property added to an open schema is now breaking, and one added to a closed schema dangerous.

    `(buf.validate.oneof)`), and write constraints from any other source as rules. New emit option `protovalidate`

### 1.713.1 — 2026-11-15

#### Changed
- **Per-thread pooled database connections** — `Database` no longer shares one psycopg2 connection across every
  request thread:
  - Each thread works on its own connection, so concurrent requests no longer queue on one connection, and one
    request's `commit` / `rollback` can no longer land in the middle of another's transaction.
  - A thread borrows a connection on first use; when the thread ends the connection returns to an idle pool bounded by
    `DB_POOL_MAX_IDLE` (default 10). An instance holds at most one connection per worker thread (~41).
  - Assigning `db.connection = conn` still pins one connection for every thread (the `requires_db` test harnesses).
- **Database index cleanup (apiome-db V381)** — OpenAPI 1.573.1 (no schema change):
  - API-key authentication stamps `api_keys.last_used_at` at most once a minute per key instead of on every request;
    V381 also drops the index on that column, so the stamp no longer rewrites every index on the row.
  - V381 drops 85 redundant indexes, adds referencing-column indexes for the 96 foreign keys a project or version
    delete checks that had none, and adds indexes for the latest-revision lookup in the project and catalog lists and the
    export webhook stale-attempt claim.

#### Fixed
- `Database.get_data_snapshot` closed the process-wide database connection after every read (`GET` of a single data
  record), forcing a reconnect for the next request. It now goes through `execute_query` like every other read.

    every thread record carries `origin`. Resolving a consumer thread never sends the reader a workspace
