### 1.710.0 — 2026-11-14

#### Added
- **Reader sign-in for Browse (PCX-1.1, #5889)** — OpenAPI 1.570.0, new tag `portal-auth`:
  - A **reader** is an ordinary `users` row with a per-tenant `portal_memberships` row (`invited | active |
    revoked`, source `magic_link`). It grants no workspace access. apiome-db V378 adds `portal_memberships`,
    `portal_magic_links` and `portal_reader_sessions`.
  - `POST /v1/portal/{tenant}/auth/magic-link` mails a one-time sign-in link (15-minute expiry, bcrypt-hashed
    with a lookup prefix). It **always answers `202`** for well-formed input, so it never reveals whether an
    account exists. A new address gets a password-less user and an `invited` membership when the installation
    sign-up policy allows new accounts; a second request reuses both. Budgeted per client address and per email
    (`APIOME_PORTAL_MAGIC_LINK_RATE_LIMIT_IP_PER_MINUTE`, default 10; `…_EMAIL_PER_MINUTE`, default 3):
    `429 portal-rate-limited` with `Retry-After`. `422 portal-invalid-email` / `portal-invalid-return-to`.
    Mail goes through SendGrid (`SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`) behind the `ReaderMailer` adapter that PCX-3.1
    will replace; links point at `APIOME_PUBLIC_BROWSE_URL`.
  - `POST …/auth/exchange` trades the token for a reader session and burns it: `410 portal-token-used`,
    `410 portal-token-expired`, `400 portal-token-invalid`. The session token is returned once, is bound to the
    tenant, lives `APIOME_PORTAL_READER_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` (default 168), and stores only its SHA-256 hash and the
    browser family of the `User-Agent`. The exchange marks the account verified only when it has no usable
    password, so an unconfirmed workspace sign-up at the same address is never unlocked by a reader link.
  - `POST …/auth/sign-out` revokes the session (idempotent `204`); `GET …/auth/me` returns the reader or
    `401 portal-session-invalid`. Revoking a session, the membership, or the user takes effect on the next request.
  - The session travels as `Authorization: Reader <token>` and is **never a REST credential** outside the
    `portal-auth` and `browse` tags: the JWT / API-key gates refuse it, and a sweep over every `GET` route proves a
    reader session gets nothing an anonymous caller does not. The browse routes check it (a revoked session is a
    `401`) and still serve the public slice until PCX-1.3.
  - Access audit rows `portal.reader.enrolled`, `portal.reader.signed_in` and `portal.reader.session_revoked`
    (source `portal`, metadata only).

### 1.709.0 — 2026-11-14

#### Added
- **Branch / merge-request spec workflow (COL-4.3, #4527)** — OpenAPI 1.569.0:
  - `GET|POST …/projects/{project}/draft-branches` lists and creates **draft branches**. Creating one copies the
    tip of a version line (a branch — `base_branch`, the default branch when omitted) into a new draft revision
    (`version_label`, the next patch version by default) that becomes the branch's tip, in one transaction, so
    edits on the branch never touch the line. Needs `versions:create`.
  - `GET|POST …/projects/{project}/merge-requests` lists and opens merge requests from a draft branch into a line
    (the line it was drafted off by default). Opening requests the COL-2.1 review of the branch tip from
    `reviewers`, or attaches the tip's open review. One open merge request per branch (`409 mr-already-open`).
  - `GET …/merge-requests/{id}` returns the branches' tips, the merge base, the review, the latest merge session
    with its conflicts, and `readiness` — `can_merge` plus every blocker (`no-review`, `review-outdated`,
    `review-pending`, `changes-requested`, `review-stale`, `approval-policy`, `conflicts`, `target-immutable`).
  - `POST …/check` runs the existing merge preview with a persisted merge session and attaches it; conflicts
    leave the session `resolving`. `POST …/merge` requires an approved, current review (and the COL-2.3 approval
    policy, when one applies), runs a fresh merge session and then the existing `version-branches/merge` path:
    `409 mr-not-ready` with `blockers`, `409 mr-conflicts` with `conflicts`, and the merge path's own refusals
    (`STALE_HEAD`, `PUBLISHED_IMMUTABLE`, `MERGE_BLOCKED_BY_COMPAT_GATE`) unchanged. The session ends `applied`
    (or `aborted` on a refusal). `POST …/review` reviews the branch's current tip after it moved on;
    `POST …/close` closes without merging and withdraws the review when the closer may.
  - apiome-db V377 adds `merge_requests` and `version_branches.draft_of_branch_id`.

### 1.707.0 — 2026-11-14

#### Added
- **Project presence and element soft locks (COL-4.1, #4525)** — OpenAPI 1.567.0:
  - `GET …/projects/{project}/presence` reads who has the project open and which elements are locked;
    `POST …/presence/heartbeat` announces a tab (`session_id`, `view`, `held`), renews the locks it holds and
    answers the same snapshot, with `lost` naming held elements another tab now holds (the previous holder's
    takeover notice); `POST …/presence/leave` releases a tab's presence and locks.
  - Soft locks are advisory leases: `PUT|DELETE …/presence/locks/{element_key}` take and release one
    (`409 presence-lock-held` names the holder), `POST …/presence/request-takeover/{element_key}` asks the holder to
    hand over, and `POST …/presence/take-over/{element_key}` forces it 15 seconds after the request. Presence lapses
    after 45 seconds and locks after 60 without a heartbeat, so a crashed tab never leaves a stuck lock.
  - `WS …/presence/ws` is the push channel (first frame `{"type":"auth","authorization":"Bearer …"}`; then
    `heartbeat`, `lock`, `unlock`, `request_takeover`, `take_over`); it sends a snapshot after each frame and every
    5 seconds, and closing it releases the tab at once. JWT only; API keys use the HTTP routes.
  - Requires `projects:view`; `APIOME_PRESENCE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 240) bounds a user's calls.
  - apiome-db V375 adds `project_presence` and `element_locks`.

### 1.703.0 — 2026-11-14

#### Added
- **GraphQL protocol adapter in the contract suite (XPC-1.2, #5730)** — OpenAPI 1.563.0:
  - `POST /v1/tenants/{t}/contracts/{ref}/suite` compiles a GraphQL version through its own
    protocol adapter: one operation per root `query`/`mutation` field, with cases in the REST
    preference order — declared `@example` arguments, generated arguments (required-only, then
    every argument, seeded through `schema_instance_synthesis`), then a required argument
    omitted, a wrong-typed argument and an unknown field selected. The selection set expands to
    `options.max_selection_depth` levels (default 3, 1–8); deeper fields and nested fields with
    required arguments are left out and reported (`SELECTION_DEPTH_LIMITED`,
    `FIELD_ARGUMENTS_REQUIRED`). The same seed gives the same digest.
  - `ContractCase` gains `protocol` (`http` default, `graphql`) and `graphql`
    (`ContractGraphqlRequest`: `query`, `variables`, `operationName`, `operation_type`, `field`);
    the manifest gains `protocol` and `unsupported` (`SuiteUnsupportedOperation`), where
    subscriptions are listed with a reason. `schema_version` and `compiler_version` are now `2`,
    and `counts` carries `negative_unknown_field`, so REST digests change too.
  - A GraphQL version with no query or mutation field answers `ok: false` with `FORMAT_MISMATCH`.
  - `POST …/run` posts each GraphQL case to the target URL itself and judges the envelope: a
    success case needs no `errors` and `data` matching the selection's schema (violations are
    located by JSON Pointer into `data`); a negative case needs a non-empty `errors` array. New
    failure codes `graphql-errors-present`, `graphql-errors-missing`, `graphql-envelope-invalid`.
    Mutations obey `allow_mutating_methods`; queries do not (provider verification too).
  - Verification targets and runs carry `protocol` (`VerificationTargetInput`/`Patch`/`Record`,
    `ResolvedTarget`, `VerificationRunInput`/`Summary`/`Record`, the JUnit `apiome.protocol`
    property). A run whose target speaks another protocol is refused `422
    target-protocol-mismatch` and audited as a denied resolve. Migration **V371** adds
    `verification_target.protocol` and `verification_run.protocol` (`http` default, CHECK
    `http`/`graphql`).

    `manifestDigest`) of the embedded manifest. It changes when curation changes (a tool enabled or
    disabled, an accepted description served) and not otherwise. The tenant-wide digest is the
    SHA-256 of the sorted `(toolsetId, digest)` pairs. Documents carry no timestamps, so they are
    byte-stable, and both routes send a content-addressed `ETag`.

    `apiome.<tenant>/agent-runtime` entry for callers holding one of the tenant's credentials.
    `search` and `version` filter it, `updated_since` does not (it has no timestamp), and it is
    also served by name on the versions routes. It is never served anonymously. A tenant with no
    enabled toolset has no entry, and a build failure drops the entry, not the page.

### 1.700.0 — 2026-11-14

#### Added
- **Bulk CSV member import and export (EID-2.5, #5671)** — two routes on the access plane:
  - `POST /v1/access/{tenant_slug}/members/import?dryRun=true` (`members:create`, multipart `file`)
    reads an `email,role,display_name` CSV (header required, only `email` mandatory, at most 1,000
    rows and 1 MiB) and returns `{dry_run, total, max_rows, seats_free, counts, rows}`. Each row
    carries its file `line` and an `outcome`: `invite`, `already-member` (a member, or listed
    earlier in the file), `invalid-email`, `unknown-role` (the `role` cell matched no role id, slug
    or name), `no-account` (no Apiome account uses the address, so the invite route would 404) or
    `seat-cap` (past the free license seats). `invite` rows carry the `role_id` to send. The dry
    run writes nothing — no membership, role or audit row. It is the only mode: `dryRun=false` is
    a 400 that points at `POST /v1/access/{tenant_slug}/members`, through which each `invite` row
    is applied, so the seat guard (`license-seats-exhausted`), rate limit and `member.invited`
    audit entry apply per row.
  - `GET /v1/access/{tenant_slug}/members/export` (`members:view`) downloads the roster as CSV:
    `email,status,role,two_factor,provenance,last_sign_in,created`. `provenance` is `invite`,
    `sso:<id>` or `scim` (read from the membership's `provisioned_by` when SSO/SCIM provisioning
    writes it; `invite` until then), `last_sign_in` is the newest successful `sign_in` in
    `auth_events`, and a cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is prefixed with `'` (the import
    strips it again). Importing an export reports every row as `already-member`.
  - `Database.get_users_by_emails` and `Database.list_member_last_sign_ins` back them;
    `license_capacity.member_seats_free` counts the free seats with the seat guard's accounting.
  OpenAPI document version 1.560.0.

    target. When on, the SDL is Apollo Federation v2 subgraph SDL: an

    inferred provenance note (`/types/<key>/@key`); no entity at all is an `n/a` loss
    `federation-no-entities`. `GraphQlFidelityRulePack` reads the option (`apply_options`) and
    reports each synthesized key as `SYNTH`, so the preview and the export agree.

### 1.696.0 — 2026-11-13

#### Added
- **Protobuf / Connect RPC export: `google.api.http` annotations (MFX-12.6, #4343)**
  - New `http_annotations` option (title **HTTP annotations**, default `false`) on the `protobuf`
    and `connectrpc` targets. When on, each `rpc` whose source operation has an HTTP method and
    route gets `option (google.api.http) = { <verb>: "<route>" [body: "*"] };` and the file
    imports `google/api/annotations.proto`. `GET`/`PUT`/`POST`/`DELETE`/`PATCH` are written as
    that verb, any other method as `custom { kind path }`. A POST/PUT/PATCH with a request body
    gets `body: "*"`, and a route variable that is not a field name (`{pet-id}`) is renamed
    (`{pet_id}`). An RPC source's `extras["http"]` binding is used when the operation has no
    REST verb, and keeps its recorded `body`.
  - Emit losses: with the option off, each binding is an `http-binding` loss (the binding is
    dropped). With it on, an `http-annotation-unbound` loss names any route variable or query
    parameter the request message has no field for, and any header or cookie.
  - Fidelity: `ProtoFidelityRulePack` reads the option (`apply_options`). A REST binding is a
    `DROP` (warn) when the option is off. When it is on, the binding is `OK` if every input binds
    and `APPROX` otherwise, so the preview and the export job agree.
  - Toolchain checks: `buf lint` / `buf build` stage the vendored `google/api` protos an
    annotated bundle imports, so the bundle builds with no network. With the default `buf.yaml`,
    `buf lint` ignores those vendored files. The `connectrpc` target now declares the same
    `buf lint` / `buf build` test tools as `protobuf`.
  - Goldens: export surface parity (with its UI, browse and CLI copies) and the proto3
    projection-corpus manifest now list the dropped REST binding.
  - OpenAPI 1.555.0 → 1.556.0.

#### Added

  behind Cloudflare, Fastly or a custom purge endpoint, and the CDN is purged when a release goes
  live:
  - `GET/POST/DELETE /v1/slate/environments/{id}/cdn` read, attach/update and detach the lane's
    provider: Cloudflare zone id + API token, Fastly service id + API key, or a custom https purge
    URL + auth header. The credential is write-only, sealed at rest under its own vault
    (`APIOME_SLATE_CDN_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS`, magic `OSCV`) and never returned; saving with
    no key configured is refused with 409 `cdn-vault-not-configured`. Blank keeps the stored
    credential unless the provider changes.

    releases on the lane's verified hosts (`POST …/promote` and `…/rollback` carry `cdnPurge`).
    Over the provider's per-purge cap, or with no changed-page record, the whole CDN cache is
    purged and the response says so. A CDN failure is reported and logged; it never fails the
    activation.
  - **Manual purges dispatch.** `POST …/cache/purge` on a lane with a provider sends every
    in-scope URL to the CDN and records `outcome: dispatched` when the CDN accepted it (V187's
    CHECK now has an attached edge to allow it); a refusal stays `recorded` with an error code such
    as `cdn-auth-rejected` or `cdn-rate-limited`. `GET …/cache` no longer claims its rules shape
    responses at the CDN: the origin does not emit them as headers.
  - `GET …/cdn/dispatches` lists every purge sent, with mode, URL count, status and a redacted
    provider message. Purges are sent by URL through the SSRF-guarded client with fixed vendor
    hosts; a custom URL that resolves to a private address is refused before the credential is
    sent.

    …/deprecations/{id}` withdraws one. After the sunset, new pins answer 409

    skips published project versions, classifies each eligible version's document before and

### 1.683.0 — 2026-11-08

#### Added
- **MCP public publish workflow + guards (V2-MCP-23.5 / MCAT-9.5, #3695).**
  `POST /v1/mcp/{tenant}/endpoints/{id}/publish` sets `published=true, visibility='public'` only
  after three guards pass; every guard runs, so a refusal lists every reason. A failure is `422`
  with `detail: {code: "publish_guards_failed", message, failed_guards, guards}`; success returns
  the endpoint and every guard's verdict. `POST …/unpublish` reverts to
  `published=false, visibility='private'` (idempotent, no guards).
  - `credentials` — the fields the public view and public pages show (name, slug, category,
    description, host; the current snapshot's server name/title, instructions and capability
    names/titles/descriptions) are scanned with the intake secret scrubber. Findings name the
    field and secret type, never the value.
  - `grade` — the current snapshot's stored grade must be at least `APIOME_MCP_PUBLISH_MIN_GRADE`
    (new setting, `A`–`F`, default `C`; `off` disables it; any other value is `503`). An unscored
    endpoint fails.
  - `reachable` — enabled, not quarantined, discovered, no consecutive discovery failures, and the
    latest health probe of the last 24 hours (if any) is `up`.
  - New models `McpPublishGuardOut` and `McpEndpointPublishResponse`.

#### Changed
- `PATCH /v1/mcp/{tenant}/endpoints/{id}` no longer bypasses the guards: a patch that makes an
  endpoint published and public runs every publish guard, and a patch that edits the name,
  description, category or URL of an endpoint that is already public runs the credentials guard.

### 1.680.0 — 2026-11-08

  periodic reachability / latency probe, much lighter than discovery: the MCP `initialize`

    enabled, non-`stdio` endpoints whose last probe is older than the cadence (quarantined ones

    probe failure is a `down` row, never an exception, and never touches discovery failure /
    backoff / quarantine state. Settings: `APIOME_MCP_HEALTH_ENABLED` (true),
    `APIOME_MCP_HEALTH_CADENCE` (300), `APIOME_MCP_HEALTH_MIN_INTERVAL` (60),

    `APIOME_MCP_HEALTH_MAX_PER_TICK` (200).

    `degraded` when it succeeded but the window's uptime is under 99%, `up` otherwise, `unknown`
    with no probe; `uptime_pct`; nearest-rank p50 / p95 latency of the successful probes.

    (`io-github-acme-weather`) instead of the last segment.

    registry endpoint with the same `registry_metadata.serverName`
    (`Database.find_registry_mcp_endpoint`, case-insensitive). One from the same registry is

    `discovered` with `duplicate-name`.
  - **`_meta` status.** Listings now keep `deleted` entries (`McpRegistryClient.list_servers_page` /

    `discovered` with `registry-deleted`. Restoring it to `active` imports it again.
    `deprecated` entries import as before. Each run's `summary.findings` lists
    `mcp-registry-deprecated` / `mcp-registry-deleted` entries. A status change re-syncs the entry

  - **Static credentials:** a stored bearer or custom-header secret is sealed (no plaintext in the
    row), masked on read, and sent in a header on discovery, never in the URL. Clearing it returns
    the endpoint to `auth_required`.
  - **OAuth:** discovery's `401` stores the metadata. `oauth/authorize` registers a client, the
    consent redirect returns a code, and `oauth/callback` stores sealed tokens with no token in any
    response. The next discovery sends the access token.
  - **One-time callback:** a callback is accepted once, and only from the user who started it.
  - **Refresh:** an expiring token is refreshed (and rotated) before a run. A token the server
    rejects is refreshed and the run retried. A failed refresh keeps the token and records why.
  - **Compare-and-set:** the token store's compare-and-set wins once and then loses against the
    same expected stamp.

#### Fixed
- `Database.store_mcp_endpoint_oauth_tokens` stamps `last_refreshed_at` with `clock_timestamp()`
  instead of `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`. The stamp is the refresh compare-and-set token and the "did a
  forced refresh change anything" signal. `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is fixed for a transaction, so two
  writes in one transaction shared a stamp: the second compare-and-set wrongly succeeded, and a
  forced refresh looked like no change. apiome-rest 1.674.0 → 1.674.1 (no API change).

### 1.674.0 — 2026-11-08

#### Added
- **OAuth 2.1 authorization code + PKCE + refresh for protected MCP servers (V2-MCP-20.4 / MCAT-6.4,
  #3680).** Once discovery has stored a server's authorization-server metadata (MCAT-6.3), Apiome
  can obtain and renew tokens for it.
  - **Routes:**
    - `POST /v1/mcp/{tenant_slug}/endpoints/{endpoint_id}/oauth/authorize` takes `redirect_uri`
      (plus optional `client_id`, `client_secret`, `scopes`) and returns the `authorization_url`.
    - `POST /v1/mcp/{tenant_slug}/oauth/callback` takes the redirect's `state` with `code` (or
      `error`, `error_description`) and `iss`. It exchanges the code and returns the endpoint id
      and its redacted credential status. Neither route returns a token.
  - **Protocol** (`app/mcp_oauth_flow.py`):
    - PKCE `S256` on every authorization. A server that does not advertise it is refused
      (`409 pkce_unsupported`).
    - The RFC 8707 `resource` goes on the authorization request, the code exchange and every refresh.
    - Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) registers a public client when no `client_id` is
      given, and is reused for the same redirect URI and issuer. A server without a registration
      endpoint needs a `client_id` (`409 client_required`).
    - The token endpoint is called with `none`, `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`.
    - An RFC 9207 `iss` on the callback must match the issuer.
    - A JWT access token whose `aud` names another resource is refused (`audience_mismatch`).
    - Requests follow the discovery URL rules: https only (http to loopback), no private IP
      literals, no redirects, a 10 s timeout and a 256 KB body cap.
  - **State** (`app/mcp_oauth_service.py`): the PKCE verifier and the client travel in a `state`
    sealed with AES-256-GCM under the credential master key, with its own envelope magic (`OMOS`).
    It is bound to the tenant and the user who started it and expires after 10 minutes. Only the
    SHA-256 of its nonce is stored (`oauth_metadata.pending_authorization`), and
    `Database.consume_mcp_endpoint_oauth_pending` accepts each state once.
  - **Storage:** the tokens, the refresh token and any client secret are sealed as an `oauth2`
    credential by the new `Database.store_mcp_endpoint_oauth_tokens`, which merges a non-secret
    `oauth_metadata.token` summary (`client_id`, `client_registration`, `scope`, `expires_at`,
    `refreshable`, `refreshed_at`, `last_refresh_error`).
  - **Refresh:** `load_endpoint_auth_headers` (used by discovery, the sweep, the test harness,
    provider verification and the contract runner) refreshes a token that expires within 60 s
    before building headers. A process-local lock and a compare-and-set on `last_refreshed_at`
    keep two refreshes from both being stored. When discovery still gets `401` with a stored OAuth
    token, it forces one refresh (`refresh_endpoint_auth_headers`) and retries once. A failed
    refresh keeps the old token and records `last_refresh_error`.

#### Changed
- `POST …/endpoints/{id}/test` now loads the stored headers off the event loop, since loading them
  may refresh a token.
- OpenAPI 1.535.0 → 1.536.0; apiome-rest 1.673.0 → 1.674.0.

### 1.673.0 — 2026-11-08

#### Added
- **OAuth 2.1 discovery for protected MCP servers (V2-MCP-20.3 / MCAT-6.3, #3679).** When a
  discovery run gets `401`, the new `app/mcp_oauth_discovery.py` parses the `WWW-Authenticate`
  challenge (RFC 9110). It fetches the Protected Resource Metadata from the `Bearer` challenge's
  `resource_metadata` URL, or from the well-known `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` URL with
  the endpoint's path, then at the root (RFC 9728). It then fetches each listed authorization
  server's `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` metadata until one validates (RFC 8414).
  - **Checks:**
    - The PRM `resource` must share the endpoint's origin and be a path prefix of it.
    - The AS `issuer` must equal the issuer it was fetched for.
    - `authorization_endpoint` and `token_endpoint` are required.
    - Every URL must be `https://` (`http://` only to loopback) and not a private IP literal.
    - Redirects are not followed, each fetch times out after 10 s, and bodies over 256 KB are refused.
  - **Storage:** the result is merged into `mcp_endpoint_credentials.oauth_metadata` by the new
    `Database.merge_mcp_endpoint_oauth_metadata`. If the endpoint has no credential, it creates an
    `auth_type='none'` row with no secret, so the endpoint still runs anonymously. It never touches
    a stored secret.
  - **Stored keys:** issuer, authorization / token / registration / revocation endpoints, resource
    indicator, scopes, the challenge's scopes, grant / response / auth-method lists, and
    `pkce_s256_supported`.
  - **Job result:** the failed discovery job's `result.oauth_discovery` reports `resolved` or
    `failed` with a code (`not_found`, `resource_mismatch`, `issuer_mismatch`, `invalid_metadata`,
    `invalid_url`, `fetch_failed`, `store_failed`).

#### Changed
- `PUT …/endpoints/{id}/credentials` without `oauth_metadata` now keeps the stored metadata instead
  of clearing it; sending `oauth_metadata` still replaces it.
- OpenAPI 1.534.0 → 1.535.0; apiome-rest 1.672.2 → 1.673.0.

### 1.671.0 — 2026-11-08

#### Added
- **Legacy HTTP+SSE MCP transport, with automatic fallback (V2-MCP-16.5 / MCAT-2.5, #3661).**
  Apiome now reaches MCP servers that still speak the 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport. The new
  `app.mcp_client.transport_sse.LegacySseTransport` opens the `GET` event stream, waits for the
  server's `endpoint` event, POSTs every JSON-RPC message to that URL and reads the responses off
  the stream. It reuses the Streamable HTTP transport's security rules (no plaintext `http://` to a
  non-loopback host, the SSRF guard), status taxonomy and protocol-transcript recording, and it only
  POSTs to an endpoint on the same scheme, host and port as the stream, so a server cannot redirect
  the endpoint's auth headers elsewhere.
  `app.mcp_client.connect.open_session` picks the transport: an endpoint stored with
  `transport='sse'` uses the legacy transport directly; any other endpoint tries Streamable HTTP and
  falls back when the `initialize` POST is answered `400`, `404`, `405`, `406` or `415`. A `401`,
  `403` or `429` never triggers the fallback, and when the server speaks neither transport the
  original Streamable HTTP error is reported. Discovery jobs (`POST …/endpoints/{id}/discover` and
  the sweep) and capability tests (`POST …/endpoints/{id}/test`) both connect this way. The
  handshake accepts protocol `2024-11-05` over the legacy transport only; Streamable HTTP still
  refuses it. No request or response shape changes.

### 1.655.0 — 2026-11-05

#### Added
- **Auto-export on version publish (MFX-39.4, #4336).**
  - **Subscriptions:** `POST` / `GET /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/auto-exports` and `PATCH` / `DELETE …/{subscription_id}`
    run an export preset (MFX-39.3) on every publish of a project: `projectId`, `preset` (id or name), `haltAt`
    (`critical` default, or `warn`), `approveLoss` (pre-approval) and `active`. Subscribing, switching on and
    pre-approving need `projects:edit` + `versions:publish`; switching off and removing `projects:edit`; reading
    `projects:view`. Audited as `export.auto_export.subscription.*`.
  - **On publish:** `publish_version` queues one run per active subscription after its response
    (`BackgroundTasks`, `enqueue_auto_export_on_publish`); a queueing error is logged and never fails the publish.
    A new sweep (`app/export_auto_worker.py`, ticked by `main.py`) claims runs (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), applies
    the preset to the published revision with `confirm`, runs the export job, and measures its loss (MFX-2.4 made a
    gate): `critical` for a severe or near-empty conversion, a types-only result or a critical construct; `warn`
    for any other loss. At or past `haltAt` without `approveLoss` the run is **halted** — nothing delivered, the
    publisher and the subscriber get an `export_auto_halted` inbox notification, audited as
    `export.auto_export.halted`; otherwise it is delivered through the preset's delivery profile as the publisher
    (`export.auto_export.completed`, with every delivery's outcome). Failed jobs, stale presets and lost runs
    (`APIOME_EXPORT_AUTO_LEASE_SECONDS`) fail the run and notify; full export slots re-queue it.
  - **Runs:** `GET /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/auto-export-runs` (`projectId`, `subscriptionId`, `limit`) lists what each
    publish did — status, export job, loss and reasons, deliveries; `POST …/auto-export-runs/{run_id}/release`
    (`versions:publish`) delivers a halted run anyway (`export.auto_export.released`).
  - Settings: `APIOME_EXPORT_AUTO_ENABLED`, `APIOME_EXPORT_AUTO_INTERVAL`, `APIOME_EXPORT_AUTO_BATCH_SIZE`,
    `APIOME_EXPORT_AUTO_LEASE_SECONDS`.
  - `app/export_auto.py` (rules), `app/export_auto_worker.py`, `app/export_auto_routes.py`; tables
    `export_auto_subscriptions` and `export_auto_runs`, and the `export_auto_halted` inbox type (V359).
  - OpenAPI: the auto-export paths and schemas merged; the notifications path and `NotificationRecord` gain
    `export_auto_halted`.

### 1.653.0 — 2026-11-04

#### Added
- **Export delivery profiles + audit (MFX-38.4, #4331).**
  - **Profiles:** `POST` / `GET /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/delivery-profiles` and `GET` / `PATCH` / `DELETE
    …/delivery-profiles/{profile_id}` store, list (`?channel=`), read, change and remove a workspace's reusable
    delivery destinations — a unique `name`, a `channel` (`git`, `webhook` or `object_storage`) and that channel's
    delivery body in the matching `git` / `webhook` / `objectStorage` block, validated by the channel's own rules.
    The credential is a reference (`credentialRef`): the git repository's linked account, or a storage credential in
    the vault — both must exist when the profile is stored. A webhook's `secret` is sealed on the profile
    (`app.mcp_credential_crypto`) and never returned; a `PATCH` without it keeps the stored one. The channel never
    changes. `projects:edit` (reading: `projects:view`); `400` for an invalid field, unknown reference or refused
    receiver, `409` for a taken name, `503` without `APIOME_MCP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS`. Audited as
    `export.delivery_profile.created` / `.updated` / `.deleted`, never with a secret.
  - **Delivering with a profile:** `POST /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs/{job_id}/deliveries` (`profileId`) runs the
    channel's own delivery with the profile's body, records the profile on the run (`delivery_profile_id`) and adds
    `profileId` to the channel's audit (`export.git_delivery`, `export.webhook_delivery`,
    `export.object_storage_delivery`). The answer summarises the attempt (`outcome`: `in_progress`, `delivered`,
    `failed`) and carries the channel's full run in `run`. `versions:publish`; `503` for a webhook secret the
    deployment cannot open.
  - **Delivery on completion:** `POST /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs` takes `delivery_profiles` (1–5 distinct profile
    ids; not with `dry_run`). As soon as the job completes it is delivered with each, in order, through the same path
    as `POST …/deliveries`, and each adds an `EXPORT_DELIVERED` or `EXPORT_DELIVERY_FAILED` event to the job (with the
    channel, run, destination and error code). A delivery never changes the job's state, and one failing never stops
    the next. Submitting profiles needs `versions:publish` (`403`) and existing profiles (`400`
    `export-delivery-profile-unknown`). The submitter's context is kept in memory with the job, never mirrored.
  - **The trail:** `GET /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs/{job_id}/deliveries` lists every delivery of a job across the
    three channels, and `GET …/delivery-profiles/{profile_id}/deliveries` every delivery made with a profile — each
    with its channel, status, outcome, profile, destination (a webhook URL without its query), attempt count and
    error. `projects:view`.
  - The git, webhook and object-storage delivery routes now share `perform_git_delivery`,
    `perform_webhook_delivery` and `perform_object_storage_delivery` with profile delivery; their behaviour is
    unchanged.
  - `app/export_delivery_profiles.py` (rules), `app/export_delivery_profile_routes.py`; table
    `export_delivery_profiles` and `delivery_profile_id` on the three run tables (V357).
  - OpenAPI: the four new paths and their nine schemas merged into the committed documents.

### 1.651.0 — 2026-11-04

#### Added
- **Webhook delivery for exports (MFX-38.2, #4329).**
  - `POST /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs/{job_id}/deliveries/webhook` sends a **completed** export job's result to
    `url` as one JSON body (`schemaVersion: export.webhook-delivery.v1`, `event: export.delivered`): the export's
    coordinates, the file manifest, the fidelity summary and full report (every target's for a multi-target job), and
    the bundle — inline (UTF-8, or base64 for a zip) up to `APIOME_EXPORT_WEBHOOK_INLINE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB), otherwise
    as a signed, expiring fetch link (`artifact: fetch` always sends the link). `GET` on the same path lists the job's
    deliveries with every attempt. Requires `versions:publish` (listing: `projects:view`); audited as
    `export.webhook_delivery` with the receiver's host only.
  - **Signed:** `X-Apiome-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body under the caller's `secret` (the
    push-webhook scheme). The secret is never stored: the signed bytes and signature are, so retries re-send them
    unchanged, with `X-Apiome-Delivery` (the run id) and `X-Apiome-Delivery-Attempt`.
  - **Retried:** the first attempt is made before the request answers; no answer, `408`, `425`, `429` or `5xx` is
    retried by the webhook delivery sweep after 10 s, 60 s and 5 min (longer when `Retry-After` asks), four attempts
    in all. A `3xx` (redirects are not followed) or another `4xx` fails the run at once.
  - **Guarded:** the SSRF guard checks `url` when it is submitted (`400 export-webhook-delivery-destination-refused`)
    and on every attempt and redirect hop.
  - `GET /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs/{job_id}/deliveries/webhook/{delivery_id}/bundle?expires=…&signature=…` — the
    fetch link: no sign-in, the signature is the credential; `403` when tampered, `410` once it or the artifact
    expires. New settings: `APIOME_API_PUBLIC_URL` (the link's base; falls back to
    `APIOME_REPOSITORY_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL`), `APIOME_EXPORT_WEBHOOK_FETCH_URL_TTL_SECONDS` (24 h),
    `APIOME_EXPORT_FETCH_URL_SIGNING_KEY` (optional; otherwise derived from the JWT secret).
  - `app/export_webhook_delivery.py` (rules), `app/export_webhook_delivery_pipeline.py` (attempts, backoff, sweep),
    `app/export_webhook_delivery_routes.py`; table `export_webhook_delivery_runs` (V355).
  - OpenAPI: the two new paths and their four schemas merged into the committed documents.

  - `POST /v1/export/{tenant_slug}/jobs/{job_id}/deliveries/git` delivers a **completed** export job's bundle into a

    `implMaxLength`; a list's item counts the groupRef's `implMinOccurs` / `implMaxOccurs`; anything else the
    fieldRef's documentation — each `APPROX`, none dropped.

### 1.646.0 — 2026-11-04

#### Added
- **FIX Orchestra emitter (MFX-37.1, #4323).**
  - `app/fix_orchestra_emitter.py`: export target `fix-orchestra` ("FIX Orchestra", data schema, needs a record
    type). Writes an Orchestra 1.0 repository (`<name>.orchestra.xml`, namespace
    `http://fixprotocol.io/2020/orchestra/repository`): messages (the source's, else root records, with `msgType`,
    `flow`, scenario and `responses`), components (held records), repeating groups (lists of records, with a
    `NumInGroup` counter), code sets (enumerations), fields declared once with tags and datatypes and referenced by
    tag, presence / constant values / `rule` + `when`, and actors, state machines and flows when the model carries
    them. Tags: the source's, else from 5000 (user-defined range); ids: the source's, else from 1. Lists of plain
    values and maps become groups, unions components; names, the version and an empty `NoCodeSet` are rewritten
    or synthesized as the XSD requires — each reported. Option `version`.

    Community, tag `v1.6`, Apache-2.0), loaded offline (`orchestra_schema_problems`); every corpus repository and
    typed source exports valid against it. (Wiring it into the export gate is MFX-37.3.)

    dropped constraints, and the re-import measured with the Orchestra importer (MFX-37.2 refines the rules).

    `MODIFY COLUMN`, standard SQL `SET DATA TYPE`), then new FKs named clear of the kept ones. Changes SQL cannot

### 1.632.0 — 2026-11-04

#### Added
- **Agent-interface fidelity packs (MFX-32.4, #4298).** The MCP (`McpFidelityRulePack`) and A2A (`A2aFidelityRulePack`)
  fidelity packs now enumerate what an operation→tool / API→agent-card conversion loses, each with its reason. Shared

  - **HTTP semantics → description text (APPROX):** each MCP tool's `description` ends with

    report lists the binding as APPROX (`HTTP binding → tool description text`).

    implicit/password flows are APPROX; mutual TLS, cookie API keys and unknown types are DROP.

    SSE); channels DROP.

  loss counts and the `wadl → wadl` cell (`ok`) move accordingly.

### 1.619.0 — 2026-11-03

#### Added
- **RELAX NG and DTD output modes for the XSD export (MFX-22.3, #4134).** The `xsd` target takes a `mode` option:
  `xsd` (default), `relaxng` (one RELAX NG grammar in the XML syntax, `<Name>.rng`), `relaxng-compact` (the compact
  syntax, `<Name>.rnc`) or `dtd` (one DTD, `<Name>.dtd`; media types `application/xml`,
  `application/relax-ng-compact-syntax`, `application/xml-dtd`). Each mode is one file, even for a multi-namespace
  item, and is written from the XSD documents the export builds (`app.xml_schema_modes`), so element names,
  occurrences, choices and entry lists are the same in every mode. `xsd_version` applies to `xsd` only; a 1.1 with
  another mode is refused.
  - **RELAX NG:** a `define` per type and per global element (`Pet.element`, chosen by `start`); `optional` /
    `zeroOrMore` / `oneOrMore`; facets as XSD-datatype `param`s; enumerations as `choice`s of `value`s; namespaces
    kept (`ns`, `namespace ns1 = …` in the compact syntax); descriptions as `a:documentation` / `##` comments.
  - **DTD:** content models (`(a, b?, c*)`, `(a | b)`, `(#PCDATA)`, `EMPTY`, `ANY`); attributes as `CDATA` or an
    enumeration of names; each namespaced element declares a `#FIXED` `xmlns`.

    defaults dropped, repeat counts other than 0..1 / 0..* / 1..* widened (`occurrence-bounds`), null as optional,
    examples dropped. DTD: every datatype (`datatype-dropped`) and facet / element enumeration (`facet-dropped`)
    dropped, an element name with two contents declared once as `ANY` (`element-merged`), namespaces as `#FIXED`
    `xmlns` (note). The XSD writer's own losses are restated in the mode's terms.
  - **Checks:** a RELAX NG export is checked by **jing** when the toolchain has it (`relaxng.schema`, via

    `relaxng.reimport`); a DTD export by the DTD reader (`dtd.parse`, `dtd.reimport`). The round trip measures
    through that import (`import_path` `relaxng` / `dtd`).
  - **Toolchain:** `jing` 20220510 is an optional bundled JVM tool (`APIOME_JING_BIN`); the image adds the Maven

### 1.618.0 — 2026-11-03

#### Added
- **Catalog URL connector (RAR-6.1b, #6467).** Catalog items imported with **Document URL** now refresh. A `url`
  connector source (`app.url_connector_source`) is registered with the connector framework, so `url` connectors
  sync through the same engine, run ledger and Refresh history as every other connector.
  - **Two modes.** With a base URL (a specification URL) the connector imports that one document as a catalog item
    and refreshes it. With no base URL it covers every live catalog item of the workspace whose latest revision was
    imported from an `http`/`https` URL (one inventory row per item, linked to it), and a URL import made later
    joins on the next run. Only the workspace's oldest such connector acts; another reports
    `url-workspace-connector-duplicate`.
  - **One conditional GET per item.** `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` from the validators kept on the
    inventory row's `deployment` (with the digest of the content they describe): `304` → unchanged, nothing
    fetched; `200` with new content → a new revision of the item with a change report; the same content → no
    revision; an error, a timeout or more than 25 MB → a failed item. The importer is detected from the document,
    falling back to the item's recorded format.
  - **Baseline.** An item with no import anchor (a backfilled item's first run) is anchored to what its URL
    serves, without a new revision.
  - **SSRF.** Every URL, and every redirect, passes the CDG-1.1 connector rule; a refused URL is reported
    (`url-refused`) and the other items are still checked.
  - A `url` connector takes no scope and no stored credential.
  - V352: one live `url` connector named **Catalog URLs** (no base URL) per tenant that has URL-sourced catalog
    items, with their inventory rows linked and `imported`. Idempotent; a tenant that already has a workspace-mode
    `url` connector or a connector named "Catalog URLs" keeps it.

  per document and passes it to `validate_json_instance` (new optional `registry` argument); the lint of that spec

### 1.610.0 — 2026-11-02

#### Added
- **ASN.1: typedefs, tags, constraints and extension markers normalized, a lint pack and an encoding-aware
  breaking-change classifier (MFI-21.5, #3995).** The parser, import source, emitter, UI card, CLI path and seven
  corpus modules already shipped; this makes the model describe what a module says, and adds what versions, diffs and
  lint need.
  - `asn1_parser` reads each type's and component's tag (`Asn1Tag`: class, number, kind), `SIZE` and value-range
    constraints, named numbers / named bits, integer and boolean `DEFAULT`s (only text ones were kept), the extension
    marker `...` with the extension additions after it (`[[ … ]]` groups flattened; they used to be dropped), inline
    `SEQUENCE` / `SET` / `CHOICE` components, `SET OF`, the module's `IMPORTS` and `EXTENSIBILITY IMPLIED`.
  - `Asn1Normalizer`: `Name ::= INTEGER …`, `Name ::= SEQUENCE OF X` and `Name ::= Other` become ALIAS types (the
    normalizer built `Type(scalar=…)` / `Type(alias_of=…)`, which the canonical model rejects, so any module with such
    a typedef failed to import; corpus `asn1/07` is no longer a known import bug). Constraints map to `minimum` /
    `maximum`, `min_length` / `max_length` and `min_items` / `max_items`; fields record `asn1_type`, `asn1_tag` (kind
    resolved from the module default, explicit on a CHOICE), `asn1_extension` and named numbers; types record
    `asn1_kind` (SET), `asn1_extensible` and their own tag; CHOICE alternatives keep their declared built-in, tag,
    extension flag and constraints. Inline constructed components become `<Type><Component>` types.
  - New `app/asn1_lint.py` (`asn1.*`, registered under `asn1`): `type-resolves`, `choice-tags-distinct`,
    `set-tags-distinct`, `sequence-tags-unambiguous` (error, with blocking-rule metadata and scanner-evaluation
    fixtures); `default-valid`, `any-deprecated` (warning); `legacy-string-type`, `extension-marker` (info).
  - New `app/asn1_breaking.py` (`asn1-encoding`): 27 rules grading components, tags, DEFAULTs, extension additions,
    SEQUENCE order (SET order is safe), value-range / SIZE constraints, ENUMERATED items, CHOICE alternatives,
    extension markers, SEQUENCE ↔ SET and alias targets by how an old BER / DER / PER peer decodes a new value.
  - Version-diff fixtures `tests/fixtures/asn1_versions/subscriber.{v1,v2-compatible,v3-breaking}.asn1`.

#### Fixed
- The ASN.1 emitter writes an ASN.1 item's tags (with their kind, so the `AUTOMATIC TAGS` header cannot change them),

    resolves to its base type; a param's options become an `enum` constraint, `repeating` a list, and `matrix` /

    values, representation media types and elements, and the grammars' sequence elements graded with XML Schema
    semantics — `element-reordered` (relative order changed) is breaking, `element-shifted` (moved only by an

### 1.599.0 — 2026-11-01

#### Added
- **Smithy → canonical model: services, operations, resources, shapes, traits (MFI-17.2, #3809).** The JSON AST mapper
  (`app.smithy_ast_mapper`, used with the Smithy CLI and for an uploaded JSON AST) keeps every trait's value

  `errors`, a service's `resources`, a resource's identifiers / properties / lifecycle / operations / children, and
  each enum member's `@enumValue`; a member targeting a simple shape inherits its `length` / `range` / `pattern` /
  `timestampFormat` / `mediaType`. The normalizer maps them:
  - `@http` → `Operation.http_method` / `http_path` and `extras["http"]` (the binding the OpenAPI projection reads, so
    a JSON-AST model now converts with its routes), the code in `smithy_http_code`;
  - `@httpLabel` / `@httpQuery` / `@httpHeader` input members → path / query / header `Parameter`s (named by the
    trait value);
  - declared and service-wide errors → `ERROR` messages (status from `@httpError`, description from the error's
    documentation); error structures record `smithy_error`, `smithy_http_error`, `smithy_retryable`;
  - `@readonly` / `@idempotent` / `@paginated` / `@deprecated` → `extras` and `Operation.deprecated`;
  - resources → `extras["smithy_resource"]` on the resource type (properties become fields after the identifiers),
    and every operation a resource binds is tagged with it; services record `smithy_errors`, `smithy_resources`,
    `smithy_service_traits`;
  - member `@documentation` / `@default` / `@length` / `@range` / `@pattern` / `@deprecated` → description, default,
    `Constraints` (a list's `@length` → `min_items` / `max_items`) and `deprecated`; other trait values →
    `extras["smithy_trait_values"]`;
  - `@enumValue` → `EnumValue.value` (positions stay where there is none); `intEnum` → `smithy_kind: "intEnum"`.
- **Per-shape AST hashes:** `extras["smithy_shape_hashes"]` maps each absolute shape id to
  `smithy_ast_mapper.shape_sha256` of its JSON AST node (sorted keys); kept out of the version fingerprint

### 1.595.0 — 2026-11-01

#### Added
- **WSDL + XSD parse & import resolution (MFI-13.1, #3788).** New `app/xml_import_graph.py` follows every import of a
  description or schema against a multi-file set — `xs:import` / `xs:include` / `xs:redefine` / `xs:override`, WSDL 1.1
  `wsdl:import`, WSDL 2.0 `wsdl:import` / `wsdl:include` — transitively and cycle-safely. Each location resolves
  **relative to the file that declares it** (`../schemas/orders.xsd` from `wsdl/orders.wsdl`), then as written (live-
  fetch members), then by a file name only one member has; it is never guessed between two same-named files. Unresolved
  and unreadable references are returned, never fatal. `resolve_bundle_path` moved here from
  `app.wsdl_bundle_validation`'s private `_resolve` (same rules).
- **WSDL 2.0 descriptions split across files** now import as one: interfaces (including `extends` across files),
  bindings, endpoints and schemas of every imported or included description are read.
- **XSD filesets stitch their imports**: `XsdImportSource.parse_fileset` passes the set to `parse_xsd(members=…)`, which
  reads the types and elements of every schema reached, merged by local name with the root's declaration winning. A
  single `.xsd` is read alone, as before.
- **Canonical-XML hash.** New `app/xml_canonical_hash.py`: SHA-256 over Canonical XML 2.0 (stdlib
  `ElementTree.canonicalize`: text stripped, comments dropped, prefixes rewritten including in QName-valued attributes)
  of the root and every imported document, in path order — algorithm `sha256-c14n2-v1`. Recorded as
  `extras["xml_c14n_sha256"]` / `xml_c14n_algorithm` and exposed as `FingerprintResult.format_hash` by the new
  `WsdlCanonicalXmlHasher` / `XsdCanonicalXmlHasher`.
- `extras["xml_import_graph"]` lists the documents read (`path`, `kind`) and the references nothing answered
  (`declared_in`, `location`, `reason`) for a description that spans files; `extras["xsd_version"] = "1.1"` for a
  schema marked `vc:minVersion="1.1"` or using an XSD 1.1-only element (`assert`, `assertion`, `alternative`,
  `openContent`, `defaultOpenContent`, `override`). 1.1 constructs are not modeled.

#### Changed
- WS-I import checks (`wsi.unresolved-import`, `wsi.wsdl-import-target`) resolve locations with the same rules as the
  parser, so lint and import agree on a set laid out in folders.
- `xml_c14n_sha256`, `xml_c14n_algorithm` and `xml_import_graph` join `fingerprint.UNHASHED_EXTRAS`: the version
  fingerprint is unchanged, so formatting, a documentation edit or a renamed file mints no version.

### 1.593.0 — 2026-11-01

#### Added
- **OData functions and actions in the canonical model (MFI-11.2, #3777).** An OData import now maps every v4
  `<Function>` / `<Action>` overload (CSDL XML and CSDL JSON) and every v2/v3 `<FunctionImport>` onto a canonical
  operation, in one service named after the entity container. Keys are `(kind, fully-qualified name, ordered parameter
  types)` — `Function Shop.Search(Edm.String,Edm.Int32)` — so overloads stay distinct and a key changes only with the
  signature. A function is `GET` with query parameters (required when `Nullable="false"`); an action is `POST` with its
  parameters on the request message's `extras["odata_parameters"]`; a bound operation routes through an entity set of
  its binding type (`/Products({key})/Shop.Discount`), an unbound one through its container import; a missing return
  type answers `204`. v2/v3 imports take `m:HttpMethod` (else `POST` when side-effecting, else `GET`). New
  `app/odata_operations.py`; the parser gains `ODataOperation` / `ODataOperationParameter` / `ODataOperationImport`,
  read for v4 only, so a v4 document with no operations and every v2/v3 extras record are unchanged.
- **OData export writes an OData source's operations back as themselves.** Kind, binding, `IsComposable`,
  `EntitySetPath`, the ordered signature, the return type, overload lists and the container import (with its
  `EntitySet`) are kept, so an OData → OData export re-imports with the same operation keys; an imported function is
  never folded into an entity set's CRUD. The XML rendering now writes `IsBound`, `IsComposable`, `EntitySetPath`, an
  import's `EntitySet`, and `ReturnType`'s `Nullable` explicitly, so an `output: both` export's two documents describe
  the same return types.

  `GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_slug}/imports` — which reads that store — and any non-owning reader kept showing it

#### CI
- **apiome-openapi polls every second.** The workflow passed `--poll-interval 1000`, but the option is in seconds, so
  the CLI checked the job once, slept for the rest of `--import-timeout 900`, and timed out on an import that had
  finished. It now passes `--poll-interval 1`.

### 1.577.2 — 2026-11-01

#### Fixed
- **The image starts again.** Node 26 (1.577.0) links `libatomic.so.1`, which the `python:3.12-slim` runtime stage did
  not have, so `node` — and with it every Node-backed bundled tool (`asyncapi-parser`, `typescript-types-extract`,
  `zod-extract`, `dbml-validate`, `prisma-validate`) — failed to load (`error while loading shared libraries:
  libatomic.so.1`), the startup toolchain self-check refused to start, and the service exited. The runtime stage now
  installs `libatomic1` and runs `node --version` right after copying node, so a missing shared library fails the
  image build instead of startup. The tools stage installs `libatomic1` explicitly too (it had it only through
  `build-essential`).

### 1.577.1 — 2026-11-01

#### Fixed

  `apiome import openapi`/`swagger`/`auto` with a file) streams the upload to a tempfile and gives the import worker
  its `document_path` (IXH-6.5, #5124). The apiome-ui worker only ever decoded `document_base64`, so every such
  import failed within a second: `Could not parse specification document: The first argument must be of type
  string … Received undefined`, reported as `INTERNAL_WORKER_FAULT`. The worker now reads `document_path` (preferred,
  as `_decode_document_bytes` does) and falls back to `document_base64`; `readPayloadDocument` in
  `apiome-ui/lib/repository-auto-refresh-import.ts`. The worker ships in this image.
- **Upload tempfiles are deleted when the job ends.** The in-process import pipeline removed its own tempfile, but
  the worker path never did; `_drive_job` now deletes `document_path` on every exit path.

### 1.574.0 — 2026-10-31

#### Added
- **DBML and Prisma outputs for the SQL DDL export (MFX-35.2, #4312).** New `output` option on `sql-ddl`: `ddl`
  (default), `dbml` (`<Name>.dbml`) or `prisma` (`schema.prisma`). It is one projection with three serializers:
  `_SqlDdlWriter.project()` builds the tables, and `render()` hands them to the SQL writer or to the new
  `app.sql_ddl_serializers` (`render_dbml`, `render_prisma`).
  - DBML: `Table`, an `Enum` per enum type (every dialect), `pk` / `increment` / `not null` / `unique` / `default` /
    `check` settings, `indexes` for composite keys, a `checks` block, and a `Ref` per foreign key.
  - Prisma: a PascalCase `model` per table with `@@map` back to it, Prisma scalars with `@db.*` native types, `@id` /
    `@@id`, `@unique` / `@@unique`, `@default` (with `autoincrement()` and `dbgenerated()`), an `enum` per enum type
    (`@map` for labels that are not identifiers), and both sides of each foreign key as a named `@relation`.
    - Every model gets a key (keys are planned as with `nested=tables`).
    - Options rejected: `output=prisma` with `dialect=ansi`, and `schema_name` outside PostgreSQL.
  - What a language cannot hold is a loss (`schema-language-dropped` → DROP, `schema-language-approximated` →
    APPROX): Prisma's missing `CHECK`, interval and nullable list; a foreign key Prisma cannot relate; a backtick in
    a DBML expression.
  - DBML gives a record with no fields a generated key (DBML has no empty table).
- **Validation.** The `sql-ddl` export gate parses `.dbml` with `@dbml/core` (`dbml.parse`) and runs `prisma validate`
  on `schema.prisma` (`prisma.validate`), through the new `app.db_schema_validation`. A runtime without the tools
  reports the check as skipped.
- **Toolchain.** New hard dependencies `dbml-validator` (`@dbml/core` 10.3.1, `toolchain/dbml-validate.mjs`) and
  `prisma-validator` (`prisma` 7.10.1, `toolchain/prisma-validate.mjs`): `toolchain/package.json`, `BUNDLED_TOOLS`,
  `REQUIRED_TOOL_KEYS`, the Dockerfile (copy, shims, build smoke test), `scripts/install_dev_toolchain.sh` and the
  CI installs. They add about 250 MB to the image.
- Tests: `tests/test_sql_ddl_serializers.py`.
  - Goldens: `tests/fixtures/sql_ddl_output/shop-*.dbml|prisma`.
  - Every corpus source passes `@dbml/core` and `prisma validate` (PostgreSQL + tables + schema, MySQL + JSON).
  - The export gate, the tool wrappers, and the option rules.

#### Fixed
- SQL DDL projection on MySQL (found by `prisma validate`, and invalid in MySQL itself):
  - a `TEXT` column in a primary or unique key is written `VARCHAR(255)` (MySQL cannot index `TEXT`);
  - a generated key beside a declared composite primary key is `UNIQUE`, so `AUTO_INCREMENT` is indexed and
    foreign keys can reference it.
- OpenAPI 1.438.0.

### 1.573.0 — 2026-10-31

#### Added
- **SQL DDL emitter (MFX-35.1, #4311).** New `app.sql_ddl_emitter` (key / format `sql-ddl`, the SQL DDL importer's
  key) writes a relational projection of the model's types as one script.
  - Every record type becomes a table and scalar fields become typed columns: `nullable=False` → `NOT NULL`;
    constraints → `CHECK`; `maxLength` → `VARCHAR(n)`; enums → `CREATE TYPE … AS ENUM` (PostgreSQL), inline `ENUM`
    (MySQL) or `CHECK … IN` (ANSI).
  - Nested objects, unions and maps become JSON columns (`nested=json`, default), or foreign keys plus junction and
    child tables (`nested=tables`, keys declared, inferred from a required `id`, or synthesized).
  - Identifiers are mangled deterministically (snake_case, prefixed, hash-capped, deduplicated, reserved words
    quoted).
  - Options: `dialect` (`postgres` / `mysql` / `ansi`), `nested`, `schema_name`.
  - An imported SQL item keeps its keys and foreign keys, and in its own dialect its column types, defaults and
    checks.
  - Every script is parsed with **sqlglot** in its dialect inside `emit()`. The export gate (`sql-ddl` in
    `export_validation`) reads it back through the SQL DDL reader.
  - `SqlDdlFidelityRulePack` reports projection decisions (keys, junction/child tables, renames, precision) as
    `SYNTH`. Renames are DROP under the old key and SYNTH under the re-import key; JSON columns and dialect
    approximations are `APPROX`; dropped constraints and dialect clauses are `DROP`.
- New dependency: `sqlglot==30.23.0` (pyproject, requirements.txt).
- Tests: `tests/test_sql_ddl_emitter.py`.
  - Goldens: `tests/fixtures/sql_ddl_output/`, regenerate with `APIOME_REGEN_SQL_DDL_OUTPUT=1`.
  - Every corpus source parses in all 3 dialects × 2 modes.
  - Every PostgreSQL script is applied to the local database in a rolled-back transaction.
- Registry fallout:
  - format counts, supported formats, version coverage (writes PostgreSQL / MySQL / ANSI DDL);
  - RC6 target list, target-tier table;
  - round-trip matrix: 108 cells, 89 pass, 19 xfail;
  - export conformance column (92 lossy, 16 refused, no silent loss);
  - corpus parity report.
- OpenAPI 1.437.0.

#### Changed
- **OMG IDL fidelity pack: profile-dependent losses (MFX-28.2, #4169).** `CorbaIdlFidelityRulePack` lays the model out
  with the IDL writer for the export's `profile` (`apply_options`) and reports:
  - constraints: a string `max_length` is written `string<N>` and a list `max_items` `sequence<T, N>` (represented,
    nothing reported); every other constraint is a `// constraints: …` comment above the member, union case,
    typedef or operation (`APPROX`, writer loss `constraints-as-comment`);
  - HTTP semantics: under `corba` the operation is an `APPROX` and its method / path / status codes / parameter
    locations a `DROP` (`http-binding-dropped`); under `dds` every operation is a `DROP` (no interfaces);
  - event channels: under `dds` a DDS topic — its payload type is declared and `// DDS topic "<address>": <type>`

    pointer); event operations `DROP` under both;

    (`SYNTH`).

  unions, `@optional`) and IDL has no field ids — the pack no longer reports unions dropped, non-null fields
  "becoming optional", or synthesized field ids; a source's field numbers are reported dropped.

  bounds (`max_items`); the parser accepts a bounded string member.

### 1.564.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Changed
- **Thrift fidelity pack: every loss enumerated (MFX-25.3, #4153).** `ThriftFidelityRulePack` lays the model out with
  the Thrift writer and reports, on the construct each concerns:
  - constraints (pattern, bounds, lengths, format) as an `APPROX` "written as a comment, not enforced" — and the
    writer now **writes** them: a `// constraints: …` line (`app.constraint_text.constraint_comment`) above each
    struct field, request-struct parameter and typedef (writer loss `constraints-as-comment`);

  - an HTTP operation: the RPC method (`APPROX`) **and** a `DROP` of its method, path, status codes and parameter
    locations (`http-binding-dropped`);
  - event operations and channels as `DROP` (the writer skipped them without a loss; now `event-operation-dropped`,

    key a re-import gives back — a renamed type / service / method (`<service>.<method>`), the `<Method>Request`

### 1.559.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **OpenAPI Overlay 1.1 and 1.2, and an `overlay` rule pack (GVM-4.1, #5876).** `app.openapi_overlay` applies each
  overlay with the semantics of the revision its marker declares, from the declared table `OVERLAY_READ_VERSIONS`
  (1.0, 1.1, 1.2; `major.minor`, patch ignored): 1.1 adds `copy` (exactly one source node, merged like `update`;
  `remove` > `copy` > `update`), primitive targets, array concatenation (at an array target and inside an object
  merge), refusal of incompatible merges before anything is written, and the all-objects/all-arrays/all-primitives
  rule for multiple matches; 1.2 adds reusable actions (`components.actions` + `$ref` references) and `$self`, and
  refuses an action with both `update` and `copy`. `extends` is checked against the fileset's base (relative path, or
  the base's `$self`). A marker outside the table (`1.3.0`) is refused with `FORMAT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` naming the
  supported revisions. Semantics, including the 1.0 primitive-target leniency, are recorded in `docs/overlay.md`.
  The IXH-7.7 intake rules `intake.overlay-unmatched-target` / `intake.overlay-action-invalid` are promoted to the
  registered `overlay` pack (`app.overlay_lint_rules`): `overlay.unmatched-target`, `overlay.action-invalid`,
  `overlay.target-expression-invalid`, `overlay.extends-unresolved` (warnings) and `overlay.version-unsupported`

  service); resource types name the profile they conform to. Before, a CapabilityStatement was read as an inferred
  resource instance. Every FHIR model now records the `fhirVersion` it targets and its release (`fhir_version` /
  `fhir_release` extras: R4, R4B, R5, R6 incl. ballots), which the fingerprint hashes, so a profile moving from R4 to R5
  is a new version with a change report; the keys are written only when declared, so profiles imported before keep
  their fingerprint. **Live discovery:** `FhirImportSource.discover(base_url)` reads `<base>/metadata` over the
  SSRF-guarded live-fetch client, and `fhir` is a catalog **Live refresh** adapter (`CatalogRefreshUpdate.adapter`).
  **Lint:** new `fhir` rule pack (`app.fhir_lint`) — `fhir.profile-status`, `-url`, `-version`, `-base`,
  `fhir.element-short`, `fhir.capability-version`, `-profile`, `-search`. Declared read versions: R4, R5, R6
  (partial; ballot). Fixtures `fhir/07`–`10` (an R5 server, an R6-ballot server, one profile in R4 and R5). OpenAPI
  1.420.0 (field descriptions only).

### 1.555.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **Webhook-instant refresh (RAR-6.3, #3540).** A verified push on a tracked branch whose delivery lists the files
  its commits touched (GitHub and GitLab `commits[].added/modified/removed`) now refreshes the tracked files among them
  right away, instead of waiting for the next sweep tick. The webhook route answers the provider first, then runs
  `app.repository_webhook_refresh.refresh_pushed_files` as a background task: it rescans the pushed branch and
  enqueues spec-faithful refresh jobs through the sweep's `enqueue_stale_files_for_branch`, limited to those paths
  (`path_filter` now also takes a set), so the freshness comparator, the tenant polling quota, the per-repository
  refresh lock, `APIOME_REFRESH_ENABLED`, the per-repository opt-out and the auto-pause all still apply, and the
  EPIC-4 executor's divergence guard still runs. A completed refresh with nothing deferred advances the cadence anchor;
  anything else leaves the repository due (the REPO-4.3 behaviour), so the sweep is the fallback, as it is for a
  Bitbucket push, a force push or a truncated commit list (`ParsedWebhookEvent.changed_paths` is `None`). New
  `Database.list_repository_import_spec_paths`; workflow-audit action `repository.webhook.instant_refresh`; the accepted
  audit row gains `instantRefreshFiles`. The receipt body is unchanged. OpenAPI 1.419.0 (version only).
- **Refresh URL-sourced imports (RAR-6.1, #3538).** A spec imported into a project from a URL now keeps following
  it. New `apiome.url_import_specs` (apiome-db V340) records each URL lineage: the stored import spec (source kind,
  descriptor, verbatim options), the `ETag` / `Last-Modified` and SHA-256 REST saw at import time, the version the
  import produced and a checksum of its rendered OpenAPI. A sweep on the refresh floor (`app.url_import_refresh_sweep`)
  sends a conditional GET (`If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since`, SSRF-guarded): 304 skips; a 200 goes through the
  RAR-2.2 newer-than comparator on `Last-Modified` and the checksum (same content or an older `Last-Modified`
  skips); a version edited in Apiome since its import holds the refresh (RAR-4.4); otherwise the stored spec is
  replayed onto the project through the spec-import engine (`repository_auto_import`, RAR-4.1) as a new
  date/time-labelled version, and the fetched validators become the anchors once that import completes. Failures
  back off exponentially; `APIOME_REFRESH_ENABLED` stops it with the repository sweep. Imports fetched with
  credentials are recorded as `authenticated` and never refreshed; no credential is stored. New routes:
  `POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_slug}/url-imports` (`imports:create`; REST fetches the URL once for the anchors),
  `GET …/url-imports` (`imports:view`, optional `projectId`), `PATCH …/url-imports/{id}` (`imports:edit`:
  `autoRefreshEnabled`, `refreshIntervalSeconds`, `useDefaultInterval`). OpenAPI 1.419.0.

### 1.554.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **Reconcile one-shot file uploads (RAR-6.2, #3539).** A catalog item imported from an uploaded file has no live
  source to refresh, so the import pipeline now records the spec it ran with on the revision's
  `format_metadata.importSpec` (`{specSchemaVersion, sourceKind, options}`, the user's `SpecImportOptions` minus the
  run-only `dry_run`, `skip_duplicate_versions`, `input_kind` and `git_source`) for every `file` / `fileset` upload. New
  `GET /v1/catalog/{tenant}/{item}/upload` says whether the item's newest version is an upload, its age, and whether it
  is `stale` (at least the tenant's `staleAfterDays` old); `POST /v1/catalog/{tenant}/{item}/reupload` (`imports:create`
  and `projects:edit`; body `{filename, documentBase64}`) replays the stored importer and options over the new file
  through the import pipeline and the tenant's import quality gate: an identical file answers `unchanged` and writes
  nothing, a changed one adds a date/time-labelled version with a change report. An upload from before capture replays
  the recorded source format with default options (`specReplayed: false`). `GET` / `PUT
  /v1/catalog/{tenant}/upload-policy` (`imports:edit` to change) read and set `staleAfterDays` (1–3650, default 90),
  stored in the new `apiome.tenants.catalog_upload_stale_after_days` column (migration V339). New
  `app.catalog_upload_reconcile` and `app.catalog_upload_routes`. OpenAPI 1.418.0.

### 1.553.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **Catalog drift email (MFI-31.3a, #6384).** With the tenant's `emailEnabled` drift setting on and a mailer
  configured, drift is emailed to the item's confirmed owner team members (owner routing's recipients, minus the
  refresh's actor; enabled, undeleted accounts with an address) beside the webhook: one email per announced event for
  `immediate` delivery, and one email per recipient per daily digest listing only the items their team owns. An
  unowned item and a **Check now** version are never emailed. New `app.mailer` (SendGrid v3, configured like
  apiome-ui: `SENDGRID_API_KEY` / `EMAIL_FROM`; a no-op when either is unset; never raises, never logs the key or a
  body) and `app.catalog_drift_email`. Links use `APIOME_UI_PUBLIC_URL`. `docker-compose.yml` passes both variables
  through to `rest`.

#### Changed

### 1.552.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **Postman → OpenAPI through the import SPI (MFI-32.7, #4409).** New `POST /v1/import/{tenant_slug}/postman/openapi`
  (requires `imports:create`, stores nothing) reads a Postman Collection v2.0/v2.1 with the registered Postman import
  adapter and returns `{source_kind, openapi, warnings}`: an OpenAPI 3.1 document emitted from the canonical model,
  and one warning per declared limit. `base_url` replaces the servers; `info.version` defaults to `1.0.0`. The web
  app's **Postman Collection** import card now calls it instead of converting in the browser.

#### Changed
- **Postman collections normalize on the shared inferred-spec engine (MFI-32.7, #4409).** `PostmanNormalizer` hands
  every request (and saved example response) to `infer_canonical_api` and post-processes with the MFI-32.5 collection
  helpers, like Insomnia and Bruno: requests sharing a method and templated path become one operation with widened
  schemas, headers become header parameters, folders tag operations, whole-variable query/header values become
  parameter defaults, and types take the engine's names (`PostOrderRequest`, `GetOrderResponse200` …). The Postman
  projection the emitter reads (`postman_folder_path`, `postman_headers`, `postman_auth`, `postman_body_*`,
  `postman_sample`, document `postman_*` extras) is still written, so export and round trip keep working. Declared
  limits (`postman.script`, `postman.auth_credential`, `postman.secret_variable`, `postman.body_mode`,
  `postman.merged_request`) reach the coverage ledger. Corpus, roundtrip and MCP toolset goldens regenerated; 13
  round-trip cells that used to fail now pass.

#### Fixed
- **Postman `api.raw` scrubbing.** The stored collection text was JSON-encoded before the secret-scrub gate ran,
  which escaped its quotes and hid `"key": "value"` credentials from the gate; it is now scrubbed as text.

  `existing_version_labels`: every live version label of the target project, oldest first (new
  `Database.list_version_labels_for_project`). The import wizard's Changes step uses it to tell whether the import's

### 1.550.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto fidelity packs (MFX-30.3, #4180).** Both packs build the schema with the
  emitter's writer and file each writer loss on its construct beside the capability verdicts (new shared
  `writer_loss_rulepack.filed_writer_verdicts(api, losses, rules)`), so the report matches the export:
  - FlatBuffers: operations/channels a critical DROP plus the root types-only advisory; constraints APPROX;
    maps APPROX (`<Map>Entry` key/value vectors); synthesized field ids SYNTH (new `synthesized-field-id`
    loss; a `.fbs` source keeps its own); wrapper tables SYNTH; renames, aliases and structs-as-tables
    APPROX (info); unsupported defaults and value-less fields DROP.
  - Cap'n Proto: an operation of a non-`.capnp` source APPROX as an interface method (new
    `operation-as-method` loss); error responses DROP; constraints APPROX; maps APPROX; synthesized
    ordinals and file id SYNTH.
- **Constraints written as comments.** New `app.constraint_text` renders constraints as one line
  (`constraints: >= 1; max length 40`; width formats such as `int32` omitted). The FlatBuffers (`//`) and
  Cap'n Proto (`#`) emitters write it above each constrained field (`constraints-as-comment`); with
  `include_comments: false` it is left out and recorded as `constraints-dropped`.

#### Changed
- Both packs no longer emit the generic "constraints → doc comment" APPROX or "synthesized field number"
  SYNTH capability verdicts; the writer's own losses replace them.
- **Compile findings.** A `flatc` / `capnp` error in the export gate is now one finding per compiler line with
  the emitted file, line and column and the rule (`flatc.compile`, `capnp.compile`).
- Goldens: flatbuffers and capnproto cells of the round-trip and conformance matrices; three Cap'n Proto
  silent-loss pairs (arazzo, flatbuffers, wadl) are now reported and left the ledger.

### 1.549.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added

  `run_cb2xml(text)` parses a copybook with cb2xml through the toolchain runner (its `*** fatal parse error ***`
  comes on stderr with exit code 0, so the error text decides; SableCC's `[line,column]` is kept);

  renders, for the check.

#### Changed

  available, rejects with cb2xml's error or each layout difference from the plan built with those options; without

#### Added
- **API Blueprint validate + round-trip (MFX-18.3, #3907).** New `app.apiblueprint_roundtrip`:
  - `validate_emitted_apiblueprint(emit_result)` parses every file with drafter when the toolchain is present; a good
    blueprint has **zero warnings**, so every `error` and `warning` annotation is a problem (`BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`).
    Without drafter (or when it goes missing mid-run) the built-in reader parses it. A drafter that is installed but
    gives no answer (timeout, no parse result) is a problem, not a pass.
  - `round_trip_apiblueprint(api, *, emit_result)` validates, re-imports through `ApiblueprintImportSource`, takes the
    canonical diff against the source and reconciles it with the fidelity report; `status` is `invalid` /
    `unparseable` / `lossy` / `lossless`, with `unexplained`, `overclaims`, `explained` and `diverges`.
  - `reimport_with_reader(emit_result)` — the gate's re-import (malformed shapes become `INPUT_MALFORMED`).
- `apiblueprint_drafter.run_drafter(text, *, strict=False)` — `strict=True` raises (`ToolchainError` / `ValueError`)
  instead of returning `[]` when drafter gave no answer; the import keeps the best-effort default.
- **Round-trip fixture.** `tests/fixtures/apiblueprint_roundtrip/openapi-petstore.json` (`APIOME_REGEN_APIB_ROUNDTRIP=1`
  regenerates it); drafter paths replay the recorded drafter 4.0.0 output.

#### Changed
- **Export gate.** The `apiblueprint` validator now rejects drafter **warnings** as well as errors (they passed
  before), rejects a drafter that fails to run, and rejects a document that does not import again
  (`apiblueprint.reimport`).

### 1.538.0 — 2026-10-30

- **RAML validate + round-trip (MFX-17.3, #3903).** New `app.raml_roundtrip`:
  - `validate_emitted_raml(emit_result)` validates with AMF's RAML 1.0 profile when the toolchain is present
    (`Violation` results only; warnings pass) and falls back to the RAML reader without it (or when AMF goes
    missing mid-run); returns `(validator, violations)`.

    `overclaims`, `valid`, `explained` and `diverges`.
  - `reimport_with_reader(emit_result)` re-imports through the pure-Python reader (malformed shapes become
    `ImportSourceError` `INPUT_MALFORMED`).
- **Export gate.** The `raml` validator now uses these helpers and also rejects a document that does not import again
  (finding keyword `raml.reimport`). An AMF failure other than unavailability rejects with its message.
- **Round-trip fixture.** `tests/fixtures/raml_roundtrip/openapi-petstore.json` pins the measured OpenAPI-petstore
  round trip (`APIOME_REGEN_RAML_ROUNDTRIP=1` regenerates it); AMF paths replay the recorded `amf` 5.7.1 reports.

### 1.536.0 — 2026-10-30

#### Added
- **WSDL bundle packaging + validation (MFX-14.3, #3891).** The `wsdl` target now has an emitted-artifact
  validator (`app.wsdl_bundle_validation.validate_wsdl_bundle`, wired as `export_validation._validate_wsdl`), so a
  broken WSDL + XSD bundle fails the export job instead of being delivered. Checks, in order:
  - `wsdl.bundle-root` — exactly one WSDL description; `wsdl.xml` — every member is safe, well-formed XML;
  - `wsdl.bundle-reference` — every `wsdl:import`, `xs:import` / `xs:include` / `xs:redefine` location resolves,
    relative to its member, to a file in the zip (URLs, absolute paths and `..` escapes fail);
  - `wsi.*` — the WS-I Basic Profile checks (`app.wsdl_wsi.check_wsi`). For a WSDL source, rules the source
    already broke (`extras["wsdl_wsi_issues"]`, `inherited_wsi_rules`) are inherited and not reported;
  - `wsdl.structure` — the unpacked bundle (private temp folder, `allow="sandbox"`) is read by `xmlschema`'s
    `Wsdl11Document`: WSDL 1.1 schema validation, every XSD built, every message / part / port type / binding /
    port reference resolved. Descriptions with SOAP 1.2 or HTTP bindings are read with the SOAP 1.1 model off;
  - `wsdl.reimport` — the bundle re-imports through `WsdlImportSource.parse_fileset`.
  Findings carry `file`, `path` and the rule as `keyword`.

#### Fixed
- **WSDL emitter bindings.** A WSDL-sourced one-way (or notification) operation's binding lists only the
  directions its port type operation has (it wrote an `output` that named no message), and an rpc-style
  `soap:body` carries `namespace` = the target namespace (WS-I R2717).

### 1.535.0 — 2026-10-30

### 1.532.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **COBOL copybook emitter (MFX-23.1, #4139).** The `cobolcopybook` export now writes a copybook for **any** source
  (it was source-bound: only a copybook import could be exported). A copybook item is still re-emitted from its own
  layout; any other model is laid out by the new `app.cobolcopybook_plan` (shared with the PL/I mode, MFX-23.3):
  - one `01` record per top-level record type, nested objects inlined as group items, levels `05`/`10`/…
    (a smaller step past 9 levels), recursion cut (recorded), a model with no record refused (422);
  - deterministic, collision-safe COBOL data names (upper case, hyphens, ≤ 30 characters, reserved words get
    `-X`, copybook-wide unique with `-2`, `-3` …);
  - `PIC X(n)` (maxLength / ISO date, time, timestamp, UUID layouts / default length), `S9(4)` / `S9(9)` /
    `S9(18)` `COMP`, decimals `S9(p)V9(s) COMP-3` (scale from `multipleOf`), floats `COMP-1` / `COMP-2`, booleans
    as `PIC X` with `88` TRUE / FALSE, enums with one `88` per value, lists as fixed `OCCURS n TIMES` or
    `OCCURS … DEPENDING ON` a synthesized `<NAME>-COUNT`, unions as `REDEFINES` (largest first); maps dropped;
  - options `numeric_usage` (`comp` | `display`), `default_string_length`, `default_occurs`, `decimal_scale` and
    `fixed_format` (free format when false). Every synthesis is recorded as an emit loss; the root of the report
    notes a document of another format (the full pack is MFX-23.2).
- Rendering fixes: a fixed table is written `OCCURS n TIMES` (was `OCCURS n TO n TIMES`, legal only with
  DEPENDING ON); numeric `88` values are unquoted and a quote in a text value is doubled; deeply nested entries
  stay within column 72.
- **Copybook parser:** the PICTURE string is the one token after `PIC` (it used to run to the end of the entry,
  swallowing a following `OCCURS` clause), and USAGE is read anywhere in the entry, including a `COMP-1` / `COMP-2`
  item with no PICTURE (imported as `float` / `double`). Every corpus example parses unchanged.
- Goldens: the `cobolcopybook` cells of both matrices — 91 refused cells now export (`lossy`), silent loss
  unchanged; the 107 `→ cobolcopybook` round-trip xfail reasons now name the actual difference.

### 1.531.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **FlatBuffers schema emitter (MFX-30.1, #4178).** The `flatbuffers` export is rebuilt to write one `.fbs` that
  `flatc` compiles, for any source: records → `table` (a source `struct` stays one when every field fits), enums with
  an underlying integer type and ascending values (and a valid default when `0` is not a value), unions, vectors,
  maps → vectors of `<Map>Entry` tables with a `(key)` field, wrapper tables for vectors of vectors / unions and for
  union members that are not tables, aliases inlined, FlatBuffers identifiers (`order-id` → `order_id`, keywords

  sources get contiguous ids from 0 (a union takes two: `<name>_type` at N-1) from
  `app.flatbuffers_identity.FieldIdAllocator`, persisted in the MFX-12.2 store under the new `flatbuffers` target

  `(deprecated)` placeholder.

  were previously dropped — and qualified type names; the normalizer skips deprecated slots (kept in
  `extras.fbs_deprecated`) and keeps ids that differ from their position in `extras.fbs_id`.

  and `app/flatbuffers_compile.py`; the export validator compiles FlatBuffers exports with
