### 1.530.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **ASN.1 fidelity pack (MFX-27.2, #4164).** `Asn1FidelityRulePack` now reports:
  - **constraints** — `OK` for each rule the module writes exactly as subtype notation, with the notation as the
    mapping (`minLength/maxLength → SIZE`, `minimum/maximum → value range`, `minItems/maxItems → SEQUENCE (SIZE) OF`,
    `enum → value set`); the ASN.1 capability profile now declares `constraints=True`, so constrained fields are no
    longer reported `constraints → doc comment`;
  - **patterns** — an anchored one-class pattern (`^[A-Z0-9_]{3,8}$`, `^\d{4}$`, `\w`) is written as a permitted
    alphabet `(FROM (…))` narrowing `SIZE` (info `APPROX`, `pattern-as-alphabet`; `asn1tools` checks it); any other
    pattern is written as a `-- pattern:` comment (`DROP`, `pattern-as-comment`). This replaces the MFX-27.1
    `(PATTERN "…")`, which wrote an ECMAScript regex into X.680's own dialect (`app.asn1_notation.pattern_alphabet`);
  - **types-only** — the critical root advisory with counts beside each critical operation / channel `DROP` (the
    writer's `services-dropped` loss carries the same text);
  - **names** — a respelled name is `SYNTH` (was `APPROX`); maps stay `APPROX` (`map-as-sequence`); recursive types
    are `OK`.
- Goldens: the `asn1` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices (`asn1 → asn1` is now `ok`: no loss).

### 1.529.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **ASN.1 emitter (MFX-27.1, #4163).** The `asn1` export is rebuilt to write one X.680 module that compiles under
  `asn1tools` for any source: records → `SEQUENCE`, unions → `CHOICE`, enums → `ENUMERATED` (numbered only when every
  value is a distinct integer), lists → `SEQUENCE OF`, maps → `SEQUENCE OF SEQUENCE { key, value }`; scalars →
  `UTF8String`, `INTEGER` (sized integers keep their width as a value range), `REAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `NULL`,
  `OCTET STRING`, `GeneralizedTime` / `DATE` / `TIME-OF-DAY`; ASN.1 built-ins (`OBJECT IDENTIFIER`, `PrintableString`
  …) pass through. A field is `DEFAULT <value>` or `OPTIONAL`, never both (the old writer wrote both).
- **Constraints as subtype notation:** `minLength` / `maxLength` → `SIZE`, `minItems` / `maxItems` → `SEQUENCE (SIZE)
  OF`, bounds → value ranges intersected with the integer's width (exclusive integer bounds exact), integer `enum` →
  value set, `pattern` → `PATTERN`. What has no notation (`multipleOf`, `uniqueItems`, string `enum`, non-time
  formats, unspellable defaults) is recorded (`constraint-dropped`, `default-dropped`).
- **Names** follow X.680 (`order_id` → `order-id`, `OPEN` → `open`, reserved words get `-Type`, collisions
  `-2`) — `app/asn1_notation.py`. New options `module_name` and `oid` (dotted or brace form); the module name
  defaults to the imported name, then a namespace that is already a module reference (so re-imported keys match),
  then the item name. `automatic_tags: false` now writes the imported `<X> TAGS` clause correctly.
- `Asn1FidelityRulePack` builds the module and files the writer's losses on their constructs (`name-respelled`,
  `pattern-dialect`, `description-as-comment`, `map-as-sequence`, `unmapped-scalar`, `exclusive-bound-inclusive`,
  `empty-enum` / `empty-choice` APPROX; `constraint-dropped`, `default-dropped`, `description-dropped` DROP), plus a
  root note for a document of another format and for keys re-namespaced under the module. Finer verdicts stay with
  MFX-27.2.
- Goldens: the `asn1` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices. `asn1 → asn1` now passes (xfail
  removed); 14 `→ asn1` cells that only read `ok` because the module could not be re-imported are now `lossy`; the
  `nacha → asn1` silent-loss ledger entry is gone.

### 1.528.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Added
- **JSON Type Definition output mode (MFX-21.3, #4128).** The `json-schema` export takes `mode: "jtd"` and writes one
  RFC 8927 document, `<Item>.jtd.json`, from the same canonical projection (`jsonschema_jtd.jtd_from_bundle`):
  `$defs` → `definitions` and a root `ref`; records → `properties` / `optionalProperties`; maps → `values`; arrays →
  `elements`; string enums → `enum`; `int32`, `float32` / `float64`, `boolean`, `string`, `date-time` → `timestamp`;
  `description` → `metadata.description` (the only `metadata` key ajv's strict mode accepts). `mode: "jtd"` rejects
  `draft`, `packaging` and `id_base`; a JSON Schema item is always rebuilt, never re-emitted.
- Expressiveness losses, recorded with their JSON Pointer and filed by `JsonSchemaFidelityRulePack` on their type or
  field when the report is computed for `mode: "jtd"`: `jtd-keyword-dropped` (DROP warn: `pattern`, bounds,
  `multipleOf`, lengths, item counts, `uniqueItems`, formats other than `date-time`, `contentEncoding`),

  and multi-type values written `{}`), `jtd-integer-as-float` (APPROX warn: non-`int32` integers as `float64`),
  `jtd-enum-as-type` (APPROX warn) and `jtd-closed-records` (APPROX info, root). The root note reads
  `document → JSON Type Definition` and renamed types map to `definitions/<key>`; format notes are not raised.
- `jsonschema_jtd.check_jtd_schema` checks RFC 8927 §2.2 schema rules; `validate_jsonschema_document` (and so the
  export validation gate) applies it to JTD output. Tests compile the output with ajv's JTD validator when Node is
  available.

### 1.526.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **JSON Schema emitter (MFX-21.1, #4126).** The `json-schema` export rebuilds a valid standalone JSON Schema from any
  typed source instead of writing canonical scalar names into `type` (`{"type": "i32"}`). The body comes from the

### 1.525.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **XSD fidelity pack (MFX-22.2, #4133).** `XsdFidelityRulePack` is now a `WriterLossRulePack`: it builds the export
  with the XSD writer and turns each recorded loss into a verdict on its construct, so the report predicts exactly what
  the export does. Rules: operations / channels → DROP, and an operation-bearing source carries a root **types-only
  advisory** (`types-only`, counting the operations and channels left out); a free-form map (untyped

  child elements APPROX (`union-as-choice`), a union with no alternatives → DROP (`union-dropped`); a nullable value →
  `nillable` + optional, info APPROX (`null-as-nillable`); examples → `xs:documentation source="example"`, info APPROX
  (`example-as-annotation`); a non-XSD source's properties → child elements, info SYNTH (`property → child element`).
- Shared XSD writer: a `standalone` mode (used by the XSD export only — WSDL / WADL output is unchanged) writes untyped
  maps as `xs:any`, writes field examples (`extras` `examples` / `odcs_examples` / `pydantic_examples`) as
  annotations, and records the approximations above.

  (`app.xsd_schema`) that WSDL (MFX-14.1) and WADL use, so the three write the same types: `complexType` + `sequence`
  and a global element per record, `oneOf` → `xs:choice`, nullable → `nillable="true" minOccurs="0"`, lists →
  `maxOccurs="unbounded"`, constraints → facets (`pattern`, `minLength` / `maxLength`, `minInclusive` /
  `maxInclusive` …), enums → `xs:enumeration`, descriptions → `xs:annotation`.
- New option `xsd_version` (`1.0` default, `1.1`): XSD 1.1 marks the schema `vc:minVersion="1.1"` and writes
  `multipleOf` as an `xs:assertion` facet.
- The `targetNamespace` is the source's namespace (none → a no-namespace schema). A type in a different URI namespace
  is written in its own document; a multi-namespace source exports one `.xsd` per namespace joined by `xs:import`
  (a zip).
- Shared writer: an XSD source's `xs:attribute` fields are written back as attributes, its enums keep their base and
  values, and a list field keeps its item type (also in WSDL / WADL exports of XSD sources). The XSD fidelity pack
  carries unions and constraints and reports renames, maps and unwritable facets like WSDL's.
- Goldens: the `xsd` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.523.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **FHIR fidelity pack: per-construct losses (MFX-26.2, #4158).** Operations: APPROX into the CapabilityStatement
  (DROP without it), and an operation-bearing source warns at the root (`operations-summarized` /
  `operations-dropped`). Unions: a union of distinct single alternatives (primitives, models, at most one enum; not
  used as a list) is written as a FHIR choice element `field[x]` (APPROX `union-as-choice-type`; standalone as a
  model with `value[x]`); any other union is DROP `union-dropped` (a model of optional elements with an exactly-one
  invariant). Maps: DROP — the type and every element typed by it are no longer written as key / value entries.
  Regex / format: a pattern, or an `email` / `hostname` / `ipv4` / `ipv6` format, is a FHIRPath `matches()`
  constraint reported APPROX `regex-as-fhirpath`; other formats DROP. Recursive types: APPROX `recursive-type` with a
  depth note. Naming: a sanitized name is SYNTH.
- The FHIR reader reads choice elements back as unions; the explicit type name of nested and choice elements is
  re-derived on export, so FHIR → FHIR round-trips unchanged.
- Goldens: the `fhir` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.522.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Added
- **FHIR StructureDefinition emitter: R4 / R5 logical models (MFX-26.1, #4157).** The `fhir` writer now writes every
  type as a StructureDefinition logical model (`kind: logical`, `derivation: specialization`, base `Element` (R4) /
  `Base` (R5)), in a `collection` Bundle or one file per resource (option `packaging`), for R4 or R5 (option
  `fhir_version`). Element paths from nesting (a record used by one field is a `BackboneElement` with the
  `explicit-type-name` extension; others are referenced by canonical URL, base option `canonical_base`);
  cardinality from nullability, lists and `minItems` / `maxItems`; FHIR primitives via `fhir_primitive`
  (`integer64` in R5, reported in R4); enums as CodeSystem + ValueSet with a `required` binding; constraints as
  `maxLength`, `minValue[x]` / `maxValue[x]`, `defaultValue[x]` and FHIRPath `constraint`s (pattern, minLength,
  exclusive bounds, multipleOf, allowed values); unions as choice models with an exactly-one invariant, maps as
  repeating key / value entries. Option `capability_statement` (default on) summarizes REST operations, title,
  description and version in a CapabilityStatement. A FHIR profile / resource source is written back in its own
  form. `FhirFidelityRulePack` predicts the writer's losses.
- The FHIR reader reads a logical-model Bundle (or one logical StructureDefinition) back: records (nested
  BackboneElements by their explicit type name), enums from CodeSystems / ValueSet bindings, title / version from
  the CapabilityStatement (`app.fhir_logical`).
- Toolchain tool `fhir-validator` (HL7 `validator_cli` 6.10.4, JVM, `APIOME_FHIR_VALIDATOR_BIN`) installed in the
  image with the R4 and R5 core packages cached at build time; export validation runs it (`-tx n/a`) and reports
  each error, falling back to Apiome's structural FHIR rules (`app.fhir_validation`).
- Version coverage: FHIR writes R5.

### 1.521.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **OData fidelity pack: keyless types, RPC / event DROP, type coercion (MFX-16.2, #3898).** Keyless types: an
  inferred key says when it was made non-nullable; a synthesized key stays SYNTH; non-resource records need none.
  RPC and events: a gRPC client / bidirectional stream and a GraphQL subscription are no longer written as one call
  — they are not written (`stream-dropped`, critical DROP); a server stream is a Function / Action returning a
  collection (`stream-as-collection`, APPROX); unary RPCs stay Actions / Functions; events and channels DROP. Type
  coercion: a `format` no CSDL type carries (`email`, `uri` …) is now reported (`constraint-dropped`) instead of
  silently lost; unsigned / unknown primitives APPROX; field numbers DROP (info).
- Goldens: the `odata` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.520.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Added
- **OData CSDL emitter: CSDL JSON 4.01 + CSDL XML (MFX-16.1, #3897).** The `odata` writer is rebuilt around one CSDL
  JSON model (the canonical output, `<Namespace>.csdl.json`); option `output` (`json` | `xml` | `both`) also renders
  it as CSDL XML (`.edmx`). Records an HTTP operation sends or returns become `EntityType`s with entity sets (a
  types-only source exposes its root records), others `ComplexType`s; every entity has a `$Key` (the source's, an
  id-like property — `key-inferred` — or a synthesized `Id` — `key-synthesized`, SYNTH). Primitives coerced through
  `edm_type` (widths, `Edm.DateTimeOffset` / `Date` / `TimeOfDay` / `Duration` / `Guid` / `Decimal` / `Untyped`;
  unsigned widened and unknowns reported). Enums (integer values; string wire values reported), `TypeDefinition`s,
  unions as complex types and maps as open types (reported), aliases inlined. `$MaxLength` / `$DefaultValue`,
  `Validation` (Pattern, Minimum / Maximum + Exclusive, MinItems / MaxItems, AllowedValues) and `Core`
  (Description, Revisions) annotations with their `$Reference`s. CRUD operations served by entity sets
  (`crud-as-entity-set`); every other operation an unbound Function (GET / query with a result) or Action with an
  import; headers, cookies and error responses reported; events dropped. OData 2 / 3 sources keep `MaxLength` /
  `Precision` / `Scale`, coerce `Edm.DateTime` / `Edm.Time`, report `sap:` / `m:` annotations and the upgrade.
- `ODataFidelityRulePack` predicts exactly the writer's losses; `WriterLossRulePack.synthesized` maps writer
  losses to SYNTH.
- Export validation for `odata` checks the OASIS CSDL JSON schema (or the CSDL XML schemas), then re-parses.

#### Changed
- The `odata` export's default output is CSDL JSON; CSDL XML is `output: xml`.
- Goldens: the `odata` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.519.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **OpenRPC fidelity pack: REST, gRPC and event losses enumerated (MFX-33.2, #4302).** JSON-RPC 2.0 has no HTTP
  semantics, streams or channels; each loss is now its own report item with kind and reason. HTTP (per REST
  operation, replacing the single `rest-as-method` approximation): `http-binding-dropped` (DROP — method and path,
  kept only as `x-http`), `http-parameters-reframed` (APPROX — the locations of path / query / header / cookie
  params and the body), `http-status-dropped` (DROP — a success status other than 200), `http-status-as-error-code`
  (APPROX), alongside `response-header-dropped` and `error-dropped`. Streaming: gRPC streams and GraphQL
  subscriptions stay DROP. Events: publish / subscribe operations are now written as notifications (APPROX
  `event-as-notification`) with their message and channel parameters as by-name params and the channel address as
  `x-channel`, instead of being dropped; a channel used by one is APPROX `channel-as-notification`, an unused one
  DROP `channel-dropped`. Field identity: a source field number is DROP (info).
- `FidelityRulePack.channel_verdicts()` list hook (default: the single verdict); `WriterLossRulePack` files writer
  losses by channel key and reports them per channel.
- Goldens: the `openrpc` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.518.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Added
- **OpenRPC emitter (MFX-33.1, #4301).** The `openrpc` writer is rebuilt to emit documents valid against the
  OpenRPC meta-schema (`@open-rpc/meta-schema` 1.14.9, vendored as `app/data/openrpc_meta_schema_1_14_9.json`;
  its JSONSchema reference points at draft-07). Every method has `params`; `info.version` is always written (`0.0.0`
  synthesized and reported); servers keep name, description and variables. RPC methods: an OpenRPC source's
  params as written, else one `params` descriptor; `result`; `errors` (`code` / `message` / `data`); `tags`;
  `deprecated`; one-way operations are notifications (no `result`); method names unique across services. REST
  sources are reframed instead of dropped: parameters and body → by-name params labeled with their location,
  the success response → `result` (`{"type": "null"}` without a body), numeric statuses → error codes, the
  binding → `x-http`. Schemas: `components/schemas` through `SchemaEmitter`, every `$ref` pointing at a written
  component (names made JSON-pointer safe), canonical scalars resolved through `CANONICAL_SCALAR_SCHEMAS`.
- `OpenRpcFidelityRulePack` predicts exactly the writer's losses (`WriterLossRulePack`): REST reframing,
  synthesized version, renames and unknown scalars approximated; events, streams, extra success responses,
  errors without an integer code, error payload types, response headers and repeated fields dropped; a REST
  root reported as `rest → JSON-RPC`.
- Export validation for `openrpc`: the meta-schema, then a re-parse (`validate_openrpc_document`).

#### Fixed
- The OpenRPC reader keeps each method's `errors` (following `#/components/errors/` references), `tags`
  and `deprecated`, and reads a method with no `result` as a notification (a one-way operation).
- Goldens: OpenRPC corpus snapshots (03, 04); the `openrpc` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance
  matrices; corpus parity.

### 1.517.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **TypeSpec fidelity pack: non-REST losses and decorator coverage (MFX-15.2, #3894).** Non-REST: a source of
  another paradigm gets a root `APPROX` (`graph → REST`, `rpc → REST` …: operations without an HTTP binding become
  POST routes, the item reads back as REST); the `rpc-as-http` loss names the operation's kind (GraphQL query,
  mutation, subscription, one-way — its reply an empty 204 —, RPC); a GraphQL subscription is reported as a
  dropped stream like a streaming call; event-role messages and a second request are `message-dropped`.
  Decorator coverage — written, no longer silently lost: operation tags as `@tag(...)` (and read back by the
  TypeSpec reader), parameter and header descriptions as `@doc(...)` and deprecations as `#deprecated`, request
  message headers as `@header` parameters, an `enum` constraint on a string or number as a union of literals
  (defaults checked against it), server-variable enums and docs. Reported where TypeSpec has no place: response
  descriptions (`response-description-dropped`, info), a type namespace other than the document's
  (`namespace-flattened`, info), the identity id (root, info). GraphQL `ID` is written as `string` without an
  unknown-type loss.
- Goldens: the `typespec` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices, corpus parity.

### 1.516.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Added
- **TypeSpec emitter: compiling `.tsp` from any source (MFX-15.1, #3893).** The `typespec` writer is rebuilt for the
  bundled `tsp` 0.65 + `@typespec/http`. Document: `@service({ title })` (the `#{}` form the old writer used does not
  compile on 0.65), the description as the namespace's doc comment, `@info({ version })` (`@typespec/openapi`),
  `@server(url, description, { variables })`. Types: `model`, `enum` (string values when they differ from the
  name, numeric values kept), `union` (named variants or member types), `model X is Record<V>`, `model X is T[]`,
  `scalar X extends <base>`, `alias X = T`. Members: optional `?` from nullability, `@minLength` / `@maxLength` /
  `@pattern` / `@format` / `@minValue` / `@maxValue` (+ `Exclusive`) / `@minItems` / `@maxItems`, `= default`
  (literals, enum members, `#[…]` lists), `/** */` docs, `#deprecated`; names that are not identifiers are
  backticked, not renamed. Operations: one `interface` per service, `@get` … `@head` + `@route`, `@path` / `@query`
  / `@header("Name")` / `@cookie("name")` / `@body`, a non-JSON body's `Content-Type`, responses as the return
  type (plain 200, `@statusCode` variants, `NXX` ranges, a `default` error as an `@error` model, response
  headers); an RPC operation is `@post @route("/<Service>/<op>")`. A TypeSpec source keeps its imports,
  namespace, interface route prefixes, field type expressions and decorators. Nothing to declare → 422.
- `TypeSpecFidelityRulePack` predicts exactly the writer's losses (dropped constraints, defaults, numeric enum
  values beside strings, verbs TypeSpec lacks, duplicate routes, unplaceable path parameters, multipart bodies
  that are not models, events; approximated renames, RPC routes, aliases, custom scalars, inline schemas,
  synthesized path parameters, default-response models). `app.writer_loss_rulepack.WriterLossRulePack` is the
  shared base of the Smithy and TypeSpec packs (losses filed by construct, severity by subject).
- Export validation compiles a TypeSpec export with the bundled compiler (each compile error is a finding) and
  re-parses it when the compiler is not installed.

#### Fixed
- The built-in TypeSpec reader (single `.tsp` imports) read no model properties (its field pattern never matched
  an indented line); it now reads them with their decorators, `?`, backticked names and `= default`. Doc comments
  were taken from shifted offsets (comment stripping changed lengths); comments are now blanked in place, strings
  aware, and `/** */` docs are read. Operations: their own `@route`, `@head`, parameters with `("name")`
  arguments and `?`, response types holding `;`. Parameters are required unless marked `?` (path and body
  always). An interface's `@route` is the one decorating it (it could be the previous interface's).
  `@service({ title })` is read. Cookie parameters. Enum members with values.
- Goldens: TypeSpec corpus snapshots; the `typespec` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices.

### 1.515.0 — 2026-10-29

#### Changed
- **Smithy fidelity pack: trait coverage and protocol-binding gaps (MFX-20.2, #3915).** `SmithyFidelityRulePack`
  now builds the model with the Smithy writer and files each loss the writer records under its construct, so the
  fidelity report predicts exactly what the export reports. Trait coverage: constraints with a Smithy trait
  (`@length` / `@range` / `@pattern` / `@uniqueItems`) are carried (the pack used to call every constraint "dropped",
  and the capability profile now declares `constraints`); `multipleOf`, an enum list, a length on a number, an
  unfitting default and a Smithy source's value-less trait are a `DROP`; renames (`INFO`), inlined aliases, wrapped
  payloads, unknown scalars and a broken required cycle are an `APPROX`. Protocol bindings: an HTTP operation is `OK`
  with its `@http(method uri)` binding as the target mapping (it used to be reported "reframed as RPC"); an
  unbindable or duplicate route, a GET / HEAD / DELETE body, a cookie or transport-header parameter and a non-record
  error response are a `DROP` on the operation. The document: a non-Smithy source's root reports its namespace, and
  the title, description, servers and version (moved to the service, or dropped with no service) Smithy has no place
  for. A carried type or operation names the shape it became.
- The Smithy writer gives an unknown scalar's loss the key of the field, parameter or type that uses it, and a broken
  required cycle the key of its field (it was the shape-qualified member name).
- Goldens: the `smithy` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices; the `smithy` silent-loss ledger
  goes from 9 pairs to 0.

### 1.514.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Smithy 2.0 emitter: JSON AST + IDL, traits and HTTP bindings (MFX-20.1, #3914).** The `smithy` writer is rebuilt
  around one model built as a Smithy JSON AST and rendered as IDL too, so the two always agree; both validate under
  `smithy validate`. Shapes: `structure`, `union` (fields or member types; `void` members target `Unit`), `enum`
  (`= "value"` when the wire value differs), `map` (string keys), named `list`s and a synthesized `<Element>List` for
  an anonymous list (lists were written as their element type), simple shapes for named scalars and scalar aliases;
  an alias of a named shape is inlined. Traits: `@required` from nullability, `@default` when it fits the target,
  `@length` / `@range` (an exclusive integer bound made inclusive) / `@pattern` on the shapes they apply to,
  `@uniqueItems` on a `<Element>Set` list, doc comments, `@deprecated`, `@jsonName` for a renamed member. Names are
  Smithy identifiers unique case-insensitively and never a prelude shape (`smithy_identifier`; renames reported); a
  trait shadowed by a model shape is written fully qualified; a cycle of required members has one `@required`
  dropped. Operations take a structure payload as input / output, else a synthesized `<Operation>Input` /
  `<Operation>Output`; HTTP operations get `@http(method, uri, code)`, `@httpLabel` / `@httpQuery` / `@httpHeader` /
  `@httpPayload` members and `@readonly` / `@idempotent`; GET / HEAD / DELETE bodies, transport headers (e.g.
  `Authorization`), and unbindable or duplicate routes are reported; a record only ever returned as an error becomes
  an `@error` / `@httpError` structure in the operation's `errors`. A Smithy source keeps its namespace, versions and
  operation order; resources and value-less traits are reported. Nothing to declare → 422 (`EmitPreconditionError`).
- New options: `output` (`idl` | `json-ast` | `both`) and `protocol` (`none` | `restJson1` | `rpcv2Cbor`).
- `SMITHY_SCALAR_FOR_KIND` in `app.scalar_aliases`.

#### Changed
- `SmithyFidelityRulePack` predicts the writer's shape, member and operation renames (`APPROX`) and dropped agents
  (`DROP`).

#### Fixed
- The Smithy IDL reader attaches doc comments to the right shape (offsets came from the comment-stripped text) and
  past trait lines; member traits whose value holds `:` or `)` (`@range(min: 1)`, `@pattern("^(a|b)$")`) are read; enum
  members written `NAME = "value"` are read.
- Goldens: Smithy corpus snapshots (descriptions), the `smithy` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance
  matrices; `smithy -> smithy` now round-trips (xfail removed); the `smithy` silent-loss ledger goes from 12 pairs to 9.

### 1.513.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **OMG IDL 4.2 emitter for CORBA and DDS (MFX-28.1, #4168).** The `corbaidl` writer is rebuilt so its output parses
  under reference IDL compilers (omniidl; Cyclone DDS `idlc`): every type, member, enumerator, operation, parameter,
  interface and module name is a valid identifier, unique case-insensitively in its scope, unlike its enclosing
  scope and not an IDL keyword (`idl_identifier`, `OMG_IDL_KEYWORDS`; renames reported); every type reference is
  fully scoped (`::com::acme::Order`); definitions are declared before use, self-recursive types forward-declared
  (a direct self reference is a one-element bounded sequence, mutual recursion is dropped and reported); unions are
  discriminated on a synthesized `<Union>Kind` enum (one case per field or member type; `void` arms select no
  member); maps are `sequence<<Map>Entry>`; nullable members are `@optional`; aliases and named scalars are
  `typedef`s; empty structs get a placeholder member; the API namespace becomes nested modules (a module named like
  one of its definitions is renamed `<Name>Module`); services become interfaces whose operations take parameters
  and the body as `in` arguments, return the first 2xx response, typedef sequences in signatures, and `raises`
  exceptions only (a record only ever returned as an error becomes one; other error responses are reported). A
  CORBA source keeps its module, typedefs and interfaces. Nothing to declare → 422 (`EmitPreconditionError`).
- New options: `profile` (`corba` | `dds` — the DDS profile writes data types only, no recursion or wide
  characters, `@key` on identifier fields), `module` (module path) and `key_fields` (DDS keys per type).
- `OMG_IDL_SCALAR_FOR_KIND` in `app.scalar_aliases` (classic CORBA spellings: `long long`, `unsigned short`, …).

#### Changed
- The CORBA IDL reader reads what the writer writes: IDL 4 annotations are skipped, scoped names reduced, `long
  long` / `unsigned …` / `long double` and bounded sequences read, a chain of single nested modules read as one
  dotted module (`com.acme`), and a data-types-only module (the DDS profile) detected as CORBA IDL.
- `CorbaIdlFidelityRulePack` predicts the writer's type, member and operation renames (`APPROX`) and dropped agents
  (`DROP`).
- Goldens: the `corbaidl` cells of the round-trip and export-conformance matrices are regenerated (their exports now
  re-import, so drift is measured); the `corbaidl` silent-loss ledger goes from 4 pairs to 5 (`flatbuffers`, which
  could not be read back before).

### 1.511.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Arazzo fidelity pack (MFX-10.2, #3871).** `ArazzoFidelityRulePack` tells a non-workflow source what Arazzo makes

### 1.510.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Collection fidelity pack (MFX-31.2, #4290).** `app.client_collection_fidelity.ExampleCollectionFidelityRulePack`

### 1.509.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Postman Collection v2.1 emitter (MFX-31.1, #4289).** The `postman` target is rebuilt over the shared client-collection
  plan (`app.client_collection_emit`, FMT-10.4) that Hoppscotch and Thunder Client are written from.
  - Folders by the new option `folder_strategy`: `auto` (default — first tag, else the service when the model has more
    than one), `tag`, `service`, `flat`; nested at ` / `.
  - Variables by the new option `variable_style`: `variables` (default — every server a collection variable,
    `{{baseUrl}}`, `{{baseUrl2}}` …, with a server template's variables declared) or `inline` (literal server URLs).
    Credential variables are always declared with an empty value.
  - Requests: `:param` path variables, query parameters (optional ones disabled), headers, and example bodies
    synthesized from the request schema (was: the JSON Schema itself) at the new option `example_depth`
    (`minimal` / `full`); form bodies as `urlencoded` / `formdata` fields.
  - Saved example responses per single-status response, with bodies synthesized from the response schema; status
    ranges reported (`status-range-response`).
  - Auth: `bearer`, `basic`, `digest`, `apiKey`, `oauth2` as Postman v2.1 auth blocks with `{{variable}}`
    credentials; written once on the collection when every request shares it.
  - Info carries the description and version. A Postman source is written back as read (its folder tree, headers,
    raw bodies, saved responses, variables, auth schemes with empty values) and reports nothing; a Collection v2.0
    source is written as v2.1 (`collection-upgraded`). A source with no HTTP operation is refused (`422`,

    type, deprecation flags, tags, streaming, type renames and namespaces, enum numbers and value docs, map key types,

### 1.504.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **WSDL 1.1 + XSD emitter, document/literal (MFX-14.1, #3889).** The `wsdl` target is now multi-file: `<Name>.wsdl`
  imports `<Name>.xsd` (`xsd:import` in an import-only `wsdl:types` schema, WS-I R2105). New option
  `layout: bundle | single` (default `bundle`; `single` inlines the schema).
  - New `app/xsd_types.py`: canonical scalar + `format` → XSD built-in (`integer`+`int64` → `long`, `date-time` →
    `dateTime`, `decimal`, `anyURI`, `base64Binary`; an imported `xsd_type` hint wins), `ncname()` for legal XML names,
    and `xsd_pattern()` translating ECMA-262 patterns to XSD (anchors removed or padded; lookaround, lazy quantifiers,
    `\b`, backreferences and anything the XSD regex grammar rejects are dropped and reported; `\/` becomes `/`).
  - Types: records → `complexType`/`sequence` + global element; lists → `maxOccurs` (from `minItems`/`maxItems`);
    nullable → `minOccurs="0" nillable="true"`; constraints → length/range/pattern/enumeration facets; enums →
    `simpleType`; unions → `xs:choice`; maps → `entry` lists; aliases and named scalars → derived types; descriptions →
    `xs:annotation`; defaults.
  - Non-WSDL sources are written document/literal wrapped: a request element per operation (parameters + body), a
    `<op>Response` element and one element per fault (`<op>Status404Fault`). WSDL sources keep their own messages,
    parts and topology, and now also their recorded `xsd_type` (`dateTime`, `decimal`).
  - Names are made legal NCNames and de-duplicated; every rename, dropped HTTP binding, event operation, map,
    untyped value, unsupported facet and deprecated flag is recorded as an emit loss.

#### Changed
- **WSDL capability profile and rule pack.** `unions`, `nullability` and `constraints` are now `True` and
  `field_identity` `False` (WSDL writes no field numbers). `WsdlFidelityRulePack` reports the target namespace (SYNTH
  when invented, info when taken from the source), renames, maps, untyped values, `multipleOf`/`uniqueItems`/
  untranslatable patterns, deprecated fields and REST operations losing their HTTP method and path.
- `fidelity_rulepack.rename_verdict` is now shared (lifted from the Cap'n Proto pack; same wording).
- Goldens: the `wsdl → wsdl` round trip now passes (xfail removed); the 22 WSDL silent-loss ledger pairs are cleared
  (ledger 628 → 606).

#### Fixed

  parameters, and maps OpenAPI `integer`/`number`/`boolean` to XSD built-ins instead of `tns:integer`.

### 1.503.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Cap'n Proto schema emitter compiles from any source (MFX-30.2, #4179).** `CapnpEmitter` now writes `struct`s with
  contiguous `@N` ordinals, `enum`s, `UNION` types as a `struct` holding an unnamed `union` group, `MAP` types as

  `interface`s whose methods take the operation's parameters and request body. Scalars map through the new

  source stay nested, and a source's imports are written `using X = import "…";` (was the invalid `@import`).

  `EmitResult.field_identity_assignments`, loaded and persisted by `emit_canonical`). A re-export is identical; a new
  member gets the next free ordinal; a removed member keeps its ordinal as an `obsolete<Name>` placeholder of the
  same wire layout (recorded as `@layout:` rows), since Cap'n Proto allows no holes. The file id is derived from the
  API identity on first export (top bit set) and then persisted. Synthesized numbers are `INFERRED` losses
  (`synthesized-ordinal`, `synthesized-file-id`); `.capnp` sources keep their own ordinals and file id.

  from source in the image) and `app.capnproto_compile.compile_capnp_schema`; the export validator compiles every
  `capnproto` export and reports *skipped* when the tool is absent or the schema imports other files.
- **Migration V337.** `apiome.export_field_identities.field_number` is `BIGINT`, and its check allows `0` and values
  above 536870911 for the `capnproto` target only.

#### Changed

  method the emitter renames to Cap'n Proto's naming rules as an `APPROX` (info) verdict. Exports that now re-import
  show those renames instead of losing them silently; nine pairs leave the export-conformance silent-loss ledger.

### 1.501.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Fixed
- **Protobuf and Thrift export from OpenAPI projects compiles (#6278).** The OpenAPI normalizer keeps JSON Schema's
  `integer` / `number` / `boolean` (width in the field's `format`), and the proto3 and Thrift emitters wrote them as
  type references (`.integer id = 1;`). New `app.scalar_aliases` reduces the fleet's scalar spellings plus `format`
  to a kind and maps it to each target's keyword (`integer` → `int32`, or `int64` with `format: int64`; `number` →
  `double`/`float`; `boolean` → `bool`; Thrift widens unsigned and `float`). A type the model defines by such a name

### 1.498.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Security
- **Export archives can no longer name a path outside the bundle (X6, #6227 — high).** The Avro emitter
  (`.avsc` and `.avdl`) turned a namespace from the imported schema or the `namespace` option into folders
  verbatim, so a namespace such as `/abs/evil`, `C:\x` or `..\x` produced an absolute, drive-letter or backslash
  member that a naive extractor would write outside its folder (zip slip). Every emitted path is now normalised by
  `zip_bundle.safe_bundle_path` (relative, `/`-separated, no `..`, drive prefix or control characters) on
  `EmittedFile`, so the manifest, the zip, the download name and the UI's file tree agree; `write_zip_entry` refuses
  any unsafe member name; Avro builds folders from sanitised namespace parts (`com.acme` → `com/acme`).
- **Download names outside Latin-1 no longer fail with 500 (medium).** `POST …/export/{tenant}/document` and
  `GET …/jobs/{job_id}/download` send `Content-Disposition` with an ASCII `filename` plus an RFC 6266
  `filename*=UTF-8''…` (`download_headers.attachment_headers`); the document route also strips quotes and control
  characters now.
- **Export downloads send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (low).**

`tests/test_export_security.py` runs every registered emitter over hostile names and extracts each bundle as a naive
tool would. Review record: `docs/RC7_CATALOG_IMPORT_EXPORT.md` §4.5.

### 1.497.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added

  - **Concurrent jobs per tenant** — `APIOME_EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS_PER_TENANT` (default 5). `POST
    /v1/export/{tenant}/jobs` answers `429` while the tenant already has that many queued or running export jobs,
    counted across instances (this process's jobs plus the shared store's, created within the time cap so a row
    left `running` by a crashed instance stops counting).

    fails with the new taxonomy code `EXPORT_JOB_TIMED_OUT` (category `resource`, not retriable).

  `0` turns either off. The existing limits are unchanged and now documented together (Export a spec →
  **Limits**, and the `POST …/jobs` description): `APIOME_EXPORT_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES` (32 MiB,

  and `APIOME_EXPORT_ARTIFACT_RETENTION_HOURS` (24 h, then `410`). `tests/test_export_limits.py` has a test per
  limit.

  artifact past its retention window leaves memory even if its job is never polled again.

### 1.496.0 — 2026-10-28

### 1.495.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Export conformance matrix (X1, #6222).** `tests/test_export_conformance_matrix.py` exports every corpus source
  family (108) to every production target (53) through the catalog export path and classifies each pair as `ok`,
  `lossy` (with a fidelity report), `refused` (with a reason), `silent-loss` (an empty fidelity report while the
  round trip shows drift) or `crash`. The matrix is checked in at `tests/golden/export_conformance/` (JSON +

  gate fails on any crash, on a new silent-loss pair or a stale entry in the tracked ledger

  `export-conformance.yml` runs it on REST, corpus and matrix changes.

#### Fixed

  (`Emitter.requires_source`: `http-operation` for Kong, Gateway API, Envoy, Istio, Traefik, Apigee, AWS API
  Gateway, Azure APIM, Hoppscotch, Thunder Client and the `.http` file; `record-type` for ODCS and Kafka Connect;

  discovers mid-emit raises the new `EmitPreconditionError`, which `emit_canonical` turns into the same `422`.

  each rename; gives an empty record a `_empty: Boolean` placeholder; writes a union over non-object members and
  an untyped value as `String`; derives request-argument names from the payload type's simple name.
- **Avro export** maps more scalar spellings to primitives (`i32`, `uint64`, `decimal`, …, case-insensitive),
  writes a reference to an undeclared type as `string`, cuts a reference cycle between schema files (reported as
  `cyclic-reference`), coerces textual defaults (`"100"` → `100`), qualifies the members of a standalone union, and
  resolves a referenced type's namespace the way its own schema is written.
- **ASN.1 export** no longer crashes on an alias or scalar type.
- **Kafka Connect export** writes an empty nested record as optional `bytes`, skips an empty root record (refusing
  when every record is empty), and renames a repeated field name.
- API 1.359.0.

    context adds `source_code`, `reimport` and `artifact_id`.
  - **Unavailable targets refused up front.** New `export_service.ensure_target_available`: a real export (resolve,
    dispatch, job submit) to a target whose registry descriptor is `available: false` is refused with `422` and the
    registry's `unavailable_reason`, before any emit. A dry run (fidelity only) still answers. No shipped emitter is
    toolchain-gated today; the guard reads `required_tools`, so one that is later is never offered and then failed.
  - **Captured-source backfill.** New `app.source_backfill` and `scripts/backfill_captured_sources.py`
    (`--dry-run`, `--tenant`): repairs a revision with no captured source from a stored copy — another revision of
    the same item, or the linked repository file (`repository_import_spec`) — only when the copy re-imports to the
    revision's recorded `fingerprint`. A repository file is scrubbed under the tenant's secret-scrub policy, and every
    repair stamps `sourceBackfilledFrom`. Prints `scanned`, `repaired`, `unrepaired`, `unverifiable` and `no_copy`
    plus each revision's outcome.
  - API 1.358.0.

### 1.493.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Lint of the emitted export artifact (MFX-5.2, #3853)** — `POST /v1/export/{tenant}/verify` now fills `lint`
  (it was always `null`). New `app.export_emitted_lint` reads the emitted artifact back through its format's import
  adapter (the IXH-4.4 round-trip seams) and lints that model with `lint_canonical_model` — the same MFI rule packs
  and score/grade formula an import uses: the format's own pack (`graphql`, `protobuf`, `avro`, `asyncapi`, `raml`,
  `smithy`, …), else its paradigm pack (`rest-conventions`, `data-contract`), else only the unconditional packs
  (`pack: "common"`). The report is advisory and never changes the verdict. A format no adapter reads back, an
  artifact the adapter refuses, or a lint fault reports `applicable: false` with a new `reason` field instead of
  failing the verify. `EmittedArtifactLint` moved from `app.export_routes` to `app.export_emitted_lint`. API 1.357.0.

### 1.492.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Several items in one export job (E1-3, #6219)** — `POST /v1/export/{tenant}/jobs` accepts `items`

### 1.491.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Version retention for live refresh (MFI-31.5, #4402)** — each catalog item's refresh setting has `keepVersions`
  (`PUT …/{item_id}/refresh`, 1–1000, default 50; V336 `catalog_item_refresh.keep_versions`). After each
  refresh-created version (and after its drift is recorded) `app.version_retention` keeps the newest N versions a
  live refresh created (provenance `refreshTrigger`) and soft-deletes the older ones with `versions.pruned_at`
  (V336), audited as `catalog.refresh.versions_pruned`. Always kept: tagged versions, conversion-source versions
  (`conversion_provenance.source_version_id`), breaking-drift versions and their baselines, locked revisions and the
  item's newest version; hand imports are never pruned. A pruned version answers **410** `version-pruned`

  `POST /v1/diff/{tenant}/classified` instead of 404. Drift events gain `parentVersionPruned`,
  `compareBaseVersionId` and `compareBaseVersionLabel` (the nearest kept earlier version when the baseline was
  pruned). Migration V336. API 1.355.0.

### 1.490.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Registry-crawl throttling and incremental resume (MFI-31.4, #4401)** — new `app.crawl_budget`: a per-crawl
  budget (`requestsPerSecond`, `maxRequests`, `maxPages`, `maxBytes` scope keys, validated against per-family
  defaults and ceilings), a `CrawlMeter` that rate-limits per host and stops a crawl cleanly when the request or
  byte budget is spent (`CrawlBudgetExceededError`, error class `budget-exceeded`), and a per-connector crawl
  checkpoint (V335 `catalog_connector_crawl_state`). The `schema-registry` connector now accepts those keys plus
  `fullPassHours` (default 24): a **full pass** lists subjects in pages of 100 from the checkpoint cursor, using
  at most half the request budget for listing, and records the cursor as each subject settles, so a sync that is
  killed or runs out of budget resumes after the last finished subject; a spent budget defers the rest and the
  run still succeeds. Between full passes an **incremental pass** probes `GET /schemas/ids/{id}/versions` above
  the stored schema-id watermark (tolerating id gaps) and reads only the subjects that changed; a registry that
  does not answer the probe (Apicurio ccompat) falls back to full passes. Only full passes mark subjects
  missing. Each run summary carries a `crawl` block (mode, requests/pages/bytes used, budget, `exhaustedBy`,
  `partial`, `resumesAfter`, `watermark`, `lastFullPassAt`). The connector engine gained the source hooks
  `bind_db`, `live_remote_ids`, `candidate_settled`, `budget_exhausted` and `crawl_report`. `registry` crawl
  connectors (xRegistry, A2A, FHIR) accept the same budget keys and now cap total response bytes per sync.
  `MAX_SUBJECTS` rises to 100,000. Migration V335. API 1.354.0.

### 1.489.0 — 2026-10-28

#### Added
- **Catalog drift and breaking-change notifications (MFI-31.3, #4400)** — when a live refresh adds a version over
  an earlier one, the refresh apply hook classifies the change with the MFI-3.3 breaking-change engine
  (`breaking_change.classify_models`, format packs included) and records a drift event (`app.catalog_drift_service`,
  V334 `catalog_drift_events`): worst severity (`safe` / `dangerous` / `breaking`), per-severity counts and the
  classified changes worst first (capped at 200). The catalog list and detail carry the newest undismissed event as
  `drift`. New routes: `GET /v1/catalog/{tenant_slug}/{item_id}/drift` (`projects:view`),
  `POST …/{item_id}/drift/{event_id}/dismiss` (`projects:edit`, idempotent), and `GET` / `PUT
  /v1/catalog/{tenant_slug}/drift-notifications` (`projects:view` / `imports:edit`; V334 `catalog_drift_settings`):
  which severities are announced (default breaking + dangerous; safe only badges), `immediate` or `daily_digest`
  delivery, `breakingImmediate`, and a stored `emailEnabled` opt-in (no email is sent yet). A sweep-created drift is
  announced as a `catalog.drift.detected` push-webhook event (artifact, versions, severity, counts, top five findings,
  app link) through the existing signed retry pipeline and routed to the item's owner team as an
  `owner_breaking_change` finding; a `Check now` drift is recorded but never announced. Digest mode holds events
  (`pending_digest`) for one `catalog.drift.digest` webhook per tenant per day, sent from the refresh sweep tick.
  Migration V334. API 1.353.0.

### 1.488.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Catalog item refresh: re-discovery through the import pipeline (MFI-31.2, #4399)** — a live-refresh check
  now behaves exactly like a manual re-import. The GraphQL and gRPC discovery runners serialize what they
  discovered into the document a manual import would upload (SDL via `print_schema_with_directives`, the
  reflection descriptor set as `reflection.binpb`) and fingerprint it with a dry run of
  `run_adapter_import_job` (`catalog_refresh.pipeline_discovery_result`). The new apply hook
  (`app.catalog_refresh_apply`) rebuilds the item's current version from its stored source and calls
  `versioning.decide_version`: an unchanged source creates nothing; a changed one is imported onto the item
  (`existing_project_id`) with a minted date/time label, so lint score capture, payload analysis, search rows
  and the verbatim source are stored as for any import, and gets the connector-sync change report (diff +
  breaking classification) against the version it supersedes, audited as
  `catalog.refresh.change_report.generated`. The pipeline's refresh mode (`refresh_source` on the internal
  payload) forces catalog routing and records `inputKind: discovery`, the endpoint, `refreshAdapter` and
  `refreshTrigger` (`sweep` or `manual`) on the revision's `format_metadata`. `status: changed` now means
  the check added a version; `POST …/refresh/check` audits the created `versionId`. A sweep-created version is
  attributed to whoever last saved the setting. A deleted item or a Project fails the check
  (`item-unavailable`). API 1.352.0.

### 1.487.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Catalog item refresh: scheduler and per-item cadence (MFI-31.1, #4398)** — a catalog item can be re-checked
  against its live source. `GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE /v1/catalog/{tenant_slug}/{item_id}/refresh` read, store and
  remove the setting: a cadence (`off` by default, `manual`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`), the adapter (`graphql`
  introspection or `grpc` reflection — adapters that declare `supports_live_discovery` and have a runner), the
  endpoint (SSRF URL policy on save, the adapter's guarded client on every call), options (gRPC `secure`) and an
  optional credential sealed with the MCP credential envelope and never returned (`hasCredential` only).
  `POST …/refresh/check` runs one check now. A background sweep (`app.catalog_refresh_sweep`, single-flight
  advisory lock) checks due items under a global concurrency cap and a per-host politeness delay; a failed check
  is recorded as `status: failed` with `lastError` and backs off exponentially, and never creates a version. A
  successful check records the fingerprint and `unchanged` / `changed`; the import-pipeline apply hook arrives
  with MFI-31.2 (#4399). `GET` / `PUT /v1/catalog/{tenant_slug}/refresh-policy` is the tenant kill switch
  (`imports:edit`); `APIOME_CATALOG_REFRESH_ENABLED` is the deployment one. New settings:
  `APIOME_CATALOG_REFRESH_TICK`, `_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `_HOST_DELAY`, `_TIMEOUT`, `_BACKOFF_BASE`, `_BACKOFF_MAX`.
  Migration V333. API 1.351.0.

### 1.486.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **OpenAPI 3.1 components importer for Primitives (#3465)** — `POST /v1/primitives/{tenant_slug}/import` and

  each entry becomes one `odb.primitives` row named after its component, and the document root (`info`, `paths`,

### 1.485.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Cross-protocol search over the normalized model (MFI-6.2, #3754)** — new
  `GET /v1/search/{tenant_slug}/model?q=…` (`app.model_search`, `app.model_search_routes`) finds every operation,
  type and message whose name, key, path or description matches, across every format the tenant imported: gRPC
  services, GraphQL fields, AsyncAPI operations and messages, Avro records, and OpenAPI Projects. `q` uses Postgres
  websearch syntax with English stemming (`createOrder` matches `CreateOrder`; `"quoted phrase"`, `or`, `-word`).
  The canonical model is matched through V135's GIN indexes (`idx_api_operations_fts`, `idx_api_types_fts`,
  `idx_api_messages_fts`); an OpenAPI Project's `path_operation` rows and `classes` are searched for revisions
  with no canonical artifact, so nothing is reported twice. Repeatable `kind` (operation / type / message),
  `protocol` (paradigm, aliases such as `grpc` work), `format` and `grade` (A–F or `ungraded`) facets compose:
  values OR within a facet, facets AND, and each facet is counted over what the others keep. Each project's latest
  revision is searched unless `all_versions=true`; `limit` (≤ 100) / `offset` page the ranked hits and `truncated`
  flags a search that reached its 2 000-row cap. Response `ModelSearchResponse` (`ModelSearchHit`,
  `ModelSearchFacets`). API 1.349.0.

#### Changed
- **Every import persists its canonical model (MFI-6.2, #3754)** — `persist_adapter_import` now writes the
  MFI-2.2 tables for every format, not only AsyncAPI, agent descriptors and Arazzo, so the search can find them.
  For the formats that newly persist, a failed write is logged and the import carries on; AsyncAPI and agent
  descriptors still fail the import as before. Arazzo is still written once, by its workflow persistence.
- **Re-index existing catalog items** — `scripts/backfill_canonical_models.py` (`app.canonical_model_reindex`)
  rebuilds the canonical model of every catalog item whose latest revision has none, from its captured source,
  with the convert flow's `build_conversion_source`. Run it once after deploying; it is safe to re-run, and
  reports items without a captured source as skipped.

### 1.484.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Alternate intake on the import-source registry (MFI-26.5, #4098)** — `ImportSourceDescriptor` gains
  `alternate_intake` (`ImportSourceAlternateIntake`: `kind`, `label`, `description`, `icon`), set from the new
  `ImportSource.alternate_intake` class variable. It names an intake method a format offers beyond File / URL /
  Clipboard (a future live introspection, reflection or registry crawl), which the **Import to catalog** wizard

### 1.483.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Import a new version: compare with the latest version (IXH-3.7, #6321)** — new
  `POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_slug}/import/project-delta` (`app.import_project_delta`). Given the incoming OpenAPI
  document and the `project_slug` (or `project_id`) the commit would use, it resolves the target the way the commit
  does (an explicit id first, else the slug trimmed and lower-cased) and compares the document with the project's
  **latest** revision, rebuilt from the database with `openapi_for_revision` — so OpenAPI projects that keep no
  captured source work. The response (`ProjectDeltaResponse`) carries the compatibility engine's `overall` and
  `findings` (the Versions → Compare / gate rules), `counts` (added / changed / removed / breaking / total), a ranked

  `severity` is the worst covering finding, or null when ungraded; breaking first; capped at 5 000 with `truncated`),
  and both documents unless `include_documents` is false. **204** when the import is not a new version of an existing
  Project (no match, a catalog item, or no revision yet). Requires `imports:create` and `versions:view`; writes nothing.

### 1.481.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **REST hypermedia conventions (MFI-19.6, #3984)** — new `app.rest_conventions`: a REST artifact's request and

  `CatalogFacets.conventions` counts them.

  `jsonapi-top-level`, `jsonapi-data-and-errors`, `jsonapi-resource-object`, `jsonapi-error-document`,
  `hal-self-link`, `hal-link-object`, `hal-forms-template`, `jsonld-context`, `hydra-collection-member`. Seeded into
  the built-in style guide by V331.

### 1.480.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Avro compatibility engine (MFI-12.4, #3785)** — new `app.avro_compatibility`: `can_read(reader, writer)` applies
  Avro schema resolution as Avro's Java `SchemaCompatibility` does (`NAME_MISMATCH`, `FIXED_SIZE_MISMATCH`,
  `MISSING_ENUM_SYMBOLS`, `READER_FIELD_MISSING_DEFAULT_VALUE`, `TYPE_MISMATCH`, `MISSING_UNION_BRANCH`, with the
  same locations; promotions, reader aliases, enum defaults, recursive types), and `check_compatibility(level, …)`
  evaluates Confluent's seven levels: newest version first, stopping at the first that fails.
  `confluent_messages` renders Confluent's verbose messages. Verified against 112 verdicts recorded from Confluent
  Schema Registry 7.7.1 (`tests/fixtures/avro_compatibility`, re-recorded with
  `scripts/record_avro_compatibility_fixtures.py`).
- **`avro` breaking-change classifier** (`app.avro_breaking`, id `avro-compatibility`): runs the check both ways over
  the two versions' schemas; a BACKWARD failure is breaking, a FORWARD-only failure dangerous, and a type or field
  change the check reads both ways is safe. Rationales name the modes broken and carry Confluent's message.

#### Changed
- **Schema registry: Avro levels are enforced.** `AVRO` is in `schema_registry.COMPATIBILITY_RULES_SHIPPED`.
  Registering an Avro version that fails the subject's level is refused with `schema-incompatible` (409; Confluent
  routes `error_code` 409, "Schema being registered is incompatible with an earlier schema…"), and
  `POST /compatibility/subjects/{s}/versions[/{v}]` answers with the real verdict and messages
  (`schema_registry_service.compatibility_verdict`). JSON Schema and Protobuf still answer
  `compatibility-rules-unavailable` (42290). `/schemas/types?details=true` lists Avro as `available` under every
  level.

### 1.479.0 — 2026-10-27

#### Added
- **Avro Parsing Canonical Form fingerprints (MFI-12.1, #3782)** — new `app.avro_fingerprint`. Every named type of an
  Avro document (`.avsc` or IDL) is fingerprinted with the named types it references inlined at first use: its
  Parsing Canonical Form (`parsing_canonical_form`, the Avro 1.12 transformations; matches fastavro on the corpus)
  hashed with CRC-64-AVRO (`crc64_avro`) and SHA-256, and a semantic SHA-256 over the same normalization that keeps
  `doc`, `default`, `aliases`, `order`, `logicalType` and custom attributes (`semantic_form`). The Avro normalizer
  records them in extras `avro_pcf` (`{full name: {crc64, sha256}}`) and `avro_semantic_hashes`
  (`{full name: sha256}`). A doc-only edit flips the semantic hash but not the PCF.
- **`AvroPcfHasher`** — the `avro` `FingerprintHasher`: `FingerprintResult.format_hash` is the root schema's PCF
  SHA-256 (`format_algorithm` `avro-parsing-canonical-form-sha256`); an IDL protocol has none.
- **`fingerprint.UNHASHED_EXTRAS`** — top-level extras recorded on the model but left out of the version fingerprint
  and the diff (`avro_semantic_hashes`), so a doc-only Avro edit mints no new version.

#### Changed
- `FingerprintHasher.hash` may return `None` for an artifact with no format hash; `format_hash` and
  `format_algorithm` then stay unset.
- Avro catalog items gain the `avro_pcf` extras, so each one's canonical fingerprint changes once: its first
  re-import after this release records a new version.
- The schema registry's `fingerprintKind` description no longer promises `avro-pcf` with this release; registration
  still keys on the canonical-model fingerprint.

### 1.478.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **Smithy breaking-change classifier (MFI-17.4, #3811)** — new `app.smithy_breaking.SmithyBreakingChangeClassifier`
  (`smithy`, id `smithy-diff`) runs `smithy diff --format csv` through the bundled Smithy CLI
  (`app.smithy_ast.run_smithy_diff`, sandboxed, no network) and maps its evaluators' severities onto Apiome's:
  `ERROR` → breaking, `DANGER` / `WARNING` → dangerous, `NOTE` → safe. Each finding's shape id joins the canonical
  change on the same entity (member → field, else its shape; shape → type, service or operation), the worst finding
  replaces the baseline grade (`rule_id` `smithy-diff.<evaluator id>`), and changes no finding joins keep the
  baseline. Without the CLI, or when a model cannot be loaded, the baseline grades stand.
- **`ClassificationResult.unattributed`** — findings from a format's own diff tool that join no canonical change
  (`UnattributedFinding`: severity, rule id, rationale, shape). They count toward `overall_severity` / `breaking`
  but not toward `counts_by_severity`, so a gate never misses a tool-reported break.

#### Changed
- **Smithy single-file import** — with the Smithy CLI available, one `.smithy` file is assembled through
  `smithy ast` like a multi-file set (inline `:=` input / output members are now read); the built-in reader is the
  fallback when the CLI cannot load it. A multi-file set keeps its assembled JSON AST on `raw["smithy_ast"]` so
  `smithy diff` compares whole models.

### 1.477.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **RAML breaking-change classifier (MFI-15.4, #3802)** — RAML has no official compatibility rules, so new
  `app.raml_breaking.RamlBreakingChangeClassifier` (`raml`, id `raml-resources`) grades the resolved model with a
  custom ruleset instead of the baseline's folded "dangerous": method parameters (`raml.parameter-added-required` /
  `-made-required` / `-type-changed` breaking, `-added-optional` / `-made-optional` safe, `-removed` dangerous), type
  properties (`raml.property-added-required` / `-made-required` / `-type-changed` breaking, `-added-optional` safe,
  `-made-optional` dangerous), enum values (`raml.enum-value-removed` breaking, `-added` dangerous, `raml.enum-reordered`
  safe) and applied resource types / traits (`raml.reuse-changed` safe; their effects are graded where they land).
  Removed resources, methods, responses and types stay breaking and additions safe (baseline). OpenAPI 1.341.0.

### 1.476.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **TypeSpec versioning: per-version emit and diff (MFI-14.4, #3797)** — Apiome's compile configuration now writes
  `output-file: openapi.{version}.json` (`app.typespec_config.OPENAPI_OUTPUT_FILE`): a `@versioned` service
  (`@typespec/versioning`) emits one OpenAPI document per version — previously each version overwrote the last and
  only the newest survived — while an unversioned service still emits `openapi.json`.
  `app.typespec_compile.read_typespec_openapi_outputs` reads every emitted document; new `app.typespec_versioning`
  orders them by the versions enum's declaration order (`declared_versions` parses `@versioned(X)` and `enum X`,
  member values or names, comments and decorators skipped; unmatched versions follow in natural order) and grades
  each step from one version to the next with the OpenAPI compatibility analysis
  (`schema_compatibility.analyze_schema_compatibility`, `version_changes`). `TypeSpecCompiled.versions` holds every
  version oldest-first and `openapi` is the newest. The catalog item records `typespec_versions` (version + OpenAPI
  hash), `typespec_latest_version` and `typespec_version_changes` (`from`, `to`, `overall`, `counts`, up to 50
  findings, `finding_count`), and keeps each version's document as `raw["openapi_versions"]` — only for versioned
  services, so unversioned items are unchanged. New recorded fixture `typespec_compile/versioned` (real compiler
  0.65.0, three versions). OpenAPI 1.340.0.

### 1.475.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **WSDL → canonical model: ports, bindings, faults, multi-part messages (MFI-13.2, #3789)** — completes the WSDL
  projection (soapAction / style and XSD occurs / facets landed with MFI-13.5). Parser: new `WsdlBinding` records
  (`WsdlDocument.bindings`: name, port type, protocol `soap11` / `soap12` / `http` from the 1.1 extension namespace or
  the 2.0 binding `type` + `wsoap:version`, transport from `soap:binding@transport` / `wsoap:protocol`); new
  `WsdlFault` on `WsdlOperation.faults` (1.1 `wsdl:fault@message`; 2.0 `outfault ref` resolved to the interface
  `fault` element). Normalizer: each port with an address is a `Server` named after the port, `protocol` = its
  binding's, extras `wsdl_service` / `wsdl_binding` / `wsdl_port_type` / `wsdl_transport` (description unchanged);
  faults are `error`-role messages keyed `<operation>#fault.<name>`; a multi-part 1.1 message becomes a synthesized
  record type (`extras` `wsdl_kind: message`, `wsdl_message`; `<Message>Message` on a name clash) with one field per
  part (`wsdl_part_element` / `wsdl_part_type`) as the operation's payload, instead of only its first part. The WSDL
  emitter writes all of it back: bindings per recorded protocol (`soap` / `soap12` / `http`, transport only when
  recorded), services and ports regrouped from the servers, portType / binding faults with their messages, multi-part
  messages from their synthesized types (not emitted as schema types), and scalar payloads as `type` parts; models
  without WSDL topology keep the single-binding export. Corpus goldens for the WSDL / WSDL 2.0 / SoapUI fixtures gain
  the servers' topology, fault messages and kitchen-sink's message types. OpenAPI 1.339.0.

### 1.474.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **WSDL / XSD breaking changes (MFI-13.5, #3792)** — the WSDL importer now records what a SOAP compatibility check
  needs (the part of MFI-13.2 #3789 this ticket depends on): `WsdlOperation.soap_action` / `soap_style` from the
  document's SOAP bindings (WSDL 1.1 `soap:` / `soap12:` operation `soapAction` and the effective `style`; WSDL 2.0
  `wsoap:action`; the first binding that states a value wins), and per element particle `min_occurs`, `max_occurs`,
  `nillable`, `default` and its simple-type restriction (`simple_type`, `base`, `facets`: enumeration, pattern, length,
  min/maxLength, min/max Inclusive/Exclusive, totalDigits, fractionDigits) for named and inline simple types (an
  element restricting a built-in type inline, previously dropped, is now a field). The normalizer records them as field
  extras `xsd_min_occurs` / `xsd_max_occurs` / `xsd_nillable` / `xsd_default` / `xsd_simple_type` / `xsd_base` /
  `xsd_facets` and operation extras `wsdl_soap_action` / `wsdl_soap_style` (`rpc` only), each only when the document
  states it; the WSDL emitter writes all of them back (named simple types once at schema level, inline restrictions
  inline; the recorded soapAction instead of a synthesized `{namespace}/{operation}`, empty when none). New
  `app.wsdl_breaking.WsdlBreakingChangeClassifier` (`wsdl`, id `wsdl-xsd`): MEP, soapAction and style changes,
  required elements added, type changes, `minOccurs` raised, `maxOccurs` lowered, made non-nillable and narrowed
  facets are breaking; optional elements added (strict receivers: XSD is not additive-safe), `minOccurs` lowered,
  `maxOccurs` raised, made nillable, default changes and widened facets are dangerous; a spelling-only move is safe.
  Corpus goldens for the WSDL / WSDL 2.0 / SoapUI WSDL fixtures gain the new extras. OpenAPI 1.338.0.

### 1.473.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Added
- **OData breaking-change classifier: §5.2 Model Versioning + `$schemaversion` (MFI-11.5, #3780)** — new
  `app.odata_breaking.ODataBreakingChangeClassifier` (`odata`, id `odata-model-versioning`), a subclass of the
  baseline that grades by OData 4.01 Part 1 §5.2: properties added nullable (`odata.property-added-nullable`) or with
  a `$DefaultValue` (`odata.property-added-with-default`) are safe, a non-nullable property with no default is
  breaking (`odata.property-added-required`); a type change (`odata.property-type-changed`) or becoming non-nullable
  (`odata.property-made-non-nullable`) is breaking, becoming nullable dangerous; an entity type's key change
  (`odata.key-changed`), a removed or retyped navigation property (`odata.navigation-removed` /
  `-type-changed`) and a new single-valued non-nullable navigation (`odata.navigation-added-required`) are breaking;
  a new collection-valued or nullable navigation (`odata.navigation-added`) and added annotations
  (`odata.annotation-added`) are safe; an unknown-nullability navigation, a partner change and a changed / removed
  annotation are dangerous. v2/v3 navigation nullability comes from the association multiplicity; v4 `$Nullable`,
  `$DefaultValue` and `Core.SchemaVersion` are read from the model's canonical CSDL JSON. Every breaking grade's
  rationale notes whether `Core.SchemaVersion` moved between the versions (`schema_versions`). Other changes keep the
  baseline grading. OpenAPI 1.337.0.

  inherit one, a derived type must not redeclare it, and each key property must exist and be a single non-nullable

  extras gain `odata_xsd_violations` / `_count` and `odata_resolution_issues` / `_count` (each issue a `kind`, `path`,
