  namespace keep their absolute id and are keyed under their own namespace; simple shapes resolve to their base
  type; a service's operations include its resources'. Errors: the CLI's validation errors →
  `INPUT_SEMANTIC_INVALID` (staging path scrubbed); an undefined target in a JSON AST →
  `INPUT_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED`; no CLI for a multi-file set → `ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` (previously only the root
  was parsed). A single `.smithy` file still uses the built-in reader. The `smithy` tool no longer has its stdout
  JSON-parsed by the runner (`parses_json=False`). `app.fileset.normalize_member_path` is shared with the RAML AMF
  seam. OpenAPI 1.322.0.

### 1.457.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Changed
- **Apache Thrift: multi-file sets, field-id breaking rules and lint pack (MFI-19.3, #3981)** — the `thrift`
  import source's `parse_fileset` now parses the root and every file it `include`s (new `app.thrift_fileset`):
  includes resolve beside the including file, then from the root's folder; an include that is absolute, a URL or
  climbs out of the set is refused (`INPUT_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED`), as is a missing one; an include cycle is
  `INPUT_SEMANTIC_INVALID`. The normalizer keys each file's types under its own namespace (or its include prefix),
  resolves qualified names (`shared.Money`, typedefs in included files), keeps every file's services, records
  `extends` in the service's `extras.thrift_extends` and the set's files in `extras.thrift_source_files`. New
  breaking-change classifier `thrift` (`app.thrift_breaking`) pairs fields by wire id: `thrift.field-renamed`
  (dangerous), `thrift.field-id-reused` / `thrift.field-id-changed` (breaking), required fields added or removed
  (breaking), optional fields removed (dangerous) or added (safe), `thrift.made-required` / `thrift.made-optional`.
  New native lint pack `thrift` (`app.thrift_lint`): `thrift.namespace-declared`, `thrift.field-no-required`,
  `thrift.unique-field-ids`, `thrift.enum-explicit-values`, `thrift.oneway-void`; implicit enum values carry
  `extras.thrift_implicit_value`. Parser fixes: methods with several parameters (previously dropped) and the last
  field / parameter / typedef without a trailing separator (previously lost) are read, `service … extends …` is
  read (previously dropped), and `//` / `#` inside quoted strings are no longer taken as comments. The reference
  resolver shared with RAML moves to `app.fileset.resolve_relative_reference`. New corpus set
  `thrift/07-orders-set`; Thrift corpus goldens regenerated. Migration `V321` re-seeds the built-in
  "Apiome Recommended" style guide with the five `thrift.*` rules (otherwise their findings would be dropped by
  `CompiledStyleGuide.apply`). OpenAPI 1.321.0.

### 1.456.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Changed
- **RAML → canonical model: resource types and traits (MFI-15.2, #3800)** — RAML resources and methods now import
  *resolved*: a resource's `type:` (resource type) and the `is:` traits on a resource, a method or a resource-type
  method are applied with their `<<parameters>>` substituted (`resourcePath`, `resourcePathName`, `methodName`,
  caller parameters, and the `!singularize` / `!pluralize` / case functions), so each operation carries the headers,
  query parameters, bodies and responses they add. Without AMF the YAML reader applies the document's own resource
  types and traits through the new `app.raml_traits` resolver (optional `get?` methods, resource types extending
  resource types, method values winning over inherited ones); with AMF the resolved model is used as is and only the
  provenance comes from the resolver. New in the canonical model: request headers as `header` parameters; a
  response without a typed body (e.g. `204`) as a payload-less response message; every response message's
  `status_code` (so an OpenAPI export keeps each status instead of collapsing them onto `200`); operation `extras`
  `raml_resource_type` and `raml_traits`; API `extras` `raml_traits` and `raml_resource_types` (library ones as
  `alias.name`). A document whose YAML anchors would expand past 200,000 nodes while resolving is refused
  (`raml_traits.MAX_EXPANDED_NODES`). RAML corpus goldens regenerated. OpenAPI 1.320.0.

### 1.455.0 — 2026-10-26

#### Changed
- **RAML parse / resolve through AMF (MFI-15.1, #3799)** — the `raml` import source now parses through the bundled
  AMF CLI (`amf`, aml-org's AML Modeling Framework) when the runtime has it, so `!include` fragments, `uses`
  libraries and external examples resolve into the imported model: an included type and every library type import
  as types (library types as `<alias>.<Type>`, e.g. `common.Error`), and arrays keep their item type. A file set
  (`fileset`, `.zip`, `.tar.gz`) is staged in a private temporary directory; a reference that is absolute, a URL,
  or climbs out of the set with `..` is refused before AMF runs (`INPUT_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED`). A missing include
  or unknown type name is `INPUT_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED`; AMF's validation violations are `INPUT_SEMANTIC_INVALID`
  with each message and line. The normalized model's `extras` carry `raml_amf_model_sha256` (a hash of the
  AMF-resolved model, independent of the staging path) and `raml_source_files`. Without AMF, a self-contained
  document still imports through the YAML reader, and a document that includes or uses other files is refused
  with `ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` instead of importing only its root. The `amf` tool no longer has its stdout
  JSON-parsed by the runner (`parses_json=False`), so AMF's own error text reaches the message. OpenAPI 1.319.0.

### 1.454.0 — 2026-10-25

#### Changed
- **Collection source cards + CLI + fixtures (MFI-32.6, #4408)** — the `har` import source's card icon is now
  `activity` (was `radio`); `insomnia` and `bruno` keep the neutral `send` icon (their marks are trademarked).
  All three advertise `file`/`url`/`paste`/`fileset` input kinds and archive suffixes, so the UI source card and
  `apiome import har|insomnia|bruno` come straight from `GET /v1/import/sources` with no new UI or CLI command code.
  OpenAPI 1.318.0.

#### Fixed
- `POST /v1/import/detect` no longer reports a Bruno `.bru` request as ambiguous with `http-file`: the `.http`
  request-line pattern (`http_file_parser._REQUEST_LINE_RE`) no longer accepts a lone `{` as a URL, so `get {` (a
  Bruno method block) is not a request line. `GET {{baseUrl}}/…` still is.
- New `tests/test_collection_import_surfacing.py`: the three descriptors, and every committed HAR / Insomnia / Bruno
  example (zipped Bruno collection included) detected as its own adapter with no ambiguity.

### 1.453.0 — 2026-10-25

#### Changed
- **Secret scrubbing & environment mapping gate (MFI-32.5, #4407)** — scrubbing is **on and unskippable** for the
  MFI-EPIC-32 formats (`postman`, `insomnia`, `bruno`, `har`, `http-file`): a new first resolution tier,
  `format_locked` (`intake_scrub_policy.LOCKED_FORMATS`), always resolves them to `enforce` with entropy detection on,
  whatever the tenant mode, entropy setting or per-format override says. The gateway formats (`kong`, `traefik`,
  `tyk`) keep the overridable `format_default` tier.
  - `PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_slug}/governance/secret-scrub-policy` refuses a `formatOverrides` entry naming a locked
    format with `422`; the policy response gains `lockedFormats`. OpenAPI 1.317.0.
  - **Environment mapping:** variable *names* are kept and secret *values* withheld —
    `client_collection.variable_record` (`{"key", "secret"}` plus `"value"` only when not secret) for
    `postman_variables` and `http_file_variables`; `client_collection.safe_named_value` scrubs Postman header, query
    and path samples (an `Authorization` keeps its scheme word). A Postman `baseUrl` with no safe value becomes a
    `{baseUrl}` server variable; the Postman emitter writes a secret variable as an empty placeholder.
  - **Security-scheme stubs:** new `security_scheme_stubs` module writes `extras["security_schemes"]` (type and
    placement only, no material) for every collection/capture importer; the OpenAPI emitter writes them as
    `components.securitySchemes` and an operation's own declared auth (`extras["security"]`, now set by Postman
    request auth) as its `security` requirement. Postman `apikey` auth records its header / query name (never its
    value). Swagger 2.0 downgrade drops the stubs with a `security-scheme-stubs-dropped` loss.
  - **Scrub report on the catalog item:** the import's scrub report is stored as `formatMetadata.secretScrub` for the
    Provenance pane; an archive finding now names its fileset `member`.
  - `.http` request files are scrubbed at parse time (URLs, query pairs, headers, bodies after variable
    substitution), and the Postman / `.http` normalizers scrub `api.raw`.
  - New `tests/test_collection_secret_scrub_gate.py`: one seeded fixture per locked format persists zero secret bytes
    in the stored source, the canonical model and the converted OpenAPI document; corpus goldens regenerated.

### 1.452.0 — 2026-10-25

#### Added
- **Bruno collection import (MFI-32.4, #4406)** — a `bruno` import source (file, URL, paste, fileset; label
  `Bruno collection`) reads a Bruno collection folder — `bruno.json`, request `.bru` files, `collection.bru` /
  `folder.bru` settings and `environments/*.bru` — from an archive (MFI-29.1) or a git selection (MFI-29.3), plus a
  single `.bru` request on its own, through the shared MFI-32.1 inferred-spec engine. New modules `bru_lang` (the
  `.bru` block lexer: dictionary / text / list blocks, `~` disabled entries, quoted keys, `'''` multi-line values,
  unknown blocks kept as text), `bruno_parser`, `bruno_normalizer`, `bruno_import_source` (with `parse_bytes` for a
  zipped folder).
  - **Archive and git intake fingerprint identically:** every recorded path is relative to the directory holding
    `bruno.json`, so an archive's wrapping folder and a git selection prefix never reach the model.
  - Folder tree → tags (`folder.bru` `meta.name`); auth and headers inherit request → folder → collection; the
    method block's `body:` mode picks the body (JSON, form, multipart, GraphQL; XML / text keep their media type).
  - Variables → server variables and query / header parameter defaults, in Bruno's precedence (request > folder >
    environment > collection); `vars:secret` and secret-named variables never become defaults; `{{process.env.*}}`
    stays unresolved (`.env` files are never read).
  - Scripts, `vars:post-response`, tests and assertions are ignored with a note (declared limits `bruno.script`,
    `bruno.test`), as are `{{process.env.*}}`, non-HTTP requests, withheld credentials and secret variables.
  - Corpus `apiome-ui/examples/bruno/` (6 single-file and zipped valid entries plus a flat fileset across all six
    rungs, 6 negative), goldens, round-trip matrix row, MCP toolset goldens, version coverage, inference-provenance
    entry, generated `secrets-bruno.bru` fixture.
  - `client_collection.check_client_text` (public) and `client_collection.apply_parameter_defaults` (shared with the
    Insomnia normalizer, output unchanged).

### 1.451.0 — 2026-10-25

#### Added
- **Insomnia collection import (MFI-32.3, #4405)** — an `insomnia` import source (file, URL, paste, fileset; label
  `Insomnia collection`) reads Insomnia **v4** JSON exports (`_type: export`, `__export_format: 4`; the flat
  `resources[]` tree rebuilt from `parentId`) and **v5** YAML exports (`collection.insomnia.rest/5.0`, a design
  document's `spec.insomnia.rest/5.0`, global `environment.insomnia.rest/5.0` files beside them) through the shared
  MFI-32.1 inferred-spec engine. New modules `insomnia_parser`, `insomnia_normalizer`, `insomnia_import_source`.
  - Folders → operation tags; requests → single-sample operations, bodies as declared (JSON, GraphQL, form,
    multipart; XML / text / file keep their media type); folder auth and headers inherited.
  - Environment variables → server variables (`{{ _.baseUrl }}` → `{baseUrl}`, base environment wins, then the
    first sub-environment; folder environments override) and query / header parameter defaults for whole-variable
    values. Secret variables (by name, or Insomnia's `secret` type) never become defaults.
  - Auth read as scheme + public facts only (OAuth 2 grant type, URLs, scopes; API key name and location).
    Cookie jars are never read.
  - Declared limits: scripts, template tags, gRPC / WebSocket requests, unit tests, API spec, mock routes, cookie
    jars, withheld credentials, secret variables. `FORMAT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` for other export formats.
  - Structural stability: the v4 and v5 exports of one collection import identically (round trip with an Insomnia
    export waits for MFX-31.3, #4291).
  - Corpus `apiome-ui/examples/insomnia/` (8 valid across all six rungs, 8 negative), goldens, round-trip matrix row,
    MCP toolset goldens, version coverage, inference-provenance entry, generated `secrets-insomnia.yaml` fixture.
  - `client_collection.load_client_yaml` shares the JSON loader's encoding and intake-guard checks.

#### Fixed
- **Secret scrub gate: YAML client exports and secret-typed variables** — the gate now redacts YAML
  `name`/`key` + `value` pairs that name a secret, YAML `token:` / `bearer:` values (quoted or not), every value in a
  YAML `cookies:` block, and any key-value variable whose `type` is `secret` (JSON, either member order, and YAML),
  whatever it is called.

### 1.450.0 — 2026-10-25

#### Added
- **HAR capture import (MFI-32.2, #4404)** — a `har` import source (file, URL, paste, fileset; label
  `HAR (inferred)`) reads HAR 1.2 / 1.1 captures from browser devtools and debugging proxies through the shared
  MFI-32.1 inferred-spec engine: calls cluster into parameterized operations and bodies into schemas widened across
  samples. New modules `har_filters`, `har_parser`, `har_normalizer`, `har_import_source`.
  - Noise filter: page assets (resource type, extension, response media type), analytics / monitoring hosts, CORS
    preflights and non-HTTP entries are left out and counted; browser-set request headers never become parameters.
  - One host per import: the host with the most API calls, or the hosts named in `har_hosts`; the other hosts are
    listed in `extras.har.hosts` and the coverage ledger.
  - New `SpecImportOptions` fields `har_hosts`, `har_include`, `har_exclude` (`host/path` globs) and
    `har_keep_noise`; a wrong-typed value is refused with `INPUT_SEMANTIC_INVALID`.
  - Credentials: `cookies` lists are never read, `Authorization` keeps only its scheme word, every other value
    passes the scrub gate. Declared limits `har.static_asset`, `har.analytics`, `har.cors_preflight`,
    `har.non_http`, `har.excluded_by_pattern`, `har.unselected_host`, `har.auth_credential`, `har.cookie`.
  - `inferred_spec.auth_scheme_from_headers` is now public.
  - Corpus `apiome-ui/examples/har/` (7 valid across all six rungs, 6 negative), goldens, round-trip matrix row,
    MCP toolset goldens, version coverage, inference-provenance entry, and a generated `secrets-har.har`
    adversarial fixture.

#### Fixed
- **Secret scrub gate: HAR cookie jars and JSON-escaped bodies** — every `value` in a `"cookies": [...]` list is
  now redacted (`cookie-jar-value`; cookie names like `sid` never said they were secret), and the secret-named
  assignment rule matches JSON-escaped quotes (`\"password\": \"…\"`), so request and response bodies that HAR
  and Postman store as strings no longer persist their credentials. The redaction keeps the string valid JSON.
- **Secret scrub gate is linear in the number of findings** — each finding's line number was counted from the top
  of the document, so a large capture with thousands of cookie values took minutes; a 12 MB HAR with 120,000
  findings now scrubs in a few seconds.
- **Coverage ledger detail for client-collection limits** — rows built from `declared_limit` records (Hoppscotch,
  Thunder Client, HAR) printed `None` as their detail; they now print the limit's note.
